screening_results.reason: This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control using a cued Stroop paradigm in healthy adults (ages 20–38). It reports within-subject modeling of congruent and incongruent trials (and sensory-conflict–weighted regressors), group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps within the prefrontal mask with peak coordinates and thresholds, and psychophysiological interaction analyses. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task details are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain maps; not connectivity-only; healthy within-age-range sample). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the sample falls outside the allowable age range (Exclusion E8): participants are older adults (study recruited ages 55–85; mean age 67.1), whereas the review restricts to ages 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function — working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts of task conditions/load), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported as tables/figures), I9 (task is working memory — an executive function), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Full text content is not available (full text = 'nan'), so core methods and results cannot be confirmed. Unable to verify whether the study assesses executive function tasks (I5), includes a within-participant task vs active control contrast (I6), reports a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map (I7/I8), uses an established executive function domain task (I9), or reports participant age/health and imaging modality (I10). Therefore no inclusion criteria can be confirmed. No exclusion criteria can be confidently applied based on the provided metadata alone. Recommend obtaining the complete article for reassessment.

This is an empirical PET study of the Stroop task (an inhibitory executive function), with healthy adult participants (mean age 27.4). It includes within-subject contrasts of incongruent vs congruent conditions (active control), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results using SPM and canonical Z-score eigenimages (with coordinates/tables/figures), and provides participant, modality, and task details. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment against inclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes older adults aged 60–85 (i.e., participants outside the 18–60 age range). The study otherwise meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive control/task-switching), I6 (within-participant contrasts such as switch > repeat and cue+target > cue-only), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and reported omnibus maps/tables), I8 (results reported with coordinates and tables), I9 (task-switching falls under cognitive flexibility/executive function), and I10 (participant ages, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite satisfying the other inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London) in healthy adult participants (ages 19–39). The paper reports within-participant contrasts manipulating planning parameters (search depth and goal hierarchy) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected results reported; coordinate tables and figures provided). Participant characteristics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-group healthy participant contrasts, and participants are within the 18–60 range. Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (Stroop inhibition/selective attention) in healthy adults (ages 22–40). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent minus congruent) serving as active control comparisons, conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with thresholding and presents results in figures and tables of Talairach coordinates (including conjunction analyses). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state baseline only, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive verbal working memory (Sternberg paradigm) in healthy adults (ages 19–28). It reports within-subject contrasts comparing an executive manipulation condition versus an active match control, uses group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2), and reports peak coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, imaging modality, and task details are provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (dot-motion task) in healthy adults with whole-brain analyses, but it does not assess an executive function task within the review's defined domains. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses present), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/tabled/figured), and I10 (participant age and healthy status and imaging modality reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not target an executive function or cognitive-control task as specified), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are directly triggered by the manuscript. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it includes clinical participants (adults with autism spectrum disorder) and is not restricted to healthy individuals (Exclusion E8). It does, however, meet the inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: antisaccade/inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrast: antisaccade vs. prosaccade), I7 (group-level whole-brain/surface-based analyses and maps), I8 (whole-brain results reported via maps/clusters/coordinates), I9 (task falls in inhibition domain), and I10 (participant age range, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No inclusion criteria are unmet. Because the study includes a clinical group (ASD), it fails the requirement that studies be restricted to healthy adults, so it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI, task-based, within-subject study of four-term analogical reasoning that explicitly manipulates and contrasts an analogy condition against semantic and perceptual active control conditions. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM), cluster and coordinate results, and targeted small-volume corrections, with coordinates and verbal descriptions provided. Participants were healthy adults (N=20; ages 19–37), imaging modality and task paradigm are fully described. The task engages executive processes (working memory/relational integration and mapping), which fall within established executive function domains relevant to the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets I5–I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (cognitive set shifting) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and adequate reporting of participants, modality, and paradigm, the paper uses fixation/rest as the baseline for within-participant contrasts and does not employ an active control condition. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E8 met: the study includes participants outside the target adult age range (8–17-year-olds included alongside adults), violating the review's 18–60 healthy adult restriction. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant task contrasts reported, e.g., High-Risk > Low-Risk), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality and task described). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (task is a gambling/risk-taking decision-making paradigm, not a canonical executive function domain such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation), and I5 is ambiguous/not clearly met as the primary focus is reward/risk decision-making rather than an explicit executive function task. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore exclude due to E8.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (SST variant) in healthy adults that reports within-subject contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected). However, the full text does not report participant ages nor an explicit statement confirming the sample as healthy (methods list 'Fourteen right handed participants' but no ages or explicit health status). Inclusion criterion I10 requires reporting of participant age and confirmation of healthy sample status; this information is missing, so not all inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered: whole-brain results are reported and this is not a connectivity-only, between-group, rest-baseline-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range-age study based on available text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because I10 is not satisfied.

Exclusion decision due to unmet inclusion criterion I10. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study assessing executive functions), I6 (within-participant contrast: target detection vs passive listening active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in figures/tables), and I9 (task maps to executive domains: working memory/target detection). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 — the manuscript reports number and sex of healthy volunteers and confirms healthy status, modality, and task, but does not provide participant ages or age range required by I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study includes healthy participants but the sample includes older adults aged 65–75, i.e., outside the 18–60 age range required by the review (exclusion E8). The article otherwise meets inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI/PET task-based study of working memory (I5, I9), reports within-participant task contrasts (load-dependent WM/high > WM/low) and includes an active control task (I6), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates (I7, I8), and reports participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task details (I10). Because participants fall outside the allowed age range, the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (participants outside 18–60). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluding because the study includes non-healthy participants (current recreational drug users) and therefore violates exclusion criterion E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). The paper does meet several inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and coordinates (I7, I8), uses an inhibition executive-function task (GO/NOGO) (I9), and provides participant, imaging modality, and task details (I10). However, it does not clearly present a within-participant contrast against an explicit active control condition (I6 not met). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it includes participants older than the allowable age range (subjects aged 65–89), which violates exclusion criterion E8. It otherwise meets the inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control/attention), I6 (within-participant contrasts, e.g., Shift vs Focus), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and described in text), I9 (task assesses cognitive flexibility/attention shifting, an executive domain), and I10 (participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No inclusion criteria are unmet. fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is a PET task-based investigation in healthy adults and includes a within-subject contrast of an executive function task (MCST) vs an active control (I5, I6). The task assesses planning/set-shifting (executive domain) and participant info (healthy, age 20–33) and modality are reported (I9, I10). However, the imaging results were analyzed/reported only within the striatum (small-volume/ROI approach); authors state that "Only those peaks falling within the striatum were considered" and used a search volume equal to the striatum. No group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is reported, so the study does not meet I7. This violates exclusion E3 (ROI/small-volume-only reporting with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, ages 19–35) explicitly investigating inhibitory/executive processes during preparation. It includes within-subject contrasts of an executive-control task versus an active control (Preparation > Watch), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with FDR correction and coordinate/figure reporting. Task paradigm maps onto inhibition/executive control and working/preparatory control domains. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) that reports within-subject contrasts (VT>FT) and within-group (Control) whole-brain, group-level random-effects SPM results (FDR-corrected) with coordinates and figures. The paper reports participant ages and confirms non-traumatised healthy control participants, describes the task paradigm in detail, and uses whole-brain voxelwise analyses. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. None of the exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-group healthy contrasts, resting-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/absent healthy adults) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of task-switching (executive function/cognitive flexibility) in healthy adults (mean age 25). It reports within-subject whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., informatively cued > non-informatively cued; informatively cued switch > repeat; no-go > go) using SPM2 with cluster correction and provides coordinate tables and figures. Participant/sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening.

This is a task-based, event-related fMRI study of set-shifting (cognitive flexibility) in healthy young adults using the Wisconsin Word Sorting Task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts against an active control condition (control matching), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and reports peak coordinates/tables and figures, and provides participant demographics and imaging/task details. The task clearly falls within executive function (cognitive flexibility/set-shifting). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes active control baseline, empirical, healthy adults within 18–60). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables, references) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (inhibition, attentional shifting, response initiation). It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., stop–go, shift–go, stop–shift, double–stop) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected statistics and peak coordinates. Participant information (healthy adults aged 18–40), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are provided. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study includes both schizophrenia patients and healthy controls (sample not restricted to healthy individuals), therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8. Additionally, the reported task contrasts (sensorimotor tapping and Sternberg probe effect) appear to be against baseline/rest rather than an active control condition, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 and likely violates E6. The paper also does not present a conventional group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for healthy participants (I7 not clearly met). Met inclusion criteria: I5 (fMRI study of executive function — Sternberg working memory), I9 (tasks within executive function domain), I10 (participant age, healthy sample info, modality and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E8, E6.

Sample includes participants outside the review age range (range 45–62, includes ages >60), violating exclusion criterion E8. The study otherwise satisfies inclusion criteria: I5 (PET study of executive function—working memory), I6 (within-subject contrasts vs active control tasks: SPA-AM, NSPA-AM, AM-MOT), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with reported voxelwise thresholds), I8 (coordinates and maps reported), I9 (working memory is an executive function), I10 (reports participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No other exclusion criteria met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task-based study in healthy adults that includes an executive component (target detection/vigilance) within an emotional oddball paradigm. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of the executive task (target > negative & neutral) and other task contrasts, conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded, cluster-corrected), with results presented in tables/figures. Participants’ ages and healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function) in healthy adult participants (mean age 23.3). Analyses include within-subject contrasts (e.g., Clever vs Stupid primes; error vs correct trials) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical mapping (conjunction analyses corrected for multiple comparisons and exploratory whole-brain searches; coordinates and SPM results reported). Task paradigm, imaging modality, participant demographics, and methods are fully described. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with whole-brain group results and reports coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within healthy 18–60 sample; active control conditions used). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, within-subject, group-level fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers (mean age 27.1) using a combined Eriksen flanker Go/NoGo paradigm assessing response inhibition and error monitoring (executive functions). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM) with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and tables/figures of activations. Within-participant contrasts (incorrect vs correct NoGo trials) are reported and treatment effects analyzed; results are presented as whole-brain maps/coordinates and figures. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/rest-only; not between-group only; empirical human neuroimaging data; participants 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion (E3): The study used PET to measure serotonin transporter (SERT) binding at rest and correlated these molecular PET measures with separately administered cognitive tests. It did not perform task-based PET/fMRI activation paradigms during executive function tasks, did not report within-participant task vs active-control contrasts, and did not present group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps — analyses are ROI-based correlations rather than task-evoked activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I9 (executive-function tasks such as Stroop and TMT B were used) and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigms are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based PET/fMRI assessing executive function during imaging), I6 (no within-participant contrast of task vs active control during imaging), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive control in healthy adults (ages 18–28). The study reports within-participant contrasts between task conditions (e.g., incongruent vs neutral, shifting vs non-shifting) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected) with tables/figures of coordinates. The task manipulations fall squarely within executive function domains (inhibition, shifting/cognitive flexibility), and participant/sample characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion: E8 applies — the study includes a clinical ADHD group and is not restricted to healthy individuals, which violates the review’s requirement for healthy-only samples. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function—inhibition Go/No-Go), I6 (within-participant contrasts such as No-Go vs Go and slow vs fast), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: inhibition), I10 (participant ages, sample status for controls, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (all relevant I5–I10 were satisfied). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (full article text including methods, results, and discussion provided). Because the study includes non-healthy participants (ADHD patients), it must be excluded per E8 despite meeting the inclusion criteria and reporting usable within-group healthy-control contrasts.

This study does report within-participant contrasts (up- vs down-regulation) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and provides participant/sample information and imaging/task details. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I10. However, the primary paradigm is rt-fMRI neurofeedback training using a meta-cognitive awareness/self-regulation strategy rather than a canonical executive-function task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control task-based paradigms) and I9 (task falls within established executive function domains) are not clearly satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I5 and I9 are not met; although related to cognitive control, the task does not fit the review's required executive-function task domains.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive control (go/nogo/voluntary selection) in adults that reports within-subject contrasts (selection+/- and selection vs go/nogo and control conditions). Group-level, whole-brain analyses are reported for healthy controls (tables/figures/coordinates are presented), and ROI analyses are supplementary; the paper provides participant ages and confirmation of healthy control status, imaging modality (1.5 T fMRI), and full task details. The task falls into established executive domains (inhibition/response selection/initiative). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain maps are reported (not ROI-only), results include within-group healthy participant contrasts (not only between-group), and an active control task was used. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 22) using a working memory with distraction paradigm (executive function/inhibition). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (face-distractor vs scrambled-face control), with coordinates and ROI follow-ups. Participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–55) using the Attention Network Test. It includes an explicitly reported within-subject executive-control contrast (incongruent > congruent), and reports group-level second-level voxelwise results with coordinates (within-sample task effects and genotype group comparisons). Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all described. Although ROI masks were defined for hypothesis testing, the manuscript reports voxelwise activation coordinates from the within-group (whole-sample) task analysis, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, resting baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are met. Full text appears complete with background, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive function (color-word Stroop) using a within-subject contrast (incongruent vs congruent) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (FLAME analyses with cluster correction) with coordinates (Table 1) used to place ERP sources. The paper clearly describes participant ages (18–34), screening for health/psychopathology and reports that the fMRI analyses were conducted on a subset of 30 psychopathology-free participants, specifies imaging modality (3T fMRI) and the task paradigm. The Stroop task falls within inhibition/cognitive control executive domains. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes active task contrasts, is empirical, and analyses are on healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study includes a healthy older adult group with ages 65–75, i.e., participants outside the required 18–60 age range (Exclusion E8). The study otherwise meets all relevant inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function — spatial working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts and active control conditions), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables), I9 (working memory falls within executive function), and I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No other exclusion criteria apply. Because inclusion criteria are otherwise satisfied but the sample includes participants outside the review age range, the study must be excluded under E8.

This study used PET [11C]raclopride to measure striatal dopamine binding and administered executive-function tasks (delayed-response working memory, Tower of London planning) behaviorally. However, no task-evoked, within-participant neuroimaging contrasts or group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps are reported. Imaging results are limited to striatal binding (ROI) and correlations with behavioral change rather than task-based activation mapping. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirements for within-subject task contrasts or whole-brain task activation reporting.

Exclusion criterion met: E8 (study includes clinical participants and is not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task assessing strategic/initiational aspects of cognition), I6 (within-participant contrasts: S−D, D−U, graded D>S>U), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I8 (results reported as figures and coordinate tables), I9 (task involves ‘initiation’/strategic processes within executive-function domains), I10 (participant ages, healthy comparison group status, imaging modality (15O-PET), and task paradigm fully reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Although the study provides within-group whole-brain activation maps for healthy participants, it nevertheless includes a clinical (major depressive disorder) sample and is not restricted to healthy adults, which triggers exclusion E8 per the review criteria.

This is an fMRI Stroop study of executive function that meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI on executive function), I6 (within-participant incongruent vs congruent contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (coordinates and cluster reporting), I9 (Stroop task = inhibition executive function), and I10 (reports participant age, imaging modality, and task paradigm). However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample was not restricted to healthy individuals (participants were recruited into ‘pure’ psychopathology and comorbid groups based on scoring above the 80th percentile on symptom measures and were included in analyses), so the study includes non-healthy participants. Therefore I exclude this study. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 satisfied).

This is an fMRI study of overt verbal fluency in healthy adults that manipulates executive demands (letter vs category retrieval; switching vs single-cue) and includes within-subject contrasts versus an active control (automatic speech). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (AFNI, cluster-corrected maps; tables/figures described). Participants are healthy adults (mean age 32, range 22–48). The tasks map onto executive function domains (cognitive flexibility/switching, initiation, controlled retrieval). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus the study meets I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This study is a task-based PET investigation of executive function (Montreal Card Sorting Task) in healthy adults and includes within-subject contrasts (active MCST vs active control). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (statistical parametric maps with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant demographics (ages 20–33) and healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses an active control, empirical human neuroimaging, participants within 18–60 and healthy).

This study uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (go/no-go inhibition) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates, but it should be excluded for two reasons: (1) Exclusion E8: the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (study includes Parkinson’s disease patients and controls), so it does not meet the requirement for studies of healthy-only participants. (2) Exclusion E6: the primary within-subject contrast reported is activation versus rest (A>R) using a passive baseline rather than an active control condition, and the inclusion criterion I6 requires a within-participant contrast against an active control. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

Although this study uses task-based fMRI of an executive/inhibition task (Stroop) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results, it is a patient vs control study that reports primarily between-group contrasts (patients>controls) without presenting an accompanying within-group task activation map for the healthy control group. Thus it violates exclusion E5. In addition, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (includes patients with essential tremor), meeting exclusion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive task), I6 (within-participant cognitive>baseline contrast generated), I7 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (coordinates/figures reported), I9 (task within executive/inhibition domain), I10 (sample status, imaging modality, and paradigm described). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Because E5 (only between-group contrasts without within-group healthy activation maps) and E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals) are met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

This PET study (15O H2O) reports task-based, within-participant voxelwise contrasts of ambivalent (cognitive conflict) vs univalent conditions, with SPM whole-brain group analyses and tables/figures of coordinates. The task probes evaluative conflict resolution and search-related working memory (executive/cognitive control processes). Healthy control within-group contrasts are reported, participant demographics and imaging modality are provided, and contrasts use an active control (univalent conditions). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive/cognitive control processes (memory retrieval, anticipation, feedback). It reports within-subject contrasts across task conditions (e.g., match vs no-match, different memory loads) and includes an active control (X trials) and fixation comparisons. A second-level random-effects group analysis was conducted and whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (tables, coordinates, figures) despite limited coverage of some posterior regions. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, mean age 25), imaging modality and task paradigm are fully described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is incomplete (only a redirect/placeholder present), preventing verification of essential methodological details. From the title, the task appears to be task-switching (an executive function), so I9 is met. However I cannot confirm imaging modality (I5), presence of a within-participant contrast vs an active control (I6), whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported (I7/I8), or that participant age and healthy sample status are within 18–60 and fully reported (I10). Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study must be excluded pending access to the full article. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I9.
