This is a task-based fMRI study of sustained attention (Continuous Performance Test — a vigilance/executive function domain) in healthy adults (ages 18–55). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (correct targets vs correct non-targets baseline; omissions vs baseline) and group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with results described in tables and figures. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality (1.5 T BOLD fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations in healthy participants, uses an active control baseline, and participants are within the 18–60 range). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study used FDG-PET acquired during a rest/passive introspection condition (no task performed in scanner) and related resting metabolism to CPT performance measured separately. Therefore it does not provide a task-based within-participant contrast (no task vs active control), nor does it report group-level whole-brain task activation maps. Analyses were region-focused (predefined prefrontal ROIs) rather than whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, and the sample included bipolar patients (not restricted to healthy adults). Inclusion criteria met: I9 (CPT/vigilance is an executive attention task) and I10 (participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task-based fMRI/PET with task in scanner), I6 (within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no whole-brain results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only analyses/no whole-brain results), E6 (resting scan without an active control task), E8 (study includes patient group; not restricted to healthy individuals). Full text appears complete.

This PET study used an auditory continuous performance task (vigilance) in healthy adults and reports group-level, whole-brain SPM results and coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based study), I7 (group whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (coordinates/figures reported), I9 (task falls within executive domain: vigilance/attention), I10 (participant age and healthy sample and imaging modality reported). However, the PET analyses use a block-design Task versus Rest contrast (rest baseline only) and do not include a within-participant contrast of the executive task versus an active control condition. Therefore I6 is not satisfied, and exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control) is met. Although ERP data separate target vs non-target, the qualifying whole-brain PET maps are Task vs Rest only, so the study does not meet the required within-task active-control contrast.

Full text is not provided (only title/metadata/redirect notice). Cannot verify that the study meets inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 cannot be confirmed). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I5 (uncertain if task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function in healthy adults—study title indicates schizophrenia focus), I6 (no evidence of a within-participant contrast in healthy participants), I7 (no confirmation of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), I8 (no whole-brain results available in text/tables/figures here), I9 (task domain cannot be confirmed as an established executive function), I10 (participant age range and healthy sample status not reported in provided content). Exclusion criteria met: none (cannot determine E3–E8 from incomplete content). Fulltext_incomplete=true; request full article PDF or main text to re-screen.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 23) using a task (PPA) that manipulates relational integration and interference resolution—both executive/cognitive-control processes. Analyses include within-participant contrasts across task conditions (RC and IN factorial contrasts) and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (whole-brain maps/tables/figures), with ROI and small-volume corrections described. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (age 18–55) using a semantic verbal fluency task (executive function initiation/working memory aspects) with an active high-level baseline (reading aloud). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (semantic verbal fluency > reading aloud) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM results with peak coordinates and cluster extent). Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, healthy adult sample within age range).

This study meets I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function via a Flanker conflict/inhibition task), I6 (within-participant contrasts: incongruent>congruent and error>correct), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (coordinates and cluster statistics reported in text), and I9 (task falls under inhibition/conflict monitoring). However, I10 is not satisfied in the provided full text: participant age information (mean/range) is not reported in the Participants section supplied, so the requirement for reporting participant age is not clearly met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered by the available text. Full-text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I10 is not clearly satisfied in the provided full text, the study must be excluded.

This PET study of an auditory continuous performance task (CPT) meets several inclusion criteria: I5 (PET study of executive/attention task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM maps reported), I8 (coordinates/tables and figures reported), I9 (task = vigilance/attention within executive domains), and I10 (participant ages, healthy status, PET modality, and task paradigm reported). However, it fails I6: there is no within-participant contrast of the executive task against an active control condition—the PET analyses use Task versus Rest (passive baseline). This violates exclusion criterion E6 (studies using rest/fixation as the only baseline). Note: while ERP data include target vs non-target contrasts, the imaging (PET) whole-brain maps used for meta-analysis are Task vs Rest. Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI, task-based, within-subject study contrasting deceptive versus honest responses (deceptive > honest), which operationalizes interference-monitoring/resolution and inhibitory control—an executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster results and coordinate tables, and provides participant demographics (mean age 23), healthy sample status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and thus appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (redirect/landing page only). Cannot verify required eligibility details. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I5 (uncertain imaging modality and task details), I6 (no confirmation of a within-participant contrast vs an active control), I7 (no confirmation of group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (no reported whole-brain coordinates/figures in provided content), I9 (task classification as established executive function domain not verifiable), I10 (participant age range, healthy sample confirmation, and detailed imaging/task information not reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (insufficient information to apply). fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adults (n=15, ages 23–34) using a task of intrinsic alertness (vigilance), which falls within the executive domain (vigilance). The paper reports task-based, within-participant contrasts (alertness vs sensorimotor control) and describes group-level SPM analyses with coordinates/tables used to define network nodes. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigm are reported. Although the current manuscript emphasizes correlational structural equation modeling, whole-brain activation results (reported via subtraction analyses and coordinates) are clearly described and satisfy the requirement for voxelwise group-level results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; thus inclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it is not a task-based executive-function activation study and violates several exclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: E3, E4, E5, E6, E8. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET of executive function; PET data are resting FDG scans after drug/placebo), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive task vs active control), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported; analyses are ROI-based), I9 (imaging was not acquired during an executive task paradigm despite behavioral working memory testing), I10 (participants are not a healthy sample restricted to age 18–60; sample is male veterans aged 52–81 including PTSD patients). The full text appears complete and provides methods/results/discussion, but the imaging design and sample do not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This is an fMRI study of a verbal Trail Making Test (vTMT) probing cognitive flexibility (executive function) in healthy adults (ages 19–43). It reports a within-participant contrast of vTMTB (set-shifting) versus vTMTA (active control), with group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses, corrected p-values and cluster thresholds, and results described in text/tables/figures. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Exclusion justified because the study includes participants older than 60 years (E8) and uses a rest baseline (eyes-open rest) as the comparison condition rather than an active control task (E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of an executive function task — working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported via SPM and coordinate tables/figures), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and described in text), I9 (task is working memory, an established executive domain), and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion I6 is not met because the primary within-participant contrasts are task versus rest rather than task versus an active control condition. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given the violations of E6 and E8, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis despite satisfying other inclusion criteria.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study includes participants outside the target healthy adult range and is not restricted to healthy individuals (E8). Although the study uses PET and a within-participant contrast versus an active control and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, the task (visual navigation) is not within the specified executive function domains required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I10 (participant information, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess a canonical executive function/cognitive control task), I9 (task does not fall within listed executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore excluded based on E8.

Exclusion criteria met: E8 (participants are elderly, age range 75–85, i.e. outside the review’s 18–60 age range). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based PET study of executive function/working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast: task vs active perceptual baseline), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and described), I9 (task is working memory, an executive function domain), I10 (reports participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Summary: Although the study fulfills all neuroimaging and task-related inclusion criteria, it must be excluded because the sample age (75–85) violates the review’s age restriction (E8). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study conducted ROI-masked analyses focused on prefrontal ROIs without reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps) and E8 (participants are elderly and include MCI patients — sample not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of executive function/dual-tasking), I6 (within-participant contrasts comparing dual vs. single task active control conditions), I8 (results clearly described in text/figures/tables), I9 (task falls within executive function domain), I10 (participant ages/health status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60 and requiring whole-brain task activation maps.

Exclusion summary: This study is excluded because it reports only between-group comparisons of resting 18F-FDG PET metabolism in methamphetamine users vs controls and does not provide any task-evoked, within-participant activation contrasts in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only between-group contrasts without within-group task activation in healthy participants), E6 (imaging consists of rest/eyes-closed baseline without an active in-scanner task), E8 (sample is not restricted to healthy participants — includes clinical MA users). Inclusion criteria met: none of the required imaging-task criteria are satisfied. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function — PET was resting metabolism), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map — whole-brain maps are for resting group differences), I8 (coordinate-reporting criterion is irrelevant because there is no task-evoked map), I9 (no in-scanner executive task; WCST was performed outside the scanner), I10 (imaging task paradigm for executive task not reported as an in-scanner task). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a PET study of an executive function paradigm (spatial working memory) (I5); it reports within-participant contrasts of the executive task versus an active visuomotor control (SWT vs VMT) (I6); it provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical mapping using SPM (I7) with coordinate/table and figure reporting (I8); the task falls within the executive domain (working memory) (I9); and participant demographics, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task details are reported (I10). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and is complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore I include the study.

This article is a quantitative meta-analysis aggregating coordinates from published fMRI studies rather than reporting original task-evoked neuroimaging data from participants. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E7 (non-empirical paper / meta-analysis without original human neuroimaging data). The study does address executive-function tasks (task-switching and Stroop) and reports coordinates and sample/modality details (meeting I9 and I10, and I8 insofar as results are reported in tables), but it does not itself present original fMRI/PET within-participant task contrasts or group-level whole-brain statistical maps (inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I7 are not met). Full text appears complete. Given E7 is met, the study must be excluded.

This PET task-based study examines planning (Tower of London), reports within-participant contrasts versus an active 1-move control, provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates, tables, figures), and reports participant age, health status, imaging modality and paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. However, the study includes Parkinson’s disease patients and is not restricted to healthy participants (and participants include older adults around/above 60), thus violating exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals / outside 18–60). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite satisfying other inclusion criteria.

The study is a PET task-based investigation with within-participant baseline vs gambling contrasts, but it does not provide group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps and focuses analyses on the ventral striatum (ROI-targeted). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E8 (study includes pathological gamblers — not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrast of task vs active control) and I10 (participant age, healthy sample info for controls, imaging modality PET, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (unclear/does not target an established executive function domain listed), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation map), I8 (no whole-brain results in acceptable formats), and I9 (task—IGT—does not clearly fall within the specified executive function domains). Full text appears complete: fulltext_incomplete=false.

Exclusion E3 applies: the study reports only ROI-based PET binding analyses (striatal and midbrain ROIs) measuring D2 receptor occupancy and does not report any whole-brain, task-evoked neuroimaging activation maps. Although the study includes executive function tasks (working memory, learning) and reports behavioral effects, it does not present within-participant task vs active-control PET/fMRI contrasts or group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I9 (tasks are within executive function domains) and I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality [PET], and task paradigms are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not functionally image task-evoked executive function activations using task-based PET/fMRI), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control neuroimaging contrast), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

Although the study administered executive function tasks and reports participant demographics and PET modality, it does not provide task-evoked, within-participant whole-brain activation contrasts. PET data were resting FDG measures acquired prior to behavioral testing and correlations with behavior; no task-based PET/fMRI activation maps or within-subject task vs active-control contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I8 (clear whole-brain task results). Included criteria met: I9 (tasks are within executive domains) and I10 (participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported). Exclusion criteria triggered: E4 (resting-state/task-less imaging without task activation maps) and E8 (study sample not restricted to healthy individuals; includes remitted MDD subjects). Conclusion: Exclude.

This PET study uses food/satiety and taste paradigms rather than established executive function tasks (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 and I9. Although it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (I7), provides results in figures/tables (I8), and reports participant, health, age, and imaging details (I10), it lacks any within-participant contrast of an executive function task (I6/I5). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly met. Hence the study is excluded for failing to assess an executive-function task domain required by the meta-analysis.

This is a PET amyloid imaging study relating PiB retention to cognitive test performance and cognitive reserve in older adults and mild AD patients. It does not report task-based fMRI/PET executive-function activations, within-participant task vs active-control contrasts, or group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/coordinates. Participants include ages well above 60 and include patients with AD. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (participants outside 18–60 and not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based executive-function fMRI/PET study), I6 (no within-participant task vs active-control contrasts), I7 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/coordinates), I9 (no imaging task paradigms within executive domains), I10 (no task paradigm reported). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study violates exclusion criteria E6 and E8. E6: the PET task contrasts are primarily against rest/fixation (eyes closed) rather than an active control condition; no within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control (I6) is provided. E8: the participant samples include older adults (mean ages ~58–70 years, with a third sample mean 68±6), exceeding the 18–60 years age range. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task PET assessing working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (tasks fall within executive domain: verbal working memory), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no executive vs active control within-participant contrast).

This PET study examined dopamine receptor binding correlated with nonlinear probability weighting in a risky-choice task. It does not investigate an executive function or cognitive-control task (decision-making under risk is outside the listed executive domains), contains no within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control, and does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (analyses are regression of receptor binding against behavioral parameters). Participant information, health status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults. It is an event-related fMRI study of executive functions (inhibition, interference control, cognitive flexibility) with within-subject contrasts in healthy control participants (No-go vs Go; incongruent vs congruent; switch vs repeat). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (within-group and between-group maps; clusterwise inference and coordinate tables/figures described). Participant ages and healthy control status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly reported. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, resting baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/only clinical samples) apply. Therefore INCLUDE.

Although this PET study reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (timing tasks versus an active control) with coordinates and sufficient participant/task information, the experimental paradigm probes motor/temporal timing (synchronization and continuation tapping) rather than established executive function domains. Moreover, the study includes Parkinson’s disease patients (not restricted to healthy individuals), which violates exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess executive function/cognitive control task), I9 (task not within established executive function domains). Therefore exclude.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes participants outside the 18–60 year range (adolescents aged 10–17) and is not restricted to adults only. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive/cognitive control), I6 (within-participant contrasts: no-go vs go, incongruent vs congruent, switch vs repeat), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and whole-brain regression), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (tasks fall within established executive domains: inhibition and cognitive flexibility), I10 (participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Although adult-only subgroup maps are reported, the overall sample includes minors which triggers E8, therefore the study must be excluded under the review’s predefined criteria.

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis): although it reports group-level voxelwise contrasts, the imaging covered limited transverse slices (not whole-brain coverage), and the authors explicitly state they could not scan the whole brain. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive-function tasks: go/no-go and WCST), I6 (within-participant contrasts: no-go vs go), I8 (results reported in figures and coordinates), I9 (tasks are established executive domains: inhibition and set-shifting), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). No exclusion criteria were violated (exclusion criteria applied: []). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (executive function: working memory, set-shifting/cognitive flexibility) in healthy adults. It reports within-participant contrasts of task variants versus a high-level active baseline (A-HLB, B-HLB, C-HLB) and differential contrasts (A–B, A–C, B–C). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are performed (SPM2) and results are reported with coordinates, tables and figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are provided (12 healthy right-handed adults, age 19–36). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group task contrasts; uses an active baseline; empirical data; healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to task-based executive fMRI: (I5) task-based fMRI assessing inhibition; (I6) within-participant activation vs active control contrasts; (I7) group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with clusterwise inference; (I8) results reported with coordinates and figures; (I9) tasks fall within executive function (response inhibition); (I10) participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and paradigm are reported. However, the sample includes both medicated schizophrenia patients and healthy controls (i.e., the study is not restricted to healthy individuals), which violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Because any exclusion criterion being met requires exclusion, this study is excluded despite providing usable healthy-control activation data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. The study is an fMRI task-based, within-subject investigation of executive functions (WCST and n-back) and reports voxelwise activation with coordinates; it meets I5, I6, I8, I9 and I10. However, it does NOT meet I7: results are based on partial-brain coverage (four contiguous slices) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map, so a qualifying whole-brain analysis is absent. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain evidence).

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of response inhibition using a go–nogo paradigm in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. It therefore satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI of executive control), I6 (within-participant contrasts such as NOGO vs GO), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (coordinates and whole-brain results described), and I9 (inhibition domain). However, I10 is not fully satisfied because the full text does not report participant ages or an age range (it only states “eighteen healthy subjects”), whereas I10 requires reporting of participant age information in addition to sample health status, imaging modality, and task. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because not all inclusion criteria are met (specifically I10).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=11 in final analyses; mean age 24) that directly investigates executive function domains (inhibition and working memory) using multiple established paradigms. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing task conditions to active control/oddball conditions (no-go vs oddball, stop vs oddball, incongruent vs congruent flanker, verbal/spatial WM vs control), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses implemented in SPM (with tables/figures and coordinate reporting). Participant health status, age, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active controls, empirical data in healthy 18–60-year-olds). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (Go/No-Go inhibition) in healthy adults (age range 19–40) using a within-subject design. The analysis models event types (hits, correct rejections, false alarms) and reports group-level, whole-brain SPM results (FDR-corrected) with coordinates and tables describing task-evoked activation. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go), an established executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., no-go vs infrequent-go; infrequent-go vs frequent-go), group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with voxelwise thresholds and FDR correction, and provides tables/figures of activations. Participants are healthy adults (n=25; ages 20–27), right-handed, with imaging modality and task adequately described. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=14, ages 18–31) using a task that probes inhibitory executive function (linguistic go/no-go). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (No-Go vs Go; Negative vs Neutral; interaction contrasts) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM random-effects with appropriate multiple-comparison corrections; results are reported as SPM maps and tables of coordinates. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/No-go) in healthy adults (n=42, ages 18–46). It reports within-subject contrasts of successful No-go (STOPS) versus ongoing Go trials, provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, and tables of coordinates), and describes participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task details. The task falls within the executive function domain (inhibition). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy and within age range). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This paper is a meta-analysis (ALE) of previously published fMRI Go/No-go studies and does not present original human neuroimaging data or within-participant task activation contrasts from participants. Therefore it meets exclusion E7 (non-empirical paper / meta-analysis without original neuroimaging data). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates / ALE), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: inhibition), I10 (reports relevant information about participant samples, imaging modality, and task paradigms). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an original fMRI/PET study of participants), I6 (no within-participant contrast from original participant data reported by this paper), I7 (does not provide an original group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map derived from participant data). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Exclusion applied: E7.

This is an fMRI Go/No-Go study of voluntary swallowing in healthy adults. Although it uses a Go/No-Go design, the study’s primary focus is sensorimotor control of swallowing rather than investigation of executive functions/cognitive control. Critically, the group-level analyses are ROI-based (counts of activated voxels within anatomically-defined ROIs with pairwise t-tests) rather than whole-brain, voxelwise group statistical maps. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). The study does report participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm (I10 met). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not primarily assess executive function/cognitive control), I6 (no clear within-participant contrast of an executive-function task vs an active control in the sense required), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), I9 (task does not clearly fall within established executive function domains as framed by this meta-analysis). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study of response inhibition using somatosensory go/no-go tasks in healthy adults. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with coordinates/figures and tests no-go and go conditions, satisfying active task contrasts. Participant demographics (age 19–32), health status, imaging modality, and task details are reported. The task assesses inhibition (an executive function). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes active task conditions, empirical, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of sustained attention (vigilance, an executive function domain) including a healthy adult control group (ages 18–50). It contains within-participant contrasts against an active control (visual countdown baseline) and event-related contrasts (correct rejections vs. other trial types). The paper describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (composite within-group activation maps with voxelwise one-sample t-tests and cluster correction), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures and ROI analyses. Participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive-function/inhibition tasks (go/no-go, flanker, SRC) in healthy adults (ages 18–25). It includes within-participant contrasts isolating inhibition-related activity (no-go vs go; incongruent vs congruent; incompatible vs compatible), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM99 results, FDR-corrected thresholds) with tables/figures of coordinates, and provides participant, task, and imaging details. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references, so core content appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-only baseline, not non-empirical, participants are within 18–60 and healthy).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using an n-back verbal working memory task (executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (2-back vs 0-back; emotion vs neutral; interaction contrasts) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a within-subjects task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=12, mean age 23.7) that includes a canonical executive-function paradigm (Go/No-go) probing response inhibition and reports within-participant contrasts (No-go > Go). Analyses were random-effects, whole-brain, voxelwise, with thresholding and tables/figures of activated regions and conjunction/exclusive masks. The paper provides participant demographics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses an active control, is empirical, and includes healthy adults in the 18–60 range).

Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the primary within-subject contrast reported and analyzed is Go/No-go > rest; rest/fixation is the only baseline used rather than an active control). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — Go/No-go/inhibition), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-group activation maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within established executive function domain — inhibition), I10 (participant/sample, modality, and task details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive function task relative to an active control condition). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because I6 is not satisfied and E6 is met, this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This empirical fMRI study uses executive-function tasks (N-back working memory and Go/No-go inhibition), performs within-subject GLM contrasts (pairwise condition contrasts), and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps registered to MNI space. Participant demographics (healthy adults age 18–50), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are described. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-groups-only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a single-subject fMRI case study (n=1) that reports within-subject planning > non-planning whole-brain voxelwise maps. However inclusion criterion I7 requires a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. Although the study provides whole-brain maps and meets other inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I8, I9, I10), it does not provide group-level analyses and therefore does not satisfy I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of inhibition with within-subject contrasts and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results in healthy participants (adults), the sample includes children (9–12 years) in addition to adults. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrasts: no-go vs go), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (results reported in tables/figures and text), I9 (task is response inhibition, an executive domain), I10 (participant ages, health status, imaging modality, and task described). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60 due to E8.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control (task switching) in healthy adults. It uses within-subject contrasts (mixed-task vs single-task; task-switch vs task-repeat) that probe executive function, and employs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVAs) with voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds. Participant demographics (N=13, age range 19–26, healthy), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported in detail. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active task contrasts beyond fixation, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (age 23–35) using a go/no-go inhibitory control paradigm, which is an established executive function (inhibition). The design includes within-subject contrasts (no-go vs go) and a crossover manipulation; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using permutation-based mapping and cluster-level inference, with results reported as coordinates and figures. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation, uses an active control condition, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/No-go), an executive function domain (inhibition). It reports within-subject contrasts (No-go vs Go and vs baseline) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with correction for multiple comparisons. Participant information (n=16, mean age 30.2, healthy) and imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and task details are provided. Whole-brain results are described and reported in tables/figures (coordinates and images). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (age 28–61) that examines executive functions (working memory, response inhibition, planning) using N-Back, Go-NoGo, and Tower of London tasks. It reports within-participant task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back, 2-back vs rest, NoGo vs Go) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with coordinates and FWE-corrected results. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go) reporting group-level whole-brain, multiple-comparison–corrected task-activation maps and adequate participant/task/imaging details, it must be excluded. Primary reasons: (1) The within-participant contrast used is GNG versus fixation (rest), and the study uses fixation as the baseline/control condition rather than an active control task — this meets exclusion criterion E6. (2) The sample includes clinical participants (Tourette disorder) and is not restricted to healthy adults, meeting exclusion criterion E8 for studies not restricted to healthy individuals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and shown), I9 (task within executive function domain — inhibition), and I10 (reported participant ages, healthy sample info, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (within-participant contrast relative to an active control condition). Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

This study reports task-based fMRI of task-switching (an executive function: cognitive flexibility) and includes within-subject contrasts (informatively cued switch > repeat and repeat > switch). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2 with coordinates and cluster thresholds reported (tables/figures). The paper reports control (healthy) participant demographics, task paradigm, and imaging modality. Although the study also includes a schizophrenia patient group, within-group whole-brain results for the healthy control group are explicitly reported, making the study eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, only between-group contrasts, resting-state baseline only, non-empirical paper, or missing healthy adult within-group maps) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 18–27) using a task-switching paradigm (cognitive flexibility) with within-subject contrasts (switch vs repeat; high vs low reward) and additional contrasts (reward anticipation vs receipt). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed with cluster-level correction and region coordinates/figures reported. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not patient vs control only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials referenced but not required. All inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (WCST), a canonical executive function (cognitive flexibility/set-shifting) paradigm, conducted in healthy adult participants (N=11; mean age 24, range 18–31). The paper reports within-subject contrasts between WCST event periods and active control trials, performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (thresholding, random-effects), and provides tables/figures of activation peaks. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (verbal n-back working memory) in healthy adult controls and includes within-subject contrasts (1/2/3-back vs 0-back active control). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported with coordinates and thresholding; within-group activation maps for the healthy control sample are presented. Participant ages (18–45 for patients, 18–42 for controls), healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm details are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines working memory using an audiospatial n-back task (1-, 2-, 3-back) in healthy adults (ages 20–30). It uses within-subject contrasts of memory load (3-back vs 1-back; 2-back vs 1-back), employs voxelwise, group-level whole-brain statistical analyses (voxelwise t-tests, Talairach coordinates reported, figures/tables), and reports participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details. Working memory is an established executive-function domain. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain results are reported; not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; not between-group only; active control used; empirical study with healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines planning (Tower of London) in healthy adults and reports voxelwise activation maps, but it lacks an active control task contrast: baseline is fixation/rest and analyses compare task difficulty levels to fixation and across conditions. This violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline without an active control) and fails inclusion criterion I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control). Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/planning), I7 (group-level voxelwise/statistical maps presented), I8 (whole-brain results described in figures/tables), I9 (task is planning). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no active-control contrast), I10 (participant ages not explicitly reported; only described as undergraduates). Full text is complete for screening.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=45, ages 18–45) using established executive function paradigms (Go/No-Go inhibition; Reward/No-Reward; Loss/No-Loss). It reports within-subject contrasts (No-Go>Go, Reward>No-Reward, Loss>No-Loss) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster reports; results are presented in figures and tables (coordinates). Participant health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. Thus all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly tests response inhibition (Go/No-go) and a working-memory-loaded variant. It reports within-subject contrasts (No-go vs Go and task vs baseline), uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with correction for multiple comparisons (P≤0.05), and provides tables/figures with coordinates. Participant age, healthy status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, not rest-only baseline, empirical human data, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive control (task-switching Stroop) in healthy adults (N=12, ages 18–30). It reports within-subject contrasts (instruction: color naming > word reading; response: incongruent > congruent), group-level voxelwise spatial F maps pooled across subjects, and reports coordinates for activations. Imaging modality, participant age/health, and task paradigm are clearly described. Results include whole-brain analyses (spatial F maps) and coordinate reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active task contrasts, empirical with original human data, participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E3 met: authors report analyses restricted to preselected regions of interest (motor cortex and preSMA) rather than a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function/inhibition go/no-go task), I6 (within-participant contrast of go vs no-go), I9 (inhibition is an established executive function domain), I10 (participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise map), I8 (not applicable because no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 25.5) using a cued task-switching paradigm (cognitive flexibility/executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., switch vs. repeat, cues vs. targets, targets vs. baseline) including group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with activation foci reported in tables and figures, and small-volume-corrected ROI follow-ups. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, not patient or out-of-range ages, and uses active task contrasts beyond rest). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included.

This is an fMRI Stroop study of inhibition with within-subject contrasts (Incongruent vs Congruent/Neutral), whole-brain voxelwise group SPM analyses reported (tables/figures), and full reporting of participants (healthy screening), modality, and paradigm. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample includes older adults recruited from a retirement association (participants clearly outside the 18–60 age range). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8 (includes participants outside 18–60). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite satisfying the inclusion criteria above. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in healthy adults (ages 21–53). The paper reports within-subject, group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (1-back vs 0-back, 2-back vs 0-back, 2-back vs 1-back) using random-effects SPM analyses and corrected SPM{Z} maps; results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates. An active baseline (0-back) was used. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (4T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of inhibition (executive function) in healthy adults, reporting within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with coordinates and figures. Participant demographics (n=20, age range 21–37), healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms (Stroop manual and imitation-inhibition) are reported. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the text appears complete for screening purposes.

Exclusion criterion E8 met: study includes clinical (Parkinson's disease) patients (not restricted to healthy individuals) and control participants whose ages range up to 68 years (outside the 18–60 inclusion window). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function - WCST), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs active control conditions reported), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with correction and reported peaks/tables), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within cognitive flexibility/executive function), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status for controls, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is excluded because it violates two exclusion criteria: E3 and E8. E3: The reported neuroimaging results in the provided full text focus on activity within a scene-selective ROI (left parahippocampal/lingual gyrus) and ROI-based comparisons; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinate results are described in the main text, so it appears to report only ROI analyses. E8: The participant sample includes older adults aged 60–77 years, which falls outside the review’s eligible age range of 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory/executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts: remember vs ignore vs passive), I9 (task within executive function domain: working memory/inhibition), and I10 (participant ages reported, healthy sample, imaging modality and task paradigm described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses task-based fMRI of an inhibition (go/no-go) executive function paradigm with within-subject no-go>go contrasts and reports whole-brain group-level results (tables/coordinates and figures). However, the participant sample consists of boys aged 8–20 years and includes clinical (ADHD) participants and unaffected siblings, i.e., participants are not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8 (participants outside 18–60 and not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (results reported in tables/figures), I9 (task falls within inhibition domain), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 are satisfied), but exclusion E8 applies, so the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis of healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of executive control (stop-signal task) in healthy adults (ages 22–42). It reports within-subject contrasts (stop vs go; post-stop stop-success vs post-go stop-success), uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM with reported coordinates and thresholding, and provides participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-baseline only, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of inhibition tasks in healthy participants that meets multiple inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) but must be excluded because participants are children/adolescents (mean age ~14.7 years), violating the review’s age restriction (Exclusion E8). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrasts: incongruent vs congruent, on vs off), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps and thresholded Z-stat images), I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (tasks in inhibition domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable inclusions are satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (participants outside 18–60 years). Therefore EXCLUDED on grounds of E8.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (n-back), an executive function domain, in adult participants. It includes within-participant contrasts (1-back vs 0-back, 2-back vs 0-back), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2, provides coordinates/tables and figures, and reports participant demographics and healthy control status. Importantly, the paper presents within-group activation results for the healthy control sample, which satisfies the meta-analysis requirement for healthy adult task activations. Although the study also includes cocaine-dependent participants, the healthy control whole-brain activation maps and relevant methodological details are reported, so inclusion is appropriate. Full text content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Inclusion criteria met: I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10. No exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 19–43). It reports within-subject contrasts isolating successful vs. unsuccessful inhibition (both contrasted to active go trials) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mapping (generic brain activation maps with permutation testing and cluster-level inference). Results are reported as coordinates, figures, and time-series plots. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm/methods are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active task baseline rather than rest, is empirical with original data, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included.

Full text appears incomplete: provided content is largely references and metadata without core article sections (methods, results, group-level analyses). From available information, I5 (fMRI study assessing executive function task-based paradigm) and I9 (task = working memory, an executive function) are satisfied by title/metadata. However I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), I8 (clear reporting of whole-brain results), and I10 (reported participant age, healthy sample confirmation, imaging modality details, and task paradigm) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met based on available text. Because essential methodological/results details are missing (fulltext_incomplete=true), I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria, so the study is excluded pending full text. Inclusion met: I5, I9. Inclusion not met/unclear: I6, I7, I8, I10. Exclusion applied: []

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Stroop color-word task (an established executive function/inhibition paradigm) with within-subject contrasts (e.g., incongruent − NI, congruent − NC, blocked contrasts C−N, etc.). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLMs using FLAME with cluster-wise correction and reported coordinates/tables and figures. Relevant participant information (young adult, college-enrolled controls, age matching, confirmation of healthy control group), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. Although the study includes a clinical ADHD group, within-group task activation maps and contrasts for the healthy control subjects are reported, allowing extraction of healthy adult activations. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria were met.

Although the study meets all methodological inclusion criteria (fMRI task assessing executive functions; within-subject contrasts for N-Back and AX-CPT; group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with coordinates; tasks fall within executive domains; participant/imaging/task details provided), it includes a clinical sample (schizophrenia patients) and is not restricted to healthy adults. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the record must be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to healthy adult task activations.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (2-back) and sustained attention in healthy adults reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 met). However, the contrasts are task versus resting baseline with eyes closed (no active control condition), so it uses rest as the only baseline and therefore violates exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast against an active control) is not met. Full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (age 18–25) using a continuous performance task (CPT‑IP) that targets sustained attention/vigilance — an executive function domain. Analyses include within-participant contrasts (CPT‑IP blocks > active control blocks ‘1 2 3 4’) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (voxelwise p<0.001, cluster-corrected), with results reported as anatomical loci/coordinates. Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (verbal 2-back) in healthy adults (mean age 30). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing the 2-back activation to an active control (0-back/one-letter search), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level ANOVA and conjunction, with tables/coordinates), and provides participant demographics, health-screening, imaging modality, and full methods/results/discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (stop-signal paradigm) in healthy adults (ages 20–33). It reports within-participant contrasts (SST vs NST, UST vs NST, SST vs UST) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99; thresholds and extent reported), with coordinates/tables provided. The task falls under executive function (inhibition). Participant health status, ages, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using an n-back working memory task in healthy adults (age 21–29) with within-subject contrasts (0-, 1-, 2-back) including a linear memory-load contrast and memory load × stimulus interactions. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed using SPM99 and results (including MNI coordinates and thresholding information) are reported. The task (working memory) is an established executive-function domain. Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, baseline includes an active 0-back control, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility) in healthy adults (n=16, age 21–29). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (task switch vs task repetition—an active control), a group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis with thresholded z-maps and reported coordinates/figures, and provides participant, imaging (3T fMRI), and task-paradigm details. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Exclusion criterion E8 met: the study includes participants outside the 18–60 age range (healthy controls aged 49–70, with some controls up to 70) and the overall sample is not restricted to healthy individuals (Parkinson's disease patients are also included). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of executive function — Tower of London planning), I6 (within-participant contrasts via parametric analyses across task difficulty and task-level comparisons), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and figures), I9 (planning is an established executive function), I10 (participant ages, health status of controls, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 were satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of the Stroop task (inhibition), an established executive function. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent > congruent and incongruent > control) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and cluster significance thresholds. Participant information (healthy native Japanese adults, ages reported, mean age 36, right-handed) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. The control condition uses color-neutral words (an active control), and the analyses are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only nor to between-group contrasts. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go) in healthy adults (N=6, ages 22–30). It reports within-participant contrasts including go/no-go vs go (an active task control) and go/no-go vs visual control, using group-level voxelwise SPM99 analyses with thresholded whole-brain maps and tables/figures of significant clusters/coordinates. Participant health, age range, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and the task paradigm are described. Although the group analysis used fixed-effects (limiting generalizability), the study nevertheless provides whole-brain, group-level activation maps and coordinate tables suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function (inhibition) activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references and appears complete.

The study meets multiple inclusion criteria for the task-based neuroimaging meta-analysis (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10): it is an fMRI study (I5) using n-back working-memory tasks (I9) with within-participant contrasts (Simple subtraction of active control; I6), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps/tables/figures for control adults (I7,I8), and provides participant ages, imaging modality, and task details (I10). Exclusion(s) met: E8 — participants are aged 50–70 years, which falls outside the review age range of 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts: manipulation/retrieval vs maintenance and vs motor control), I7 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analysis reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and illustrated), I9 (task falls within executive domain: working memory), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: None (all required inclusion criteria were reported/satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because E8 is violated (age outside 18–60), the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (one- and two-back vs zero-back active control), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps using permutation-based cluster inference. Participant details (healthy adults aged 21–29), imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), and task paradigm are all clearly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion based on E3: the study does not provide a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Although fMRI contrasts (Difficult vs. Control; Easy vs. Control) and individual subject SPM t-maps were computed, group analyses were performed on manually defined VOI spatial-extent measures (percent suprathreshold voxels) using t-tests rather than a voxelwise whole-brain group map. Additionally, image acquisition covered only eight axial slices of the superior brain (not whole-brain coverage). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — planning/Tower of London), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs an active control condition), I9 (task falls in executive domain — planning), I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the study is excluded under E3.

This is a review/methods paper (non-empirical) that summarizes and illustrates covariance-based analyses using prior PET/fMRI studies but does not report original empirical, within-participant task vs active-control contrasts or group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps for a healthy sample. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E7 (non-empirical paper). Inclusion criteria not met include: I5 (not an original fMRI/PET study assessing executive function), I6 (no within-participant contrasts reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps provided), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results presented), I9 (although working-memory/executive topics are discussed, no original task data are reported), and I10 (no participant/sample imaging details for an original empirical study). No inclusion criteria are satisfied by this article as the study itself is a review/methods paper.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract available). Based on the abstract: meets I5 (fMRI study of cognitive interference/executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast: interference vs. neutral), and I9 (task maps to inhibition/cognitive interference). However, I cannot confirm I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map) because the abstract only reports group activity without specifying whole-brain voxelwise results or tables/coordinates/figures. I10 is not fully satisfied because participant ages are not numerically reported (only described as "adult volunteers"). No exclusion criteria (E3-E8) are clearly met. Because not all inclusion criteria can be verified from the provided content, I exclude the study pending full-text review.

This study is a PET task-based neuroimaging experiment using a working-memory (N-back) paradigm (executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (2-back minus 0-back active control), provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and thresholded activation maps with stereotactic coordinates and figures, and gives participant demographics (ages, healthy control status), imaging modality (H2(15)O PET), and full methods/results/discussion. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes within-group healthy control activations (so E5 not met), reports whole-brain task activations (E3/E4 not met), uses an active control (not rest-only; E6 not met), is empirical human imaging data (E7 not met), and the healthy control subgroup falls within the adult age range (E8 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task), an executive function domain (inhibition). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., StopSuccess vs StopFailure; StopSuccess vs Go with 0% stop probability) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level inference and reported coordinates/figures. Participant information (n=24, ages 19–26, healthy) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, baseline includes active Go trials, and sample is healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI Stroop (inhibition) task and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps for healthy controls and TBI patients, with participant ages, modality, and task described. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast against an active control condition—task activation is contrasted against rest/fixation only. Additionally, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (it explicitly includes TBI patients), which conflicts with the review’s focus on healthy adults. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E6 (rest/fixation as only baseline) and E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) with simultaneous EEG. It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., Load 7 vs Load 3; comparisons across loads and to Load 0 baseline), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM5 with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level correction, and provides participant demographics (20 healthy right-handed adults, age 18–28), imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.
