No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range participants) are met. Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (visual target switching/working memory) in healthy adults (N=9, ages 19–42). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., target switching vs. non-switching) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses with voxel-wise FDR correction and tables/figures of coordinates and maps. Imaging modality, participant health/ages, and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. It reports within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 1-back for Category and Location), uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction, and presents results in figures/tables. Participant age, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported (healthy adults, 18–30). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an event-related whole-brain fMRI study of executive function (interference suppression and response inhibition) with within-subject contrasts (incongruent>neutral, no-go>neutral), clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, coordinate reporting, and full reporting of participant demographics and healthy status, the sample includes children (ages 8–12) in addition to adults. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the 18–60 years range or not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I-criteria were reported), but exclusion E8 is met because participants fall outside the 18–60 age range.

The study is an fMRI investigation of an executive function task (n-back working memory) in healthy adults (mean age 36.3, range 25–51). It reports within-subject contrast analyses (parametric modulation of BOLD by n-back difficulty) and group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level random-effects maps (SPM2) with FDR correction; results are presented as maps, tables, and coordinates. Task falls within working memory (an established executive domain). Participant/sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), this is task-evoked fMRI (not resting-state or connectivity-only), within-group contrasts in healthy participants are provided, and participants are within the 18–60 age range. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI Stroop study of cognitive control in healthy adults with within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and full reporting of participants, ages, modality, and paradigm (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, all task activation statistical inference was carried out within an a priori ROI mask (BAs 24/32, 8/9/46, 7/40) using SPM2 and significance was reported within these ROIs; no whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task-evoked activation map is reported. Because the paper reports only ROI-constrained task results (and not whole-brain voxelwise activation maps), it violates exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (stop-signal task) in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 20). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (GO/STOP vs GO ONLY; correct vs incorrect STOP trials; parametric modulation of STOP likelihood) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (thresholding, coordinates, figures, and tables). Participant health status, age, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical sample). Full text is complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=43, age 18–30) using the Stop-signal task (inhibition), an established executive function domain. It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., StopInhibit–Go, StopInhibit–Fixation, Go–Fixation) comparing task conditions (active control Go), and reports group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (second-level contrasts for the entire group; search region = 137,514 voxels). Although primary statistical inference is reported within anatomically defined ROIs with small-volume correction, the methods describe whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis and results include MNI coordinates and statistical maps/figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, empirical with human data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines inhibitory control (go/no-go), reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (PLS) with tables/figures and coordinates, and provides participant demographics and healthy screening. However, it includes older participants aged 60–80 years, i.e., participants outside the eligible 18–60 age range for this review, violating exclusion criterion E8. Therefore, despite meeting all inclusion criteria (I5–I10), the study must be excluded because it includes participants older than 60. (a) Exclusion met: E8. (b) Inclusion met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. (c) Inclusion not met: none.)

This fMRI study reports task-based whole-brain activation during an established executive-function task (Chinese-character Stroop; inhibition/action-monitoring). It includes within-participant task-vs-control contrasts and presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results for the normal control group (one-sample t-test; fixed-effects maps and tables/figures), with between-group random-effects analyses also reported. Participant demographics and screening for healthy controls are described; imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are fully detailed. Age range reported for patients is 18–60 and groups did not differ in age; healthy control status is confirmed. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory in healthy adults (N=14) using a Sternberg paradigm, which falls under executive function. The study reports within-subject contrasts of the experimental (working memory) condition versus an active control task, and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests) were performed and thresholded, with results reported in tables/figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and full task/method details are provided. Although reporting emphasized ROIs (foci reported only within predefined ROIs), a whole-brain voxelwise group analysis was conducted, satisfying the whole-brain map requirement. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an event-related fMRI study of planning (Tower of London) in healthy adult participants (n=17, ages 21–39) that reports within-participant contrasts of the executive/planning task versus two active control conditions. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects, p<0.05 FWE-corrected) with activation coordinates in tables and figures. The study clearly reports participant demographics, imaging modality and task paradigm. The task falls within an established executive-function domain (planning). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not using rest/fixation as the only baseline, and this is original empirical human neuroimaging data with participants in the 18–60 range. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (female, age 19–33) using a Stroop paradigm that targets executive function (inhibition/conflict). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent trials; ATD vs BAL) and behavioral measures. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (cluster-corrected; results reported in tables/figures and coordinates), and ROI analyses are supplementary — satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text content including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This study reports task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults performing an N-Back working memory task (executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (2-Back vs 0-Back active control), group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and reported coordinates (with correction and small-volume results), and provides participant demographics and imaging/task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not patient-group-only, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This fMRI paper investigates amygdala responses to anticipation of pain while subjects perform a Continuous Performance Task (CPT) as an active coping manipulation. Although imaging, healthy adult sample, ages, and task details are reported (I10), the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirements: (1) the primary focus is emotional/pain anticipation rather than an executive-function/cognitive-control task contrast (fails I5 and I9); (2) it does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map for an executive-function contrast — results are reported as ROI-based amygdala analyses (meets exclusion E3 and fails I7/I8); and (3) there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition as required (fails I6). Therefore the study should be excluded from a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

Although this fMRI study assesses an executive-domain task (sustained attention/CPT-IP) and reports whole-brain, group-level, within-subject activation maps for healthy participants, it also includes a clinical sample (unmedicated bipolar patients) and is not restricted to healthy individuals. Exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60 years or not restricted to healthy individuals) therefore applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive/cognitive control task), I6 (within-participant contrast of task vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), I9 (task falls in executive domain: vigilance/sustained attention), I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore exclude per E8.

Although this study meets the inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI of executive function using a working memory reading-span task, within-participant contrasts against an active baseline, group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis reported, and participant/ imaging/ task details provided), it includes an elderly participant group (mean age 68.8, range 65–71). This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60). Because any exclusion criterion triggers exclusion, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study assesses working memory (an executive function) with within-subject n-back load analyses and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps, it recruited both healthy control subjects and clinical patient groups (hyperthyroid, hypothyroid, subclinical hypothyroid). The review exclusion criterion E8 disallows studies not restricted to healthy individuals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task fMRI on executive function—working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts across n-back levels/0-back as active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain activation maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/figures), I9 (task within executive domain), I10 (participant ages, health status, imaging modality, paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Therefore excluded due to E8 (not restricted to healthy participants). Full text appears complete.

The full text is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 23.9) investigating conflict, task-switching, and errors—established executive functions. It uses within-subject contrasts (e.g., correct incongruent vs correct congruent; task-switch vs correct incongruent; error vs correct), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholds, cluster correction) with coordinates and figures. Imaging modality, task paradigms, and participant details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=19, mean age 26.6) using a task that probes emotional conflict resolution—a form of cognitive control/inhibition. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; high vs low conflict-resolution trials), group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) with reported MNI coordinates, and detailed methods (task, acquisition, preprocessing, and analyses). Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting baseline only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10.

Excluded due to E8: the study sample includes participants outside the 18–60 year age range (older adult group mean age = 67), which violates the review's age restriction. The study meets the following inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function—working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts comparing combination vs. feature conditions), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported and localized), I8 (whole-brain results reported via coordinates and figures), I9 (task falls within executive function domain—working memory), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No inclusion criteria are unmet. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), but exclusion E8 necessitates exclusion from the meta-analysis.

This study includes both schizophrenia patients and healthy controls and is not restricted to healthy adult participants, violating exclusion criterion E8. It otherwise meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (fMRI study of working memory, an executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts: 1-,2-,3-back vs 0-back), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain t-maps were computed), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/tables), I9 (task is working memory, an executive domain), and I10 (participant ages, healthy-control status, imaging modality, and task described). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (study not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to healthy adults despite providing usable within-group data for controls.

This is an empirical fMRI study of reversal learning (a cognitive flexibility/executive function task) in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–30). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., first postreversal vs. second acquisition; errors vs. acquisition) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and coordinate tables. Task paradigm, imaging modality, and participant demographics/health screening are clearly reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study used task-based fMRI of working memory (2-back) with an active control (CPT-X) and reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and coordinate/figure results, and provided participant age, health status screening, imaging modality, and task details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: participants include ages 13–28 (minors <18) and the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (includes non-psychotic first-degree relatives at genetic risk for schizophrenia). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (n-back for faces) in healthy adults (ages 21–27). It reports within-subject contrasts across task loads (0-, 1-, 2-back; 0-back serves as an active control) and performs group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with reported Talairach coordinates and tables/figures. Participant demographics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, baseline includes active control, empirical with healthy adult sample). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This fMRI study examines working memory (auditory N-back) in cognitively intact adults and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group and within-subject (2-back vs 0-back) contrasts with coordinates and participant/task details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample age range was 25–75 years, which includes participants older than 60 and therefore violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis despite meeting the other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=57, mean age 28.6) using a modified flanker/no-go task assessing inhibition and interference monitoring (executive function). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (INC>CON, NOGO>CON, INC>NEU, NOGO>NEU) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99 random-effects) with tables/figures of activations and coordinates, and provides participant demographics, task details, imaging methods, and behavioral correlations. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations in healthy adults aged 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it is not restricted to healthy adults (includes schizophrenia and depressed patient groups) and appears to report primarily between-group contrasts without a clear within-group whole-brain task activation contrast for the healthy control sample. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals) and E5 (only between-group contrasts presented / no clear within-group healthy participant activation map provided). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive/context processing), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported for between-group effects), I8 (results described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function/working memory domain), I10 (participant demographics, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no explicit within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition reported for healthy participants). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is excluded because it uses rest as the baseline (activation vs rest block design) and does not include an active control condition for the within-participant contrast, violating inclusion criterion I6 and meeting exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function—modified Stroop), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported as tables/figures/coordinates), I9 (task falls within executive/inhibition domain), I10 (participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 27.4; N=18) using a Sternberg task. It reports within-subject contrasts of the WM task versus an active control (arrow task) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 with FDR correction; results reported as statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Participant health status, age, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses an active control, empirical, healthy adult sample). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function in healthy adults (working memory, response selection/conflict monitoring). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., Repeat-Unexpected vs Repeat-Expected; Refresh vs Repeat) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with reported coordinates and ROI analyses. Participant demographics (n=16, ages 18–27, healthy, right-handed), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are provided. The design includes active control conditions (Repeat vs Refresh) and multiple within-participant contrasts that map onto executive function domains. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials are not required. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of semantic verbal fluency in healthy adults that explicitly examines cognitive control demands (pacing, inhibition, working memory, sustained attention). It contains within-subject task>control contrasts (task blocks vs. an active control saying “nothing”), reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures of activations, and provides participant demographics (ages 21–37) and health status. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, uses an active control, is empirical, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because inclusion criterion I10 is not met: the full text does not report participant ages (it notes seven healthy right-handed male subjects but gives no age information). The study does meet I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function using the WCST), I6 (within-participant contrasts across 3D/2D/1D conditions), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported across seven subjects), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures and coordinates), and I9 (task assesses cognitive flexibility). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E8: none). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of the Multi-Source Interference Task (MSIT) in healthy adults (mean age 30.4) that probes cognitive control/interference (an executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (interference vs control), reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses in Talairach space with figures and tables of coordinates, and provides participant demographics, imaging modality, and task details. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–41) assessing executive function (spatial N-back working memory and verbal fluency). It includes within-participant contrasts of an executive task versus an active control (2-back vs 0-back), and reports group-level whole-brain mixed-effects voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected) with peaks/localizations described in text/tables and figures. Task paradigms, imaging modality and parameters, participant screening confirming healthy status, and ages are reported. Hematological measures and control visual stimulation are described, and behavioral results are provided. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active control, empirical human imaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and references. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to probe an executive function (planning via the Tower of London task), reports within-participant contrasts (easy and difficult TOL conditions vs yoked active control), and presents group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM results, corrected P<0.05) with coordinates and figures. Participant details confirm healthy adult samples within the 18–60 range and imaging modality and paradigms are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and quality metrics, so it appears complete. Inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion met: E8 — the study includes a clinical schizophrenia patient group and is not restricted to healthy individuals. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI; 2-back working memory with faces), I6 (within-participant contrast of WM task vs active control condition), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task is working memory, an executive-function domain), I10 (participant age range, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because any exclusion criterion suffices for exclusion, I exclude this study based on E8.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a counting Stroop (inhibition) paradigm, reporting within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-model ANOVA with cluster-thresholding). Participant age (mean 39, range 27–56) and health screening (no Axis I disorders) are reported. Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps/clusters and tables/figures, and the task falls within established executive function domains (inhibition/response inhibition). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-group contrasts, active task baseline used, empirical human neuroimaging data, healthy adults aged 18–60).

Although this fMRI study uses a two-back verbal working-memory task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps for both patients and healthy controls, it does not include a within-subject contrast of the executive task against an active control condition. The paradigm used blocks of 2-back stimuli contrasted with rest/fixation (with occasional motor events during rest to balance motor responses), i.e., rest is the primary baseline. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (task vs an active control) is not met and exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control) applies. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London) in healthy adults (ages 19–38). It reports within-participant contrasts between task conditions (ambiguous vs unambiguous; single vs multiple solution paths; planning vs execution), uses group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected maps, and provides participant demographics, imaging modality and task details. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for executive-function domain (planning), within-subject task contrasts, whole-brain group maps, and reporting of sample/imaging details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, includes active task condition contrasts beyond fixation, and participants are healthy within 18–60). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using the Stop-signal task (inhibition), an established executive function paradigm. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., successful and unsuccessful Stop-trials vs. Go-trials and vs. Stop-irrelevant trials) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates, tables, and figures. Participant demographics (n=15 after exclusions, mean age 22.9, healthy), imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete. Recommended for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (stop-signal task) in healthy adults (N=54, ages 22–45). It reports within-participant contrasts relevant to executive control (SE>G for errors; pSEi>pSEni for post-error slowing), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (figures and peak coordinates, FWE-corrected values). Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are all reported. Although the paper also includes connectivity analyses (GCM/GCA), it additionally provides whole-brain task activation maps, so exclusion criteria for connectivity-only or ROI-only studies do not apply. Full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Thus all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met; no exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI to assess working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain (I5, I9). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of n-back levels versus a 0-back active control (I6) and provides group-level whole-brain, voxelwise activation maps and coordinates with permutation clusterwise thresholds (I7, I8). Relevant participant details (ages 22–45), healthy control sample description, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported (I10). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group without within-group in healthy participants, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages/restricted healthy-sample violations) are met. Thus the study is eligible for inclusion.

Excluded because the paper reports primarily between-group (CHR vs. healthy) whole-brain group comparisons and does not present an accompanying group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy sample alone. For the planned meta-analysis of executive-function activations in healthy adults we require within-group healthy activation maps; absence of those maps meets exclusion criterion E5.

Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of an executive task: n-back working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast performed: 2-back vs 0-back), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables), I9 (task falls within executive function domain), I10 (participant/sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). 

Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported for the healthy group alone). 

Exclusion criterion applied: E5 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying within-group healthy task activation contrast).

This paper is an fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain, in healthy adult participants (mean age 27; N=13 analyzed). It reports within-subject contrasts of executive-task conditions (e.g., lag 2 vs lag 1; comparison vs identity match) and task×material interactions rather than only rest, satisfying the requirement for within-participant task contrasts. Analyses were group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM2 random-effects results (FDR correction reported for some contrasts) with coordinates and tables described in the text and figures. Participant characteristics, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy participants) apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET H2[15O] study of the Tower of London (planning) meets multiple inclusion criteria for the review (see below) but should be excluded because it violates age and baseline requirements. Exclusion reasons: (E8) participants include ages up to 70 years (age range 49–70), thus not restricted to 18–60; (E6) the study uses rest/fixation as the only baseline/active control (category analysis compares task to rest) and does not include a within-participant contrast against an active control task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of executive function/planning task), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (task is planning, an executive function), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition). Therefore exclude.

The study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this executive-function meta-analysis. Specifically, although it is an fMRI study that reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and provides participant demographics and task details (satisfying I5, I7, I8, and I10), it does not include a within-participant contrast of an executive-function task versus an active control designed to isolate executive processes (I6 not met). Additionally, the task is a visual imagery vs perception paradigm and, while the authors discuss cognitive control involvement, the task does not clearly fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) as required by I9. Therefore it is not eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain, with clear task paradigm and participant ages reported (means ~34.3 and 37.7 years). It reports within-participant contrasts (1-back>0-back, 2-back>0-back, 2-back>1-back) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (FSL/FLAME; Z-stat images, cluster correction) for both MDD patients and healthy control subjects. Healthy within-group activation maps are described (controls show frontal activation in contrasts), and results are reported in text/figures/tables. The baseline (0-back) is an active control condition. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-group healthy maps, and participants are within the adult age range. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adult participants (ages 20–29), reporting within-subject contrasts of working memory task versus an active control task and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effect analysis in Experiment 2 and fixed-effect in Experiment 1). Whole-brain results are reported with coordinates and figures. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group patient contrasts, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 21–31) that manipulates working memory load (two-back vs one-back) and reports neural activations. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing the high working memory load (two-back) to the low-demand baseline (one-back), meeting the requirement for an executive-function task contrast. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (coordinates and activations in prefrontal cortex and precuneus) in addition to ROI analyses, satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion. The working memory manipulation falls clearly within an established executive function domain. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, out-of-range participants) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults, reporting within-subject contrasts (structured vs unstructured sequences) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected) with peak coordinates. Participant ages for imaging (21–34) are within 18–60 and sample health is reported. Imaging modality, task paradigm, and relevant methodological details are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

While the manuscript reports task-based fMRI of an executive function task (Stroop) with within-subject incongruent vs congruent contrasts and whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy control participants, it must be excluded because the study sample is not restricted to healthy adults and includes clinical (bipolar) participants and includes participant ages up to 65 (outside the 18–60 range), violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive/cognitive task), I6 (within-participant contrast: Stroop incongruent vs congruent), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function—inhibition), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: []. Exclusion criteria applied: E8 (study includes non-healthy participants and participants outside age 18–60). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results and discussion. Therefore EXCLUDED based on E8 despite meeting the executive-function task and reporting requirements.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults performing mental addition/subtraction of fractions with an active control condition (numbers without operators). It includes within-participant contrasts (math vs control), group-level voxelwise random-effects whole-brain analyses (activation maps and Talairach coordinates), and reports participant age statistics, healthy sample status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. The task includes a clear working-memory and cognitive-control component (semantic working memory/conflict resolution discussed), fitting an executive-function domain. No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not connectivity/resting-state only, include within-subject contrasts, and use an active control. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures/tables). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a counting Stroop (inhibition/response-conflict) task with an active nonlinguistic control. The paper reports within-participant Stroop versus control contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation results (clusters, corrected thresholds), and includes methods, results, and discussion. Participant sample is described as healthy young adults; imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The article reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in healthy adults (male, age 18–43). It includes within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 0-back), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects), and reports results in tables/figures/coordinates. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task activation, uses an active 0-back control, is empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults with within-subject contrasts and participant details reported (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, all group-level inferential analyses are ROI-based (caudate, DLPFC, M1, PPC) and the manuscript does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinate tables/figures that would allow inclusion. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain group results (I7) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criteria E8 and E6. E8: participants include ages 50–65, thus include individuals older than the allowed 18–60 range. E6: the primary task contrasts are reported relative to a resting/fixation baseline (rest circle) rather than an active control condition; no within-participant contrast against an active control condition is provided. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — 2-back working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain SPM analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates described), I9 (task is working memory, an executive domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast versus an active control). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (verbal n-back) in healthy adults (mean age 21.8) that reports within-participant contrasts using an active control (0-back) and parametric contrasts (e.g., 2B>1B). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (P<0.001 uncorrected) with activation coordinates and figures. Participant health and imaging modality are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active control, empirical, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (an executive function) with within-participant BOLD contrasts and cortex-wide (vertex/whole-brain) activation maps reported in figures, and reports imaging modality and task paradigm. However, the provided full text does not report participant age or explicitly confirm healthy sample status, so inclusion criterion I10 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered based on the available information. Therefore the study must be excluded because not ALL inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study is excluded because it includes clinical (severe TBI) participants and is not restricted to healthy individuals (Exclusion E8). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory — an executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts reported, e.g., 2>0 and 3>0 back), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results described with anatomical labels/coordinates), I9 (task falls within executive domain — working memory), I10 (reports imaging modality, task paradigm, and confirms healthy control sample). Inclusion criteria not met: none of the I5–I10 criteria are lacking in principle. However, because the study sample includes patients (i.e., is not restricted to healthy adults), it violates exclusion criterion E8 and must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study (3T BOLD) of working memory using an N-back paradigm (executive function domain: working memory) in healthy adults (n=26, mean age 21.2). The design includes within-participant contrasts (parametric linear increase in load: 0-back/1-back/2-back), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM5 with coordinates reported, and behavioral/performance covariates. 0-back serves as an active baseline and the analyses examine task-evoked activation maps (reported thresholds and tables). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-state, empirical with original human fMRI data, participants 18–60 and healthy). Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied.

This is an event-related fMRI study of proactive motor inhibition (an executive function: inhibition) in healthy adults (ages 23–37). It includes within-subject contrasts (e.g., mixed-block no-cue vs cued; SOA100 vs SOA500) and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses implemented in SPM2 with coordinates and thresholding reported in tables/figures. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, empirical human neuroimaging data within 18–60, includes within-participant task contrasts). Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present). Consequently, all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of attentional control (Simon and spatial Stroop), which falls under executive function/cognitive control. It reports within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) for both tasks and conducts group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunction, disjunction, and direct contrasts) with tables/figures of activations. Participant age range (24–40), healthy status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (ages 18–32). It uses task-based within-subject contrasts (IS, DS, NI, PV; contrasts such as IS vs PV, IS vs DS), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and whole-brain connectivity maps, and provides participant demographics, imaging modality, and task paradigm details. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-baseline-only, not non-empirical, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy).

This is a task-based fMRI study of contextual inhibition (an executive function domain: response inhibition) in healthy adults (mean age 28.5). The study reports within-subject contrasts (INH and ACT compared with REST and directly with each other), conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (conjunction and contrast analyses) with corrected P-values and tables/figures, and provides participant, imaging modality, and task details. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an inhibition (Go/Nogo) paradigm (an established executive function domain). Within-subject contrasts were modeled and reported (Nogo–Go; Go/Cue–Go/Noncue; Cued-Nogo–Uncued-Nogo), and group-level voxelwise analyses with whole-brain cluster correction were performed and reported in tables and figures (coordinates provided). Healthy control participants are described and screened; demographic and task details (modality fMRI, task paradigm, age matching) are reported. The task uses active go trials as control rather than rest. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, not resting-state only, empirical human fMRI data, healthy adult sample present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it includes clinical (OCD) participants and is not restricted to healthy adults (exclusion E8). The article otherwise meets multiple inclusion requirements: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function—N-back working memory), I6 (within-participant 2-back vs 0-back contrast), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with reported clusters), I8 (results reported in tables/coordinates and text), I9 (working memory is an established executive function), and I10 (participant ages, healthy-control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). However, because the sample includes patients (OCD) and is not restricted to healthy adults, it violates E8 and must be excluded from a meta-analysis of healthy adult executive-function activations.

The study uses fMRI and an n-back working memory task (executive function) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and sufficient participant/task details. However, the experimental contrast compares task ON periods to rest (eyes open) OFF periods rather than to an active control condition. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control) and it violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control task). Summary: exclusion IDs met: E6; inclusion IDs met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10; inclusion ID not met: I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Stroop inhibition paradigms in healthy adults (mean age 23.3) that meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI (3T), presents within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; congruent vs neutral) with an active control (row of X's), and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with stereotactic coordinates and tables. Participant health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully reported, and the full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-groups-only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back), an executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts between conditions (e.g., Binding vs Sign and Speech; 2Binding > Sign + Speech), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM2 with FDR-corrected maps and tables/figures, and provides participant demographics (healthy hearing native signers, mean age 35). The paradigm, imaging modality (fMRI), and results meet the meta-analysis requirements for task activations in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy participants) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (Stroop inhibition/conflict), with healthy adult participants (mean age 26.5). It reports within-subject contrasts of task conditions (moderate/high conflict vs low conflict and incongruent vs congruent), and performs group-level random-effects voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain contrasts and reported coordinate tables/figures). Participant demographics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. EEG connectivity is additional but does not replace task activation reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active task contrasts, is empirical, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement that the task be an established executive function paradigm (I9). While it uses fMRI and probes cognitive control aspects of deception, the primary paradigm is episodic recognition memory with instructions to feign impairment rather than a canonical executive function task (e.g., working memory N-back, inhibition/Go–NoGo). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level, whole-brain SnPM paired t-test maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures and clearly described), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not explicitly assess an executive function or cognitive-control task as defined by the review), I6 (no within-participant contrast of a defined executive function task vs an active control as required), and I9 (task does not clearly fall within established executive function domains). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-baseline-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study uses an n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain) with within-participant contrasts against an active 0-back baseline, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and cluster coordinates (including trends analysis in the healthy control group), and provides participant age information, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm. The healthy control group’s within-group whole-brain results are reported (coordinates, clusters, figures), meeting the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of executive-function (set-shifting/planning) using the Montreal Card-Sorting Task and provides within-subject contrasts against an active control condition (e.g., retrieval without shift vs control; continuous shift vs control). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (statistical maps thresholding described; peaks/tables and figures provided). The healthy control group activations are presented separately (within-group results and inter-group comparisons), and participant age, healthy-status screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. Although the study also includes Parkinson’s patients, the presence of clearly reported healthy control within-group whole-brain activations makes it eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a go–nogo task (inhibition = executive function) with healthy control participants. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (NOGO vs GO and hand-specific contrasts) and random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses in healthy controls, with results reported as coordinates and figures. Imaging modality, task paradigm, and confirmation of healthy control status are described. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with whole-brain group maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants only) are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (Stroop task and syntactic ambiguity requiring conflict resolution) in healthy adults (n=17, ages 18.5–34.5). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs neutral Stroop; S3–S1 syntactic contrast) and conducts group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported coordinates and figures (Tables 2–3, Figures 3–4). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are described. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (inhibition) using a modified Stroop task. It reports within-subject contrasts (interference minus color naming), group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects SPM maps for both healthy controls and marijuana smokers, and presents coordinate/figure results. Participant ages (18–47), healthy control characterization, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are all described. Active control conditions (color naming/word reading) were used rather than fixation alone. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, within-group healthy control activations are reported, and the full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study satisfies I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and is eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive-function activations in healthy adults.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (fMRI verbal working memory task — executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast: memory vs control), I7 (group-level whole-brain GLM reported and thresholded), I8 (ROIs and coordinates reported), I9 (task is working memory). Inclusion IDs not met: I10 (participant age information not reported in the full text; although healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm are described, ages or age range/mean are not provided). Therefore the study fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (I10 missing) and must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults. It is an empirical fMRI study employing task-based paradigms assessing executive functions (PRLT for cognitive flexibility/reversal learning and Tower of London for planning) (I5, I9). Within-subject contrasts versus active baseline conditions are reported (monetary gain/loss vs neutral baseline for PRLT; planning vs baseline and parametric difficulty contrasts for ToL) (I6). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are performed and reported (FDR-corrected maps, group ANOVAs, interaction maps), with results shown in figures and tables of activations/coordinates (I7, I8). Participant information and sample characterization (healthy control group, exclusion criteria, imaging modality, and task paradigms) are described in the methods and demographics (I10). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, absence of within-group task activations in healthy participants, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are violated. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This task-based fMRI study uses a working memory (Sternberg) paradigm (executive function domain) with within-participant contrasts (five digits vs arrows baseline). Group-level voxelwise activation analyses were performed (activated voxels identified with pairwise t tests and thresholding), and results for the healthy (normal) participant group are reported. The paper reports participant ages, confirmation of a healthy control group, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details. Although the study also includes a schizophrenia group, the healthy control within-group whole-brain activation is present and usable for meta-analysis of executive function in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–32) using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test to probe cognitive flexibility (an executive function). The authors report within-subject contrasts of shift events versus ordinary correct (active) trials, perform group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and report peak coordinates and statistical maps/figures. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state baseline only, and sample is healthy and age-appropriate). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory that reports within-subject 2-back vs 0-back contrasts and whole-brain, group-level activation maps for both controls and patients. However, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (it includes a clinical group of never-medicated adult ADHD patients alongside healthy controls). This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrast against active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (working memory task within executive domains), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, task described). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 are satisfied). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI experiment of working memory (n-back) in healthy adults and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and coordinate tables. It therefore meets I5 (fMRI of executive function task), I7 (group-level whole-brain maps), I8 (results reported as tables/figures), I9 (working memory is an executive domain), and I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm described). However, the study does not include an active control condition contrast (e.g., 0-back or other non-executive active control). The analyses reported contrast task blocks to rest and compare within-subject task performance across chewing conditions ([Before] vs [After]), which uses rest or fixation as baseline and lacks an appropriate active control contrast. This violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation only baseline without an active control), and means inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast of executive task relative to an active control) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures, tables). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (n-back), a canonical executive function. It includes within-participant contrasts (2-back > 0-back, 1-back > 0-back) using an active 0-back control, and reports second-level random-effects analyses with whole-brain corrected main task effects (FWE) and voxelwise results described in tables/figures. Participant details (healthy adults, mean age 27.4), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation, active baseline used, empirical human data, healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI, task-based, whole-brain study of response inhibition (SART) comparing adults and young adolescents. It meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI executive-function task), I6 (within-participant contrasts: successful inhibitions and commission errors vs Go-trial baseline), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (results reported in maps/tables), I9 (inhibition is an executive function), and I10 (reports ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task). However, it includes participants aged 10–14 (minors) in addition to adults, thus violating exclusion criterion E8 (includes participants outside the 18–60 years range). Although adult-only maps are reported, the study sample is not restricted to healthy adults 18–60, so it must be excluded per E8.

The paper is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (Stroop and oddball tasks) in healthy adults (mean age ~25.7). It reports within-subject contrasts of executive tasks vs active control conditions (Stroop-incongruency vs Stroop-congruency; Word- and Color-oddball vs Oddball control). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with coordinate tables and figures (p<.005, uncorrected). Participant details, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not rest-only baseline, empirical with healthy adults 18–60). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, references).

This empirical study used task-based fMRI in healthy adults performing the Conners' Continuous Performance Test (a vigilance/inhibition executive task). The authors report within-subject contrasts (task blocks vs baseline/active control of meaningless images) and group-level voxelwise analyses (one-way ANOVA producing whole-brain t-maps and cluster-level activations). Participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, baseline is active images rather than fixation-only, empirical data in healthy 18–60 y/o). Although sample size is small (n=8), this does not conflict with the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study should be excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: participants include ages 22–76, i.e., participants older than 60 are included. The study otherwise meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function via an n-back working memory task), I6 (within-participant contrast: 2-back vs 0-back active control), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with random-effects maps), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and figures), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), and I10 (participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion is based solely on participant age range exceeding 18–60.

Excluded per E4: the study reports fMRI analyses but does not present a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map. It reports ROI-restricted activation analyses in the anterior cingulate and reports whole-brain psychophysiological interaction (functional connectivity) results, but no whole-brain task activation contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study using a task involving cognitive control/inhibition—emotional Stroop), I6 (within-participant contrast: positive vs neutral words), I9 (task falls within cognitive control/inhibition domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, fMRI modality, and task described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore excluded under E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an executive function domain. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (Go/NoGo vs Go) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses for healthy controls and patients, with multiple-comparison correction and Talairach coordinates/tables/figures. Participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, within-group healthy activation maps are provided). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of Stroop interference (executive function/cognitive control) in healthy adults (mean age ~25.7). It reports within-subject contrasts of task conditions (RI vs CO, RI vs SI, SI vs CO, CO vs SU) and performs group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables of coordinates and figures. The task (size-Stroop) falls within inhibition/conflict domains of executive function. Participant demographics, imaging modality, methods, results, and discussion are fully reported in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest baseline only, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range ages) are met.

Full-text reviewed. Exclusion rationale: No exclusion criteria directly met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrasts: duration vs control tasks), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures), I10 (healthy adult sample with ages reported and fMRI modality and task details). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (study does not assess an established executive function or cognitive control task — it investigates duration/time perception), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Because the study’s task domain (temporal perception/duration discrimination) is outside the meta-analysis scope of executive function task activations, the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes children (6- and 10-year-olds) in addition to adults, so participants are not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — working memory CN-BT), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures and clearly described), I9 (task falls within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (participant ages, healthy sample screening, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast against an independent active control condition; the reported contrast is correct n-back responses vs. baseline/non-target trials, which does not fulfill the specified active-control requirement). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps and reported coordinates in healthy adults (meets I7, I8, I10). However, the task is voluntary breath holding (inhibition of respiration) rather than a standard executive-function task paradigm; the manuscript does not present a within-participant contrast of the executive/cognitive control task against an active control condition. Breath-hold events were modeled against resting/ongoing breathing and CO2 was included as a nuisance regressor rather than serving as an active control contrast. Therefore it fails I5 (clear task-based executive function paradigm), I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control), and I9 (task clearly within established executive-function inhibition paradigms). It thus violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation or passive baseline used rather than an active control). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–24) examining cognitive control/mindset implementation during an anagram task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (each abstraction condition vs. the other two) and group-level voxelwise analyses with reported statistical parametric maps and coordinate foci. Whole-brain analysis procedures are described; results are reported as figures and tables of peak coordinates. Participant demographic and health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. Although the authors used anatomically defined a priori ROIs for corrected inference in lateral PFC, whole-brain (gray-matter) thresholds and voxelwise group analyses were also performed and coordinates/figures are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI Stroop task study that reports within-subject interference vs facilitation contrasts, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM), and provides coordinates and healthy control within-group activation maps. However, the sample includes participants aged 16–45 (controls and patients), i.e., participants under 18, and the study includes clinical (schizophrenia) participants rather than being restricted to healthy adults. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (participants outside the 18–60 range or not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study is excluded from a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

This fMRI study uses a Stroop color-word interference task (an executive/inhibition task), reports within-subject incongruent vs congruent contrasts, provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/figures, and reports participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, it includes participants aged 47–72 yrs (range includes >60 years), which violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the 18–60 age range). No inclusion criteria are unmet. Because E8 is triggered, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite satisfying the other inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an executive function, in healthy adults (11 male never-smokers, ages 20–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses (zero-order and first-order/parametric load effects) with voxelwise correction (P<0.05) and presents coordinates/tables and figures of activations. The task paradigm and imaging modality (fMRI) and participant demographics/health are clearly reported. Within-participant contrasts across working memory loads (parametric/first-order effects and load-specific 0/1/2/3-back vs rest maps) provide task-evoked activation maps suitable for meta-analysis of executive function. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy participants) are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=20, aged 22–30) including an n-back working memory task (an executive function). It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., 1+2-back vs 0-back) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps thresholded at p=0.05 FWE (figures and cluster results reported). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are described. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results present; not a connectivity-only or between-group-only study; active control used for n-back; healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.
