Imaging modality, participant health/handedness, ages, and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy sample). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory in human participants. The study reports within-participant contrasts comparing memory trials to matched control trials (active control with similar stimuli and motor responses), uses a voxelwise GLM and reports whole-brain activations in figures and coordinate tables, and the task falls squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). Imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. While participant demographics (exact ages and explicit statement of healthy status) are not shown in the provided excerpt, the full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and refers to human participants; therefore inclusion is judged appropriate with moderate confidence.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes within-subject contrasts of an executive/ cognitive-control task (the distraction condition involving holding a six-letter string; a working-memory manipulation) versus an active attend/look condition. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM2, AlphaSim correction) with coordinates/tables and figures. Participants’ age (mean 24.4), healthy-sample screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. The task (distraction) falls within the working memory/executive function domain. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses an active baseline (look), is empirical with original human neuroimaging data, and includes healthy participants aged 18–60. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Although this fMRI study reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and provides full methodological detail, it does not test an established executive function task domain. Met criteria I7, I8 and I10 are satisfied (whole-brain voxelwise analyses, clearly reported maps/coordinates, and adequate participant/imaging/task details). However, it fails to meet key inclusion requirements: I5 (the study’s primary aim is to characterize synesthetic perception, not to assess an executive-function task or cognitive-control paradigm per se), I6 (there is no within-participant contrast that isolates a predefined executive-function task versus an active control designed to probe EF), and I9 (the tasks do not fall within standard EF domains such as working memory, inhibition, set-shifting, planning, vigilance, or initiation; the DLPFC activation reflects incidental conflict in a perceptual task rather than an a priori EF manipulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (n=17, mean age 25.7). It reports within-subject two-back WM versus 0-back reference contrasts (active control), group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM99 with thresholded maps and tables/figures (conjunction and cognitive-subtraction results). Participant health, age, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports task-based fMRI (N-back working memory) in healthy adult participants using a within-participant 2-back vs 0-back contrast, with group-level voxelwise analyses in SPM99 and coordinates/vouchered loci reported for prefrontal activation. Participant characteristics (adults 18–60, healthy controls/subgroup matched for age, handedness, IQ) and imaging modality/task paradigm are described. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (coordinates/figures reported), I9 (working memory = executive domain), and I10 (participant age/healthy status/imaging modality/task reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group healthy activation contrast, uses active control). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an fMRI Stroop (inhibition) task in OCD patients and healthy controls, with task vs active control contrasts and voxelwise random-effects group analyses. However, for the meta-analysis target (healthy adult executive-function activations), the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts (patients vs controls) and pre/post patient maps; it does not present a standalone group-level, whole-brain task-activation map for the healthy control group in the text/tables provided. Therefore it fails the requirement that healthy-participant within-group whole-brain activation maps be available (exclusion E5). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (within-participant task vs active-control contrasts were computed), I8 (results reported via tables/figures/coordinates), I9 (task falls within executive domain: inhibition), I10 (participant demographics, healthy-control status, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met (for the purposes of this review): I7 as applied to healthy participants (no reported group-level whole-brain within-group activation map for controls). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive processes (letter vs visuospatial decision tasks) in healthy adult volunteers. It reports within-subject contrasts (letter vs visuospatial; tasks vs baseline) using an active control baseline (simple reaction-time task), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and corrected statistics. Tasks probe executive functions (response selection, inhibition, conflict monitoring). Participant sample is described as healthy right-handed volunteers (n=16); imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigms are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of executive function with within-participant contrasts and whole-brain maps.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI (I5) to examine working-memory processes (an executive function domain, I9); includes within-participant contrasts between active task conditions (l/r vs b/n and l/r vs d/n; I6); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 with random-effects inference and reports coordinate tables and activation figures (I7, I8); and provides participant age range, healthy status, modality, and task paradigm details (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity- or resting-state-only (E4), not between-group-only (E5), and an active control task contrast is present so baseline-only exclusion (E6) does not apply; participants are healthy adults within 18–60 so E8 is not violated. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion so is sufficiently complete.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 24.6) that directly probes working memory and recognition processes (an executive function domain). The within-subject contrasts include game > dot (a working-memory vs. perceptual-motor active control), game > scene, and game > random. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (fixed-effects) were performed and significant clusters are reported (tables/figures and coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Participant, imaging modality, and task details are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to this meta-analysis are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical fMRI study (I5) using task-based paradigms targeting working memory/attention (executive function domain; I9). The analyses include within-participant contrasts across task conditions/set sizes (e.g., ns < nm, nm > nl) at the group level (I6). Whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses are reported with cluster-level correction and tables/figures/coordinates (I7, I8). Participant characteristics (age range, mean ages), confirmation of healthy sample, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigms/methods are provided (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper includes whole-brain activation results (not ROI-only), is not a connectivity-only or between-group-only study, uses active task contrasts (not just rest/fixation baseline), is empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults within 18–60, and is not a review/simulation. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling extraction of required data. Therefore this study should be INCLUDED.

This study must be excluded because it includes both healthy controls and schizophrenia patients and therefore is not restricted to healthy individuals (exclusion E8). The paper is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-subject GLM contrast images (Sternberg working memory probe/encode, auditory oddball, sensorimotor), performs whole-brain group-level analyses and reports spatial maps and coordinates. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function—working memory), I6 (within-participant GLM contrasts/contrast images), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results reported as figures/tables/coordinates), I9 (includes working memory task), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status for controls, imaging modality and task paradigms). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, within-subject event-related fMRI study of cued task switching (executive function/cognitive control). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and tables/figures of activation foci (coordinates). It includes within-participant contrasts (advance target vs. advance cue and congruency contrasts) that are task-based contrasts between active conditions. Participant age range, healthy status, imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), and full task methods are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations, healthy adults 20–29). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI, whole-brain, task-based study in healthy adults that reports group-level voxelwise results (meets I7, I8, I10). However, the paradigm investigates smooth pursuit eye movements (sensorimotor/motion processing) rather than a canonical executive function/cognitive control task. Although the authors discuss working memory, attention, and monitoring components, the primary task does not fall clearly within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails I5 and I9. The within-participant contrasts are comparisons of pursuit/blanking conditions rather than an executive-task vs active control contrast per the review definition, so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is an fMRI task-based study of verbal working memory (an executive function). It uses within-subject contrasts of maintenance versus an active case-judgment control, reports group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects t maps and coordinates) and functional connectivity, and provides participant demographics (11 healthy adults, mean age 21.4). Thus it satisfies I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control, empirical fMRI study with healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that includes within-subject, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts that probe cognitive control/executive processes during an empathy/perspective-taking task. Although the primary topic is empathy for pain, the authors explicitly test and interpret contrasts (e.g., No Pain: Dissimilar > Similar) in terms of executive functions such as response inhibition and self–other distinction (rIFC, dmPFC), and perform whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported coordinate tables. Participant age and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active task controls, empirical data in healthy 19–34 year-olds). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion of executive-function-related task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive working memory (dual-task WM span) in healthy adults. It reports within-subject contrasts of the executive dual-task (Read+Remember) versus active component tasks (Read, Remember), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM and coordinates/tables/figures of activations. Participant ages and healthy status are provided (18–31 yrs, right-handed volunteers). Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigms, methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=21, ages 20–26) using modified Wisconsin Card Sorting Test set-shifting paradigms that probe cognitive flexibility/executive control. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., A minus D, A minus B, B minus C) and group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with thresholding and peak coordinates reported (Table 1 and figures). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are described. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baselines, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy participants). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study that includes an executive task (Stroop) and reports group-level ICA maps of the default mode network, but it does not provide a within-participant, whole-brain task activation contrast isolating executive function (e.g., incongruent>congruent Stroop) relative to an active control. The paper’s primary analyses are connectivity/ICA-based and resting/task-modulation of the default mode network rather than standard voxelwise task-evoked activation maps for executive-control contrasts. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-focused without an appropriate whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task including an executive paradigm), I8 (coordinates/tables reported), I9 (task falls within executive domain — Stroop), I10 (participant/sample and imaging details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive task vs an active control condition isolating executive demands), I7 (no conventional group-level voxelwise task activation map for an executive-control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, ages 19–28) using task-based paradigms addressing executive/cognitive control (Stroop for conflict/inhibition; time-estimation for performance monitoring). The paper reports within-subject GLM contrasts (incongruent>congruent; errors>correct; correct feedback>error feedback) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with stereotactic coordinates, tables, and figures (p<.005, contiguity threshold). Participant health, age range, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (n=19, ages 22–34). It reports within-participant contrasts of load (5 vs 3 items) using a low-load active control, a delayed match-to-sample working memory task. Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM2) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates/tables/figures reported. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete.

This study must be excluded because it includes participants outside the eligible age range (13-year-old children in addition to adults), meeting exclusion criterion E8. The study otherwise satisfies the inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — visuospatial working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts comparing WM events to control trials), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected results and reported coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and text), I9 (task falls within executive function — working memory), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely due to E8.

This fMRI study examines attentional modulation (selective attention/vigilance) during an active task, which falls within executive function domains. It includes a within-participant contrast (attend vs. ignore prepulse), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM maps and coordinate tables), and provides participant/sample details, imaging modality, and task paradigm. The paper contains full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only without within-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of language switching that directly tests cognitive control/executive function (language switching vs single-language naming). It reports within-subject contrasts (mixed/alternating vs blocked single-language) using group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM2 analyses with tables/figures describing activation loci (DLPFC, ACC, parietal, etc.). Participants are healthy adults (mean age 21.4), imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm (covert picture naming with mixed/blocked conditions) are clearly reported. The switching task falls within established executive domains (cognitive flexibility/inhibitory control). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, within-group contrasts present, active control condition used, healthy adult sample 18–60). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults assessing attention/alertness (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains. It reports within-subject contrasts between two active task conditions (distributed vs focused spatial attention) and performs whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level random effects) with coordinates/tables and figures. Participant age range and health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline without active task, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory/reference-frame shifts (executive function domain: working memory). It reports within-subject contrasts (AlloSpace vs EgoSpace; Space vs NonSpace) and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with FDR correction; results are reported as coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (n=21, mean age ~22), imaging modality is fMRI, and experimental methods, results, and discussion are fully present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active control conditions, empirical, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates/figures (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the reported contrasts are task phases versus an implicit/rest baseline (blank “relax” trials were unmodeled), and there is no within-participant contrast against an active control condition. The review’s I6 requires an active-control within-participant contrast, and E6 excludes studies that use rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control task. Therefore I6 is not met and E6 applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Excluded on the basis of lacking an active control contrast (E6); included criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10; inclusion criterion not met: I6.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults using a GO–NOGO paradigm that probes response inhibition (an established executive function). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (NOGO vs GO) and whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with thresholded statistical maps and coordinate tables/figures. Participants’ ages and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are all reported. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Recommended for inclusion in meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an event-related fMRI study of healthy adults explicitly probing planning and online control of motor sequences (planning is an executive function). It uses within-subject task contrasts (IG vs EG; complex vs simple; premovement vs movement) rather than rest-only baselines, and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with coordinates and figures (voxel-wise ANOVAs, cluster thresholds, Table 1, whole-brain ROIs). Participant demographics (n=26; ages 19–50; healthy status) and imaging modality (fMRI) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active task contrasts, is empirical with original human fMRI data, and includes healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This PET study of the PASAT in healthy adults meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function activation meta-analysis. It uses task-based PET imaging assessing executive processes (working memory/attention) (I5), includes within-participant contrasts of the executive task versus active control tasks (PASAT–repeat immediate, PASAT–repeat prior; I6), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with coordinates and corrected p-values (I7, I8). The task falls within established executive domains (working memory/attention; I9). The paper reports participant ages, confirms a healthy sample, specifies imaging modality (PET), and details the task paradigm (I10). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided and appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (mental arithmetic) in healthy adults, with within-subject contrasts against an active control (zero trials). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level SPM analyses with coordinates and figures, and provides full participant demographics (N=20, ages 20.3–39.6, healthy) and task details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic that explicitly discusses working memory involvement (an executive function). It uses within-subject contrasts (complex vs. simple calculation) with simple calculation as an active control (not fixation), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with FDR-corrected results and Talairach coordinates presented in tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults (ages 22–40), imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting baseline only, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Although the study uses fMRI, a within-participant task vs active control contrast, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, and tests a healthy adult sample with ages reported, the experimental task (Word Memory Test delayed recognition) is an episodic/declarative memory retrieval task rather than an executive function or cognitive-control task as required (I9). Therefore it does not meet the key inclusion criterion that tasks fall within established executive function domains. Full text is complete and exclusion criteria E3–E8 do not apply. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task not clearly assessing executive function/cognitive control), I9 (task not within listed executive-function domains). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This is an empirical PET study of spatial working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. It uses task-based within-subject contrasts (spatial span and spatial manipulation vs matched visuomotor control) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM96 with whole-brain exploratory searches and stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1, figures). Participants are healthy right-handed adults aged 44–55. Imaging modality (PET), task paradigms, participant details, and statistical whole-brain results (coordinates and mapped images) are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults using an n-back working memory paradigm (executive function). It includes within-participant contrasts (2-back identity vs passive; identity vs location), and reports group-level, whole-brain volume- and surface-based statistical maps (voxelwise group analyses and Talairach coordinates/figures). Participant demographics (age 19–47, healthy), imaging modality (fMRI, 3T/4T), and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, active control present, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This study used fMRI in healthy adult samples and analyzed task data (including 3-back working memory) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps, and reports results clearly — satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the presented analyses focus on trial-by-trial RT regressors and task-vs-fixation contrasts (fixation baseline), and I find no within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition (e.g., 3-back vs 0-back or another active control). Therefore I6 is not met. Because the study appears to use fixation/rest as the baseline for task-related contrasts without reporting an active control contrast, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDED for failing to meet I6 (and triggering E6).

The study is excluded because it includes non-healthy participants (patients with schizophrenia are part of the sample) and therefore is not restricted to healthy adults (exclusion E8). Also, the task contrasts use fixation/baseline (rest) as the baseline/control rather than an active control condition, violating the requirement for an active within-participant control (exclusion E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I7 (group-level composite t-maps/whole-brain maps were computed), I8 (whole-brain results are described in the text/figures), I9 (working memory is an established executive function domain), and I10 (participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast vs an active control condition). Given these violations, the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study of attentional control (Stroop-like interference) in healthy adults (ages 18–30). It includes within-subject contrasts (interference vs control blocks), group-level random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with coordinates/tables, and full methodological/participant details (imaging modality, task paradigm, healthy sample). The task clearly falls within executive function (inhibition/attentional control). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults using a go–nogo paradigm (response inhibition), meeting the executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts (nogo vs go) and group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (conjunction and interaction), with coordinates and statistical maps described in text and figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task details are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, active control present, empirical human imaging in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion).

Exclusion rationale: (a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the primary analyses are restricted to a priori ROI/small-volume tests rather than reporting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map) and E8 (the sample includes adolescents below 18 years; participants are a mixed-age sample including ages 9–17 and adults, so the study includes participants outside the required 18–60 age range). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI examining cognitive control/decision-making), I6 (within-subject contrasts of task conditions, e.g., risky vs safe selections and inclusion of an active control wheel), I8 (results reported with coordinates and described in text), I9 (task engages cognitive control/conflict monitoring processes relevant to executive function), and I10 (participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task details are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported; analyses were confined to ROIs/SV-corrected spheres). Given violation of E3 and E8, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E8 — the study includes clinical participants (bipolar disorder) and is not restricted to healthy individuals, despite inclusion of a healthy control group. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI Stroop, an executive/inhibition task), I6 (within-participant contrast: incongruent vs congruent trials), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain composite maps and voxelwise t-statistics reported), I8 (results reported in figures and described in text), I9 (Stroop falls within inhibition/executive function), I10 (participant ages and healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: none – all applicable inclusion criteria were satisfied for the control-task activation. However, because E8 applies, the study must be excluded per the protocol (it is not restricted to healthy adults). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of attentional control (a form of executive function/cognitive control) in healthy adults (ages 19–45). The authors report within-participant contrasts (shift color/location vs hold) and perform group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunction and searchlight MVPC) with cluster correction. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly described. The task probes cognitive control (shifting attention/cognitive flexibility), and results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level, within-subject contrasts and provides participant demographics and imaging details, it does not examine a task that falls within the review's specified executive function domains. Met: I5 (fMRI task-based study addressing cognitive control/conflict), I6 (within-participant contrasts: Magic vs Causal Control; Surprise vs Causal Control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables and described), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, modality, and task paradigm reported). Not met: I9 — the paradigm involves perception of magic tricks and violations of causal expectation (a perceptual/reasoning paradigm probing disbelief/conflict detection) rather than established executive function tasks (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The authors interpret activations in terms of conflict/cognitive-control, but the task was not designed or categorized as a canonical executive function task. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (undergraduate sample, mean ages ~20–21) using a cognitive-control reappraisal paradigm. It reports within-subject contrasts (Reappraise > Negative and Negative > Reappraise) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR-corrected results and reported MNI coordinates. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and full task details are provided. The paradigm operationalizes cognitive control of emotion (reappraisal), fitting the meta-analysis objective of executive function/cognitive-control task activations. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active control conditions, healthy adults within 18–60, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete.

This is an empirical, within-subject fMRI study of a go–nogo paradigm (inhibition/conflict) in healthy adults (ages 19–60). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME, cluster thresholding) with coordinates and figures, and includes within-participant contrasts relevant to executive function (go vs nogo; compatibility and co-action vs single-actor interactions). Imaging modality, sample demographics/health, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active task baselines, empirical with original human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is not accessible (only a redirect/placeholder page shown), so core article content (methods, results) cannot be verified. Therefore I cannot confirm that the study meets the required inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (cannot verify). Inclusion IDs not met / not verifiable: I5 (cannot confirm it is an fMRI/PET task assessing executive function), I6 (cannot confirm within-participant contrast vs an active control), I7 (cannot confirm group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (cannot confirm coordinate/figure whole-brain reporting), I9 (cannot confirm tasks fall within defined executive domains), I10 (cannot confirm participant age range, healthy status, imaging modality and task paradigm). fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive function (Stroop attentional control/inhibition) in healthy adults (N=16, ages 18–30). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; incongruent-eligible vs incongruent-ineligible) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise ANOVA, Kolmogorov–Smirnov maps converted to Z-scores, and tables of Talairach coordinates). Participant demographics, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although the study meets all imaging and task-based inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) — it is a whole-brain fMRI study using an executive-domain (vigilance/RVIP) task with within-participant RVIP vs active control contrasts and reports voxelwise group maps and coordinates — it includes clinical participants (schizophrenia patients) and is not restricted to healthy adults. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria met: E8.

Although this study is a task-based fMRI investigation of sustained attention (vigilance) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in a healthy control sample, it does not include an active control condition for the required within-participant task vs active-control contrast. The task contrasts are reported primarily against a fixation baseline and practice (novel vs. practice) repetitions; therefore the study uses rest/fixation as the primary baseline rather than an active control. This violates exclusion criterion E6 and fails inclusion criterion I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive domain—vigilance), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables), I9 (task falls within executive function domain—vigilance), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-subject contrast against an active control).

This is an fMRI task study of executive function (working memory monitoring) in healthy adults (N=13, ages 19–27). It reports within-subject contrasts (self-ordered vs recognition; externally triggered vs recognition; self-ordered vs externally triggered). Analyses were performed as group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise statistical maps with thresholding and coordinates reported. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of working memory (N-back), an executive function task, in healthy adults. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., 2-back/4 vs 2-back/1 and conditions vs 0-back), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR correction, and presents whole-brain activation maps and cluster results in text/figures. Participant demographics (mean age 26.6, healthy screened) and imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, inappropriate sample age/health) are met. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext is complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly manipulates executive function (working memory load) and visuo-spatial attention using task-based paradigms. It includes within-participant contrasts of high vs low load (active control conditions) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise), with results reported in figures and tables. Participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an fMRI study of a canonical executive function (visual spatial working memory; n-back). It reports within-subject contrasts (2-back and 1-back relative to 0-back active control), and group-level voxelwise analyses identifying whole-brain activation clusters (right inferior frontal gyrus and intraparietal sulcus) derived from the 2-back vs 0-back contrast. Core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and participant details (nine healthy adults aged 26–32), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. Although a volume-of-interest analysis was used for effect-size extraction, the regions were first identified via a whole-brain second-level contrast. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in healthy adults (analyzed N=31, age 20–50). It reports within-subject contrasts (2-back > 0-back; verbal vs spatial) using a group-level mixed-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analysis with cluster-thresholded statistical maps and peak coordinates. Task falls within executive function (working memory). Participant, imaging modality, and paradigm details are reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of planning (autobiographical and visuospatial), which falls within executive function domains (planning). It reports within-subject contrasts of planning tasks relative to an active control (counting) and/or fixation, includes group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (PLS maps, tables of activation peaks, figures), and provides participant demographics confirming a healthy adult sample (ages 18–29). Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigms, and behavioral results are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only report, not only connectivity/resting analyses, not between-group only, not non-empirical, and participants are within the 18–60 healthy range). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI, task-based study of directed forgetting that explicitly probes intentional inhibition/cognitive control. It includes within-subject contrasts of Forget versus Remember instructions (F > R and related F_F > R_F contrasts), reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables of coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The task targets inhibitory/ executive control processes (memory suppression), and participant information (healthy adults, mean age ~27), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed paradigm are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range ages) are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a reversal learning task (cognitive flexibility/affective switching), an executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts of task events versus an affectively neutral active baseline (e.g., CR > BL, FRE > BL) and second-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and tables. Participant details are provided (healthy adults, mean age 32, range 22–53), imaging modality and task paradigm are described, and methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. The active baseline is not simple rest/fixation. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This study is an fMRI investigation of creative idea generation (alternative uses, name invention, object characteristics, word endings) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (FWE-corrected) and detailed participant information. However, the meta-analysis requires studies to assess executive function/cognitive control tasks within established EF domains. The present tasks are creativity-focused and, although the authors discuss working memory and selection/inhibition processes, the paradigms are not standard executive function tasks (e.g., n-back, go/no-go, task-switching) and the contrasts are not explicitly framed as EF vs active control. Therefore I5 (study assesses executive function) and I9 (tasks fall within established EF domains) are not met; I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive task vs active control) is not met for the same reason. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I7 (group-level whole-brain maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported), I10 (participant age/health/imaging/task described). No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 apply. Conclusion: exclude because key inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I9 are not satisfied.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: participants are outside the review's targeted age range (sample are healthy older adults mean age 63, all >55). The study otherwise meets the inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive inhibition), I6 (within-participant incongruent vs congruent contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and text), I9 (task falls under inhibition executive domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). No inclusion criteria are unmet, but exclusion E8 takes precedence. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of visuo-spatial working memory in healthy adults, meeting inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts between task conditions), I9 (working memory domain), and I10 (reported participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task). However, the study did not acquire or report group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps: scans were limited to parieto-frontal coverage for 12 subjects and occipito-temporo-frontal coverage for 6 subjects (no whole-brain acquisition), so I7 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Therefore exclusion criterion E3 applies (no whole-brain results / only limited-coverage/ROI-style reporting). For these reasons the paper should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (age 19–33) examining working memory manipulation (an executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (manipulation cue vs retrieval cue) and other within-participant contrasts. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cue minus maintenance contrast reported at p<0.05 FDR and shown in figures) and provides coordinates and descriptions of results. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study violates exclusion criteria E6 and E8. E6: the fMRI contrasts are reported relative to a resting/fixation baseline (21 s fixation blocks) and no active control task condition is used; the main contrasts and ROI analyses compare task to baseline rather than to an active control. E8: the healthy control sample is elderly (mean age 69.1 years), outside the required 18–60 age range for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: 2-back working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain/voxelwise maps are reported and shown in figures), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and illustrated), I9 (task falls within executive domains: working memory), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition). Because E6 and E8 are violated, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study investigates sentence comprehension and memory encoding (passive listening to narratives) rather than executive function or cognitive control tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/tabled/figured), I10 (participant age and healthy sample and imaging modality reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (does not assess executive function or cognitive control task-based paradigms), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control), I9 (tasks do not fall within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failure to meet required executive-function-related inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (source vs picture tasks) in healthy young adults and reports within-subject task contrasts and participant/sample details (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, the authors restricted analyses to a mask of regions taken from a prior study and report percentage signal change in those ROIs; no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are presented. Therefore the paper appears to report only ROI-based analyses and does not provide whole-brain results, violating inclusion criterion I7 and meeting exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E8 — the study includes participants outside the 18–60 yrs range (breathholding group ages 11.5–24.2), so the sample is not restricted to adults 18–60. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — verbal working memory), I6 (within-participant task vs control blocks and task-based contrasts), I9 (task falls within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (participant ages and health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I7 — the paper does not clearly present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (analyses appear to use per-subject voxelwise maps with group comparisons on activation volumes rather than a group voxelwise statistical map). Because E8 is met and I7 is not met, the study must be excluded for this adult executive-function meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI (and MEG) task-based study of working memory (an established executive function domain) in healthy young adults (I5, I9). The authors performed within-participant contrasts of encoding versus baseline/control epochs (active encoding vs control epochs) to obtain task-evoked effects (I6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were carried out with multiple-comparison correction and results are reported in tables/figures (I7, I8). Participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not restrict to ROI-only analyses (E3), is not connectivity/rest-only (E4), includes within-subject task activation contrasts in healthy participants rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), does not use only rest/fixation baseline (E6), is empirical human neuroimaging work (not E7), and participants are healthy adults within 18–60 years (not E8). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion based on: E6 (study uses fixation/rest as the baseline for task contrasts rather than an active control) and E8 (study includes a clinical autism sample and is not restricted to healthy adults). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are reported), I8 (results reported with coordinates and figures), and I10 (participant ages, imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, and screening of control participants are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (tasks are sensorimotor eye-movement paradigms, not clearly within established executive function domains), I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition), and I9 (tasks do not fall within canonical executive function domains like working memory/inhibition/planning). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control processes. It reports within-participant contrasts (insight vs analytic trials) that reflect differing modes of cognitive control/cognitive flexibility, uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses with reported cluster coordinates, and describes imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm (CRA problems) in healthy participants. The report identifies ACC preparatory activity related to cognitive control/conflict monitoring and switching, mapping onto executive-function domain (cognitive flexibility). Participant health, modality, and paradigm are described; although precise ages are not enumerated in the excerpt, the sample is described as neurologically healthy adults. Given the whole-brain maps/coordinates and within-subject task contrasts in an executive/control-relevant paradigm, the study meets inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

While this is an event-related fMRI study with group-level whole-brain voxelwise results and tasks that involve planning/working memory and effector selection (I5, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), the manuscript does not report participant ages or explicitly confirm a healthy adult sample (I10 not met). Additionally, the primary contrasts rely on fixation/rest baselines and comparisons between movement types rather than a clear within-participant contrast of an executive-task versus an active control condition (I6 not met). Because the review requires explicit reporting of participant age/healthy status and a within-participant task versus active control contrast, this study does not meet all inclusion criteria. Exclusion criterion E6 (use of rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control task) is therefore applicable.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-subject contrasts of manipulation and monitoring tasks versus an active recognition control condition and direct task contrasts (e.g., manipulation vs monitoring). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted with corrected thresholds; results are reported as coordinates and shown in figures/tables. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 24, range 21–31). Imaging modality, task paradigms, methods, and results are all clearly reported in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active control, empirical with healthy adults in 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria listed.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of a task-switching paradigm (executive function: cognitive flexibility/control). The full text reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinate tables and figures, within-participant contrasts (deviant vs. congruent trials and session comparisons), and reports participant demographics (11 healthy adults, mean age ~25) and imaging/method details. The task falls within established executive function domains. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults aged 18–60). Full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function) in healthy adults (n=12, mean age 24). It reports within-subject contrasts (NT vs CT, PT vs NT) using an active reaction-time control task (CT). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported/thresholded and peak coordinates are provided (Table 1, figures). Methods, results, and participant details are fully described. The paradigm is a working memory automatization task and a dual-task assessing processing capacity, which fits established executive-function domains. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Full text appears incomplete in the supplied content (only metadata/abstract available), preventing verification of all required inclusion criteria. From the abstract it is clear the study used PET imaging (I5 satisfied). However I6 (explicit within-participant contrast against an active control) cannot be fully confirmed—while sequences were compared to simple repetitive movement, the full methods/contrasts are not available. I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results) cannot be confirmed from the abstract. I9 (task falls within established executive function domains) is uncertain: the task is motor sequencing with suggested involvement of spatial working memory but may be primarily motor/execution rather than an executive-domain task. I10 (sufficient reporting of participant age and healthy status) is not provided in the abstract. Because the full text is not provided, I cannot verify whether any exclusion criteria (e.g., use of rest-only baseline, ROI-only analyses, non-healthy participants) are met or violated. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete/full-text unavailable for full verification. Inclusion IDs met: I5. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion IDs met: none (cannot determine)." ,

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-Back) in healthy adults (mean age 31.8), reporting within-participant contrast (2-Back > 0-Back). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and coordinates/thresholds are reported; results are presented in text, figures, and tables. Imaging modality (BOLD fMRI), sample demographics, and task paradigm are described. Supplemental material is referenced but not required for core criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of prospective memory and working memory (executive function/cognitive control). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., PM-1Back vs NB-1Back; NB-3Back vs NB-1Back), uses group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with whole-brain results and cluster thresholds (tables/figures/coordinates reported), and provides participant demographics confirming a healthy adult sample (ages 19–29). Tasks fall within executive function domains (working memory, sustained attention/monitoring). Imaging modality is fMRI and full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI task study of negative priming (an inhibition/executive control paradigm) in healthy adult participants (ages 22–28). It reports within-subject task contrasts (NeuI > C, NegI > C, NegI > NeuI) and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates (tables/figures). Imaging modality, participant health/age, and task paradigm are clearly reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adult bilinguals that explicitly investigates cognitive control processes (translation requiring inhibition of the dominant language and language switching requiring set-shifting/phonological recoding). It reports within-subject contrasts (translation vs reading; switching vs no-switching) using group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with tables of coordinates. Participant ages (25–39), healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and detailed task paradigms are reported. The tasks map onto established executive function domains (inhibition, cognitive flexibility). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active control baselines, empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults aged 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given these points, the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study adapts the Symbol Digit Modalities Test and reports a task-based within-subject contrast (activation vs active control) in 18 healthy adults. The task engages executive domains (working memory and selective attention). Group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t-test, p<0.05 FDR corrected) with coordinates in Table 1 and figures. Relevant participant/sample (mean age 32.5, healthy controls), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and full task paradigm/methods are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy activations, uses an active control). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an executive-function domain) that: (1) uses a task-based paradigm probing manipulation/maintenance (WM) versus an active control condition (three Xs/button press) and reports within-participant contrasts ([load − control]); (2) reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and stereotaxic coordinates and figures; (3) provides sufficient participant information (healthy control group demographics, imaging modality, task details) and examines healthy controls separately; and (4) clearly falls within established executive function domains. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group healthy participant activations). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This task-based PET study in healthy adults (n=6, ages 19–32) assesses conditional movement selection (stimulus-response mapping), a form of cognitive control/response selection. It includes a within-subject contrast of conditional versus active control tasks (conditional − (power+precision)/2), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates and t-values, and provides participant demographics, healthy sample confirmation, imaging modality, and task details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses fMRI to assess an executive function task (verbal 2-back working memory; I5, I9); includes within-participant contrasts of task vs an active baseline (symbol discrimination) allowing task-evoked contrast (I6); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and random-effects group analyses with stereotaxic normalization and correction for multiple comparisons (I7) with results presented in figures/tables (I8); and provides participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task details (I10). The healthy control group provides within-group activation maps appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive-function activations in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-only baseline, or age-range violations). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study tested working memory (delayed recognition) for voice identity and location — an established executive function domain (working memory). It reports within-participant contrasts of each memory task versus an active sensorimotor control, and direct voxelwise group-level whole-brain statistical maps (Z-maps) with tables/figures and ROI analyses. Participant age (18–27), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activation maps; not connectivity-only; includes within-group contrasts; uses an active control; healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

The paper reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory for grasp-target information (working memory = established executive function domain). It includes within-subject contrasts examining mnemonic processes (delayed vs. immediate grasping) serving as an active control comparison, and delay vs. baseline regressors. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are reported (SPM2; thresholding; coordinate tables and figures). Participant characteristics (n=21 healthy adults, mean age 23.6) and imaging modality (fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline without active contrasts, empirical, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study includes a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain) with within-subject task block modeling and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Z-statistic maps, cluster-corrected). Participant age range (22–52), healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. The 2-back task used alternating task and control epochs including an active control (‘TAP’ response epochs), and the GLM produced whole-brain activation estimates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, not resting-state-only, empirical human data, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (delayed-recognition of kinesthetic hand movements), which falls within executive function (working memory). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., Set 3 > baseline) against an active control (circular patterns). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise SPM results with coordinates and thresholding reported. Participant information (healthy adults aged 20–28), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so full-text is complete.

This is an fMRI, task-based, within-subject study that explicitly contrasts tool-planning (TOOL-NOGO) versus an active control (CONTROL-NOGO), reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with coordinate tables, and investigates planning — an executive function domain. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the provided full text does not report participant ages or age ranges (it reports only 'healthy adults' and sample sizes/handedness), and the review's I10 requires that relevant information about participant age be reported. Because I10 is not satisfied in the provided content, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text is judged complete for the purposes of screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=30, mean age 30) using a task that falls squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports within-participant, task-based contrasts (e.g., WM/DMS correct vs incorrect and subsequent memory contrasts) analyzed in a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM and presents coordinates and figures of whole-brain results. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. There are no violations of exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, does not use rest/fixation as sole baseline, is empirical with original human neuroimaging data, and participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an event-related fMRI study manipulating verbal working memory load (HOLD vs RELEASE) in healthy adult participants (fMRI n=10, mean age 26.1). The design includes within-subject contrasts of task conditions (HOLD vs RELEASE) addressing working memory, an established executive function domain. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed with SPM and reported (thresholds, coordinates, tables/figures described), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, empirical data in healthy adults).

This is an fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function) in healthy adults that reports within-subject contrasts (multiple updating-load conditions vs 0-load and a memory control task), group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinate tables and figures, and participant/sample, imaging modality, and task details. The experimental contrasts constitute active control comparisons (0-arrow with visual fillers; separate memory control task). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the supplied full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI task-based study (Go/NoGo) probing executive domains (response inhibition, vigilance/ initiation). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., Go vs NoGo, FWarning vs SWarning) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using random-effects SPM with FWE correction and provides coordinate tables and figures. Participant details (healthy, right-handed adults, ages ~22–28) and imaging modality and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, empirical human data within age range). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study meets the inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI engaging executive processes via the reverse-alphabetizing WM/manipulation task), I6 (within-participant contrasts between Alpha and retrieval tasks), I7 (whole-brain, group-level ST-PLS results reported with tables/figures), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures), I9 (task engages working memory/executive control), and I10 (participant ages, healthy screening, imaging modality, and task paradigms reported). However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes participants older than 60 years (older group ages 62–80), so the study includes participants outside the 18–60 healthy adult range required by the review. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite satisfying the inclusion criteria. Inclusion IDs not met: none.

This is an empirical, within-subject fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers that includes executive function tasks (2-back working memory and a variable attentional control task) with active control conditions (0-back, sensorimotor control). Group-level voxelwise SPM analyses are reported with peak MNI coordinates and statistical maps described (FWE-corrected values reported within ROIs), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results as reported in the text/figures. Participants are healthy adults and imaging modality and paradigms are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met. Note: statistical corrections were performed within anatomically defined ROIs rather than reporting whole-brain FWE, but voxelwise group-level results and coordinates are provided, which meets I7/I8 for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (two-back vs one-back and two-back vs sensory-motor), i.e., active control contrasts, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported maps/coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (ages 22–31). Imaging modality and task paradigm are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (N=17, ages 18–30) that uses a delayed match-to-sample working memory paradigm (executive function domain: working memory). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of DMS (working memory) versus active control (CON) tasks (e.g., DMS delay > CON delay), and performs group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise statistical maps and reported coordinate tables/figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task details are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: participants are outside the 18–60 age range (mean ages ~72–74) and the sample is not restricted to healthy individuals (includes Alzheimer’s disease patients). The study otherwise meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts: EWM > SM), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with corrected statistics), I8 (coordinates and activation tables described), I9 (working memory is an established executive function domain), and I10 (participant ages, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No other exclusion criteria apply. Because E8 is decisive (age and sample restrictions), the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task in middle-aged adults, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (within-participant 2-back vs 0-back contrast), I9 (working memory is an executive function), and I10 (reports age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). However, the study’s primary analyses are ROI-based: group inferences were conducted by averaging voxelwise t-values within 8 a priori ROIs (derived from a separate dataset). The paper does not report a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain coordinate table for the current sample, thus failing I7. Because it reports only ROI-based results with no whole-brain group map, Exclusion E3 applies. Additionally, the sample includes participants with metabolic syndrome (a clinical group), so the study is not restricted solely to healthy individuals, triggering Exclusion E8. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Excluded due to E8: the participant age range reported is 17–61, which includes individuals outside the eligible 18–60 age range. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive-related processes, e.g., working memory/relational integration), I6 (within-participant contrasts: fluid analogizing vs. active symbol-counting condition), I7 (group-level, whole-brain random-effects statistical maps reported and thresholded), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and shown in figures/tables), I9 (tasks fall within executive domains—working memory/relational reasoning), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because E8 is violated, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of attention switching (cognitive flexibility), satisfying executive function domain criteria. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., novel switch vs repeat, novel nonswitch vs repeat), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and cluster-level correction. Participant information (healthy adults, mean age 22.4, N=18 for main analyses) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting baseline only, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.
