This is a task-based PET study of healthy adults that explicitly investigates inhibitory control and action selection (executive functions). It reports within-subject contrasts (isolated index-finger vs full-hand movement; rest vs movement) that probe selection/inhibition, and includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with cluster-level whole-brain correction and reported coordinates/locations. Participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality (PET) and task details are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because study reports only connectivity/covariance analyses during a single-task FDG-PET CPT and does not provide a within-participant task vs active-control contrast nor a group-level task-evoked activation map. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports primarily connectivity analyses without a whole-brain task activation map) and E8 (sample includes participants older than 60 years: age range 20–69). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based study of cognitive/vigilance task), I9 (task falls within executive domain: vigilance), I10 (reports participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-subject contrast of task vs active control), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation/contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an FDG-PET correlational study of resting glucose metabolism in patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) and controls, relating clinical scores of executive and behavioral deficits to baseline metabolism. It does not use a task-based fMRI/PET activation paradigm or report within-participant task vs active-control contrasts in healthy adults. It therefore fails the meta-analysis requirements for task-evoked, within-subject executive control contrasts and healthy-sample task activations. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (no within-group task activation contrast in healthy participants), E6 (resting metabolic measure rather than task with active baseline), E8 (includes patient population; not restricted to healthy adults). Inclusion IDs met: none []. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no task-based PET/fMRI paradigm—resting metabolism only), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (no task-evoked whole-brain group-level activation map for an executive task), I8 (no task activation coordinates/maps), I9 (no task belonging to established executive domains performed during imaging), I10 (does not report a task paradigm for imaging in healthy participants). Full text appears complete.

This study used PET ligand binding ([11C]-raclopride) at rest to measure striatal D2 receptor availability and correlated these measures with behavioral executive tasks. It did not perform task-evoked, within-participant PET activation contrasts or report group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps. The imaging analyses were ROI-based rather than whole-brain. Participants were an older, post-menopausal sample (ages 58–91), i.e., outside the 18–60 healthy adult range. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring task-based fMRI/PET activation contrasts and whole-brain task maps. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results) and E8 (participants outside 18–60). Inclusion IDs met: I9 (tasks are executive domains: working memory, planning) and I10 (participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7, and I8 (no task-evoked whole-brain results).

The study uses PET with a modified Stroop task and presents within-subject conflict vs no-conflict contrasts and group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 met). However, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults: it includes 25-day abstinent heavy marijuana users and a control group, so participants are not confirmed as a healthy sample (violates E8 and I10 is not met). Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement to include only healthy participants.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–38) examining a visuospatial mental operation that the authors frame and test as involving executive processes (sequencing/planning/executive control). The study includes within-participant contrasts of operation versus active control (S2-VSMO+ > S2-VSMO− and S2-VSMO+ > S1-VSMO+), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2, voxel-wise corrected threshold) with coordinates and ROI follow-ups. Participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range samples) are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Although this is a PET study in healthy adults relating FDOPA kinetics to performance on an executive/vigilance task (CPT), it does not provide task-evoked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps. Imaging analyses use ROI-based kinetic measures rather than a within-participant task vs active-control contrast or whole-brain task activation maps. Additionally, the sample includes ages up to 64 years (outside the 18–60 inclusion window). Therefore the study fails key inclusion requirements for task-evoked, whole-brain activation data and violates age restrictions.

Exclusion criteria met: E8 — study includes clinical Parkinson's disease patients (not restricted to healthy participants) and reports participant ages exceeding the 18–60 range (controls up to 67 years; some patients up to 64). Inclusion criteria met: I7 — group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) fMRI analyses are reported; I8 — whole-brain results are reported and described (coordinates and maps); I10 — participant ages, healthy status (controls vs patients), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm (reward learning) are reported. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — the task is a reward-based reinforcement learning paradigm, not an executive function/cognitive control task; I6 — there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition; I9 — the task does not fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Because E8 is violated and multiple required inclusion criteria for executive-function studies are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of interference resolution (arrow flanker) with within-subject Incongruent vs Congruent contrasts, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (coordinates and corrected clusters reported), and full participant and paradigm details. However, it includes older adults (mean age 74) outside the review's age range (18–60), violating exclusion criterion E8. Therefore it must be excluded despite meeting all inclusion criteria. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion IDs not met: none. Exclusion IDs met: E8 (participants outside 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the manuscript reports PET-based correlational/functional connectivity (‘associativity’) analyses during a continuous performance task and does not provide a within-participant task > active-control contrast or a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map in healthy participants. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (connectivity-only analyses without a whole-brain task activation map), E5 (no within-group task activation contrast for healthy participants; emphasis is on between-group connectivity differences), and E8 (sample not restricted to healthy adults and includes participants outside 18–60: controls up to age 69 and inclusion of patient groups). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based study of an executive-domain CPT), I9 (task = vigilance, an executive domain), I10 (reports participant ages, healthy-control status, PET modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast vs active control) and I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete = false).

This PET study includes a task (auditory CPT) and reports participant details and imaging modalities, but does NOT provide a within-participant task vs active-control contrast nor a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Instead, analyses are ROI-based correlations of metabolism and flow and between-group comparisons including patient groups. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria and meets multiple exclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results), E5 (no within-group task activation contrast in healthy participants; analyses are correlative/between-group), E8 (sample not restricted to healthy individuals — includes unipolar and bipolar patients). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (PET study with task-based paradigm), I9 (task falls within executive domain: vigilance/CPT), I10 (reports age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of task vs active control), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete for screening purposes (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a PET Stroop study reporting within-subject incongruent vs congruent contrasts and whole-brain, group-level maps for healthy control participants (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 satisfied). However, the study includes a clinical patient group and therefore is not restricted to healthy individuals, which meets exclusion criterion E8. Because any exclusion criterion triggers exclusion, the study is excluded despite meeting all inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This PET study investigates go players’ planning and checkmate-judgment using task vs a passive stare baseline. While it is a task-based PET study in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM results (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10), the within-participant contrasts are versus a passive fixation/baseline (staring at the center) rather than an active control condition. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and falls under exclusion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite otherwise meeting other criteria.

This PET study used an auditory oddball task (vigilance/attention) and reports within-participant contrasts (oddball vs reference), voxelwise, group-level whole-brain SPM analyses, and provides participant ages and healthy control sample details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample includes both healthy volunteers and schizophrenic patients (i.e., the study is not restricted to healthy individuals), which triggers exclusion criterion E8. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite meeting the other inclusion criteria.

This PET study used an auditory continuous performance task (vigilance) in healthy adults and reports within-subject comparisons of ethanol vs placebo with whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study with an executive/vigilance task), I9 (task falls within executive domain: vigilance), I8 (whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables), and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). However, the study does NOT provide the required within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition (I6 not met): the primary contrasts are pharmacological (ethanol vs placebo) rather than task>control. Consequently, the required task-evoked within-subject activation maps for an executive-control contrast are absent (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) were triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 (and by extension I7) are not met, the study is excluded.

Full text reviewed and excluded because the study does not evaluate a prototypical executive-function task. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality [PET], and task paradigm described). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (though PET was used, the study assesses emotion induction and heart-rate variability rather than a task designed to assess executive function/cognitive control), I6 (no within-participant contrast of a defined executive function task versus an active control condition—the Emotion vs Neutral contrast reflects emotion induction, not a canonical executive task contrast), I9 (tasks do not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, or cognitive flexibility; cognitive-control elements are incidental to emotion maintenance). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) were triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is a PET neuroimaging experiment in healthy adults using a task-based spatial working memory (spatial span) paradigm, which falls within executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts of span conditions versus an active visuomotor control and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM99 voxel-based exploratory search with corrected peaks), plus ROI analyses. Participant demographics (age range 21–38), healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and task details are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet key methodological inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Although it examines executive function (WCST) in healthy adults (I9) and reports participant details, healthy sample status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigm (I10), it is not a task-based neuroimaging activation study. PET was used to measure D2/D3 receptor binding at rest and these binding maps were correlated with behavioral WCST scores; there is no within-participant task-versus-active-control contrast (I6 not met) and no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (I7 not met). The paper therefore does not satisfy I5 (PET/fMRI task-based executive function paradigm in the imaging data) or I6/I7. No exclusion criterion from the provided list directly applies (e.g., it is not solely an ROI-only report without any voxel-based analysis, though the analyses are receptor-binding correlations rather than task activations).

This study uses task-based fMRI of an executive task (letter fluency) with a within-participant contrast (fluency vs an active control ‘nothing’), and reports participant ages and imaging/task details. However, it does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinates in the manuscript (analyses are ROI-focused), so it fails the requirement for whole-brain results (I7/I8). Crucially, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults: the study includes participants with autism spectrum disorders (clinical group) and includes some participants under 18 (ages 14 and 16), violating the review’s restriction to healthy adults aged 18–60. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results) and E8 (includes non-healthy participants and participants below the specified age range). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I7, I8, I10.

This study is a PET receptor-binding correlation study, not a task-based neuroimaging activation study. It measured extrastriatal D2 receptor binding at rest and correlated binding potentials with neuropsychological test scores. It does not include any within-participant task vs active-control imaging contrasts, nor does it report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (no task-based PET/fMRI executive-function activation). Inclusion/exclusion summary: exclusion IDs met: none of the listed exclusion criteria directly apply; inclusion criteria met: none; inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET executive task), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I10 (no task paradigm reported for imaging). Full text appears complete.

This study is a PET investigation of the MSIT (an executive/inhibition task) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with coordinates, and provides participant age and healthy-sample information (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 satisfied). However, the PET imaging contrasts compare cognitive activity (MSIT) to rest rather than to an active control condition; no within-participant PET contrast of task vs an active control (e.g., interference vs control trials) is reported, so inclusion criterion I6 is not met. Two exclusion criteria are therefore triggered: E6 (rest used as the only baseline for the imaging contrast without an active control task) and E8 (sample includes participants aged 65–75, i.e., outside the required 18–60 range). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and any exclusion criterion disqualifies the study, the study must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not report task-based executive-function activations in healthy adults. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (PET was acquired during mental rest, not an active executive task/active control), and E8 (participant ages 40–81, which lies outside the meta-analysis age range 18–60). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I10 (the paper reports participant ages, confirms nondemented/healthy sample status, specifies imaging modality [FDG-PET], and describes the scanning paradigm [mental rest]). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no fMRI/PET task-based executive-function or cognitive-control paradigm was used), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive task vs an active control condition), I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation map — the SPM analyses are of resting/pre-post metabolic change, not task-evoked activation), and I9 (no task falling within established executive function domains). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given these violations, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis of task-evoked executive-function activations.

The study is excluded because it does not provide task-evoked, whole-brain neuroimaging activation maps for executive function. Specifically, PET was used to measure baseline D2 receptor binding (ROI analyses) correlated with behavioral variability, rather than a task-based within-subject activation contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only PET binding results with no whole-brain task activation maps) and E8 (sample ages 41–65 includes participants >60 years). Inclusion criteria met: I9 (executive task: set-shifting IEDSS) and I10 (reported participant age, healthy status, imaging modality PET, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET activation study), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7/I8 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps or coordinates reported). Full text appears complete.

This full text reports an empirical PET study of executive-function tasks (dual-task and integration paradigms) in healthy adults, with group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) and reported activation coordinates. It includes within-participant contrasts of executive conditions versus active control single-task conditions (e.g., [dual − (auditory + visual)]), reports random-effects analyses and voxelwise thresholds, and provides participant demographics (right-handed healthy adults, ages 21–25). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, baseline is active control (single tasks), it is empirical with original human PET data, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

While the study is a PET task-based experiment with a within-participant active control, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and reports participant demographics and healthy status, it does not investigate an executive function or cognitive control task as defined by the review. The paradigm is an implicit motor sequence (serial reaction time) learning task assessing procedural/motor learning and motor planning rather than established executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning in the sense of complex goal-directed executive planning, vigilance, or initiation). Therefore I5 and I9 are not met, so the study must be excluded.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: met inclusion I5 (neuroimaging study of an executive task) and I9 (task falls within executive domain: updating/working memory). Cannot verify I6 (presence of a within-participant contrast vs an active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported), I8 (acceptable whole-brain results reporting such as coordinates/figures), or I10 (participant age/healthy sample and full imaging/task details) from the provided content. No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete/full-text content, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

Only the title, abstract and metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). However, the provided content does not allow confirmation of: I6 (within-participant contrast of task vs an active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map reported), or I10 (participant ages and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample). No exclusion criteria from the list can be confirmed based on the truncated content. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified without the full text, exclude pending retrieval of the complete article.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract available). From the abstract: this is an event-related fMRI study of inhibition of imitative responses, reporting within-subject incongruent vs congruent contrasts and activations in prefrontal and parietal regions. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task-based study), I6 (within-participant contrast: incongruent vs congruent), I9 (task assesses inhibition/executive control). However I7 (verification of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map) and I10 (reported participant age and explicit confirmation of healthy adult sample) cannot be confirmed from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met, but because the full text is incomplete and key items (I7, I10) cannot be verified, the study must be excluded pending access to the full article.

Exclusion E8 met: sample includes participants aged 17–27 (one or more participants aged 17), i.e., includes an under-18 participant and therefore falls outside the meta-analysis age range of 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing response inhibition/executive function), I6 (within-participant no-go vs. go contrasts), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with random-effects maps), I8 (results reported as activation maps and coordinates), I9 (task domain = inhibition, an executive function), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Because exclusion criterion E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite satisfying other inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility/set-shifting in healthy adults (ages 20–39). The study reports within-participant contrasts (targets vs novels; target-shift vs target-maintain), and performed a whole-brain voxelwise analysis using SPM99 with group-level t maps. Task falls within executive function domain (cognitive flexibility). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (4-T fMRI) and detailed task methods are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-state only, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore meets all inclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study of an executive function (response inhibition via a Go/No-Go task) in healthy young adults (ages 18–22). It includes within-participant contrasts (Press for all letters except X − Press for X) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (P<0.001) with coordinates and cluster statistics; ROI analyses are also reported but whole-brain results are present. Relevant participant information (age range, health status with exclusion of Axis I diagnoses, imaging modality, and task paradigm) is provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI results, connectivity-only analyses, lack of within-group task activation, only rest baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy sample) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers (n=19; age range 19–46) using a stop-signal inhibitory control task (an established executive function domain). It reports within-subject (placebo vs atomoxetine) task contrasts that estimate BOLD responses to successful and failed inhibition relative to go trials (an active baseline), satisfying the requirement for a within-participant task contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using permutation-based cluster-level inference and peak coordinates are reported; whole-brain maps/coordinates are clearly described. Participant characteristics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and the task paradigm are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and the sample is healthy adults within 18–60 years. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion applied: E6 (study uses a blank-screen/fixation control as the only baseline rather than an active control). Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function—antisaccade/inhibition), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures), I9 (task assesses inhibition, an executive function), I10 (participant ages and healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition; the control was a rest/fixation blank screen). Full text appears complete. Because E6 is met (violates required active control baseline), the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of the Stroop negative-priming paradigm (an inhibition/selective-attention executive function task). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; primed vs non-primed) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (with cluster-level correction) and also reports within-group activations for healthy controls (right DLPFC). Participant ages and healthy control status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task details are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no indications of incompleteness. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibition (stop-signal task) with both MDD and healthy control participants (HC ages 19–37). The study reports within-subject contrasts (hard vs easy inhibit; errors vs correct) and conducted whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level analyses with cluster correction. Task falls squarely within the executive function domain (inhibition). Participant age ranges, healthy control status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only, resting-state, or non-empirical paper). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore the full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract: the study is a PET investigation of a GO/NO-GO inhibition task with within-subject task-minus-control and task-minus-task contrasts, and reports healthy participants—so I5, I6, and I9 are satisfied. However, participant ages are not reported in the provided content (I10 not met). Also, although the abstract mentions rCBF change images and identified fields of significant change, the provided content does not allow confirmation that group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were reported (I7 cannot be confirmed). Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I10) is not met and I7 cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending retrieval of the complete article. Based on the provided content (title and abstract), the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive/inhibition task), I6 (within-participant contrasts: GO vs NO-GO), I7 (reports whole-brain group-level activations across the brain), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures), and I9 (task is inhibition, an executive function). However, the supplied full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided) and does not report participant ages; I10 (relevant information on participant age) cannot be verified. Per screening rules, ALL inclusion criteria must be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are explicitly met based on available information. Therefore I must EXCLUDE this record pending a complete full text that confirms I10.

The study includes appropriate fMRI executive-function task data (Go/No-Go inhibition) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses, but it does not provide a within-participant (within healthy-controls) task activation map isolated to healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports between-group contrasts and whole-group effects but does not report a within-group healthy-only task activation contrast), and E8 (study sample is not restricted to healthy individuals — includes an antisocial personality disorder patient group). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive function task), I7 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables), I9 (task is an established executive function: inhibition), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast map reported for healthy participants alone). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion met: E8 — study includes older adults (mean age ~72.8 years) outside the meta-analysis age range 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — Go/No-go/inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrasts/modeling of inhibitory trials vs other events/baseline), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported as clusters/tables described in text), I9 (task within executive function domain: inhibition), I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Although all inclusion criteria are satisfied, the presence of participants outside the 18–60 range (E8) requires exclusion. fulltext_incomplete=false.

Provided content is limited to title, abstract, and metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). However, the available text does not confirm a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map or report of whole-brain coordinates/figures (I7 cannot be verified), nor does it report participant ages or explicitly confirm a healthy sample (I10 not verifiable). Because core inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an fMRI study of cognitive control in healthy adults (ages 18–29) with within-subject contrasts (inconsistent vs consistent actions) and adequate reporting of participants, imaging modality, and paradigm (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, the authors did not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Their voxelwise analyses were restricted/masked to selected regions and they primarily report ROI and region-restricted voxelwise results rather than an unrestricted whole-brain map. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/region-restricted analyses with no whole-brain results). Accordingly, exclude.

This is a task-based, within-subject fMRI study manipulating executive demands (two-back vs one-back; source vs item memory) in healthy adults (age 24–37). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects) are reported with coordinates and statistical thresholds; contrasts compare high- vs low-load active task conditions. Participant, imaging modality, and paradigm details are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, participants are healthy and within age range). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a methods-focused paper introducing Activated Region Fitting (ARF) with simulations and a single-subject empirical application (Go/No-Go). While it uses fMRI and an executive-function inhibition task (Go/No-Go) and includes a within-subject No-Go>Go contrast, it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map required by inclusion criterion I7. The empirical data are from a single subject and ARF-derived region estimates rather than a conventional group whole-brain activation map. Participant demographic/health details sufficient for I10 are not clearly reported for a healthy adult group. Therefore the study fails required inclusion criteria (notably I7 and I10) and must be excluded.

Because key inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I10) cannot be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending retrieval of the complete article.

This is an fMRI study of an executive-function task (n-back working memory) with healthy adults, whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses and reported coordinates; however the reported within-participant contrasts are 0-back vs rest and 2-back vs rest. The manuscript does not report a within-participant contrast of the executive function condition relative to an active control (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

This study includes healthy adult participants but also reports data from an elderly group (mean age ~69 yrs), i.e. includes participants outside the review age range (18–60). The study otherwise meets inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI and PET on executive-function tasks (working memory 2-back) (I5); reports within-participant contrasts using an active control (2-back vs 0-back) (I6); provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses/SPM maps (I7) and reports coordinates/figures (I8); the tasks fall under executive function (working memory) (I9); and participant demographics, health status, imaging modality and paradigms are reported (I10). However because E8 is met (participants outside 18–60 included), the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=12, ages 22–40) that directly investigates motor planning and self-initiation—domains listed in the review inclusion (planning, initiation). It includes within-participant contrasts isolating planning/initiation processes (e.g., IP_INT – IP_EXT; planning internally vs externally triggered) and contrasts versus an observation/rest condition. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM second-level maps, coordinate reporting, ROI follow-up reported but whole-brain results are primary). Participant demographic, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are clearly provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task contrasts, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10).

Excluded because the study sample is not restricted to healthy adults (includes adults with childhood ADHD and healthy controls), violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive functions: Stop and Switch tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts: Successful Stop–Go, Unsuccessful Stop–Go, Switch–Repeat), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables), I9 (tasks are established executive domains: inhibition and cognitive flexibility), I10 (participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigms reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded based on E8.

Exclusion IDs met: E3 (only ROI/masked small-volume analyses reported, no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-activation map presented) and E8 (sample comprises nicotine-dependent smokers, i.e., not a healthy-only sample). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — Stroop cognitive control), I6 (within-participant contrast: incongruent>congruent), I9 (task falls within executive function/inhibition domain). Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map reported — analyses were masked/ROI small-volume corrected), I10 (while age and imaging/task details are reported, the sample is not a healthy sample — nicotine dependence present, so confirmation of healthy sample status is not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide whole-brain task maps and for including non-healthy participants.

The study includes both healthy control participants and a clinical group (ADHD). Exclusion criterion E8 applies: the sample is not restricted to healthy individuals. Although the paper reports task-based fMRI of an inhibitory (executive) paradigm (Think/No-Think), includes within-subject NT>T contrasts, reports group-level whole-brain analyses and coordinates, and provides participant ages (18–23) and task details, the presence of a clinical sample (ADHD) means the study is not confined to healthy adults and therefore must be excluded under E8. Inclusion criteria I5–I10 are otherwise satisfied (within-subject executive fMRI paradigm, active control contrast, whole-brain group maps reported, coordinates described, inhibition task, and participant info). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met based on available information: I5 (event-related fMRI task-based study), I6 (within-subject contrast: targets vs distractors), I9 (task involves inhibition/categorization consistent with executive function domain). Inclusion criteria not verifiable / not met from available text: I7 (cannot confirm a group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map from the abstract alone), I8 (format of whole-brain results not confirmable), I10 (participant ages and confirmation of healthy sample not reported in provided text). No exclusion criteria were clearly met from the abstract alone. Because I7 and I10 cannot be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study cannot be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult smokers (ages 20–40) using the N-Back working memory task (an established executive function). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., 3-back vs 1-back and pre- vs post-smoking blocks) and group-level voxelwise SPM{T} maps entered into a second-level (random effects) ANOVA, with reported MNI coordinates for significant clusters in left DLPFC. Although analyses were constrained to an a priori ROI with small-volume correction, results are reported as voxelwise group statistics/coordinates (satisfying coordinate reporting per I8). Participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses an N-back working memory task (executive function) and reports group-level, whole-brain connectivity (mutual information/coherence) maps comparing rest and task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of executive/working memory task), I9 (task is working memory), I10 (reports participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and paradigm). However, it does NOT meet critical inclusion criteria: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition is reported — the primary comparisons are connectivity differences between rest and the N-back), and I7 (the paper does not report whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise activation maps; analyses are connectivity-based). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only connectivity analyses without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on task-evoked activations.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract the study is an fMRI n-back working memory task (meets I5) and the task falls within executive function (meets I9). However, I cannot confirm several required items from the full text: (a) whether there is a within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition (I6), (b) whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures are reported (I7/I8), and (c) whether participant ages and confirmation of a healthy sample are reported (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met from the available content. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, I exclude the study pending access to the full article.

This fMRI study uses an established executive-function task (incongruent color-word Stroop) in healthy adults (ages 23–44). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing the distraction (Stroop) condition to control (e.g., (PD+HD)>(P+H), (PD−HD)>(P−H)), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with corrected thresholds and cluster/coordinate results, and provides participant, modality, and task details. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG-fMRI study of an n-back working memory task in healthy adults (ages 29 and 34). It meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts such as 3-back vs 1-back), I9 (task falls within working memory/executive domain), and I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). However, it does NOT meet I7: the review requires at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. This paper reports single-subject analyses (two individual subjects) and describes spatial overlap across these two subjects but does not present a group-level voxelwise statistical map or group GLM. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are directly triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because inclusion criterion I7 is not satisfied.

This is an fMRI task-based study using a Stroop variant (emotional counting Stroop) that probes cognitive control/inhibition (executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 24.2). It reports within-subject contrasts (negative vs neutral words; neutral vs fixation) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (KS statistical maps) with reported coordinates and corrected p-values. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm are provided. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations in healthy adults and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: It is a PET study of sustained attention/working memory in healthy volunteers (I5 met), includes within-participant contrasts between task conditions (I6 met), and the tasks fall within executive domains (working memory/vigilance) (I9 met). However, the report does not provide the full paper to confirm that a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map was produced and reported (I7 not confirmed). Participant ages are not reported in the provided content (I10 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly triggered from the abstract alone. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text access.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the available abstract: this is a PET study in young healthy adults performing the WCST with an active sensorimotor control, so I5 (PET/executive task), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I9 (task in executive domain: cognitive flexibility/working memory), and I10 (participant age/healthy sample, imaging modality, task paradigm reported) are satisfied. However, I7 (presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or clearly reported whole-brain results) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met based on the abstract. Because the full text is not available to verify whole-brain voxelwise results and detailed reporting, I exclude the study pending access to the complete article.

The study is excluded because it does not report any task-evoked neuroimaging activation results or group-level whole-brain statistical maps required for this meta-analysis. Although participants were tested inside an operating MRI scanner, the paper explicitly states “We do not report the brain-imaging data in this paper, but focus on the behavioral data.” Therefore it fails key inclusion requirements for an fMRI/PET activation study. Inclusion criteria met: I9 (task-switching is an executive function/cognitive flexibility task). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study is not an fMRI/PET activation study reporting imaging results), I6 (no within-participant imaging contrast reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (no whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I10 (insufficient explicit neuroimaging reporting; imaging modality is mentioned but no imaging results or confirmation of healthy sample imaging data provided). No exclusion criteria from the list apply directly (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of an executive function task (N-back working memory) in healthy adults (age 21–27). It reports a within-subject contrast (2-back > 0-back, an active control), performs group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with FWE correction, and also provides participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality and task details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This fMRI study reports task-based working memory (n-back) activation with healthy control participants and provides within-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (cluster-corrected maps) for controls. The paradigm uses an active control (0-back) and an experimental 2-back contrast (exp–con), meeting the within-participant contrast requirement. Participant ages (controls mean 30.8 ± 5.98) are within 18–60 and healthy status was confirmed by SCID; imaging modality and task details are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back) in healthy postmenopausal adults. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects, BrainVoyager) and reports regional activation results (BA labels/coordinates) across N-back loads. The N-back includes an active control condition (0-back) and analyses examine load-specific effects (2-back/3-back) and within-subject contrasts (post-treatment versus baseline; condition-specific contrasts), satisfying the requirement for a within-participant task-versus-control contrast. Relevant participant info (mean age, health screening) and full imaging/task details are reported. I found no violations of exclusion criteria: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not connectivity-only, include within-group task activation contrasts, and use an active control (0-back). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=10, mean age 28) using the n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-participant task contrasts (0-back, 1-back, 2-back), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM t-maps of task-evoked deactivations (voxelwise maps thresholded and reported). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all described. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses an active control 0-back condition, is empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, this is an fMRI n-back verbal working memory study in 20 healthy right-handed male volunteers with voxelwise regression and reported coordinates, so inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI study of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active sensorimotor control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (coordinates reported), and I9 (working memory task) are satisfied. However, inclusion criterion I10 (relevant information reported regarding participant age) cannot be confirmed from the supplied content. Because the full text is incomplete and I10 cannot be verified, not all inclusion criteria are demonstrably met; therefore the study is excluded pending access to the complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are evident from the available information.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes an established executive function task (verbal working memory: n-back) and a visual attention task, using within-subject contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back; 4-balls vs 2-balls) relative to active control conditions. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM2; voxel-level FWE correction; repeated-measures ANOVA), and results are reported across the whole brain. Participant characteristics (N=22, healthy adults, age 30±8), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts in healthy adults, uses active control conditions). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Meets inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibition (go/no-go) that reports within-subject contrasts and whole-brain group-level results, and provides participant age, diagnostic status, imaging modality, and task details. However, the sample consists of male children and adolescents (not adults) and includes clinical (ADHD) participants as well as controls. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60 years or not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis focused on healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 were reported). Exclusion criteria applied: E8.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: met inclusion criteria I5 (PET study of executive function: RVIP - sustained attention/working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts reported, including comparison to a simple sustained attention control), and I9 (task falls within executive domains: vigilance/working memory). Inclusion criteria not met or not verifiable from provided content: I7 (cannot confirm group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps from the truncated text), I8 (unable to verify whether whole-brain results are reported in tables/coordinates), and I10 (participant age not reported; only ‘eight healthy volunteers’ stated). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met. Because critical methodological details and whole-brain result confirmation are not available in the provided full text, I exclude the study pending access to the complete article.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract: this is an event-related fMRI study using a GO/NOGO task assessing inhibition, so I5 is satisfied. The abstract implies within-participant contrasts (e.g., successful inhibition vs. other trials), so I6 is satisfied. The task falls within an executive function domain (inhibition), so I9 is satisfied. However, the available content does not provide the full article methods/results needed to confirm a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analysis (I7) nor report participant ages and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample (I10). Because ALL inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text availability. No exclusion criteria (E3-E8) are determinable from the provided text.

Excluded because the sample is not restricted to healthy individuals (E8). Although no participants met criteria for lifetime MDD and the age range (18–27) is within 18–60, the study intentionally sampled women with a range of depressive symptoms and compared low- and high-depressive-symptom groups (HD mean CESD=15.4), so the cohort is not a clearly healthy-only sample. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (within-participant contrasts, e.g., invalid>valid), I7 (group-level whole-brain omnibus contrasts were performed), I8 (whole-brain results described/reported), I9 (task assesses cognitive control/executive function). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (confirmation of healthy sample status not satisfied because participants with elevated depressive symptoms were included). Therefore the study should be excluded per E8.

This fMRI study (WCST, Nelson version) tests cognitive flexibility (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 20–24) using a task-based within-subject contrast (R1 vs R2 shifts). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were reported with thresholding and peak coordinates (with SVC reported), and full methods, results, and participant information are provided. The contrast (initial novel shifts vs later shifts) constitutes an active within-participant task comparison. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because baseline/control was passive rest (subject instructed to lie still), violating E6. Met inclusion: I5 (task-based PET study), I9 (task involves motor planning — an executive planning domain), I10 (reports healthy young participants, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Did NOT meet inclusion I6 (required within-participant contrast versus an active control — study used rest baseline), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map; results are presented from single-subject/parametric maps rather than a group-level whole-brain analysis), and I8 (no qualifying group-level whole-brain results reported in tables/coordinates). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation (I7) and instead reports ROI-based extraction and analyses (violates E3). Additionally, the sample includes older adults (67–77 years) outside the review age range 18–60, violating E8. The study does satisfy that it is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (Go/No-go) and reports healthy participant status and task details (I5, I9, I10). However, it lacks a clearly reported within-participant contrast against an active control condition (I6 not met) and does not present whole-brain maps or coordinates (I7 not met). Therefore it must be excluded.

Full text provided appears to be only title and abstract (fulltext_incomplete=true). The study is an fMRI working-memory study reporting whole-brain task activations in controls and alcoholics, so it meets I5 (fMRI of executive function), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text), and I9 (working memory task). However, the reported contrasts in the abstract are task vs rest (e.g., 2-back vs rest, center vs rest) with no clear within-participant contrast against an active control condition (I6 not met), which triggers exclusion E6 (rest-only baseline). Additionally, the sample includes alcoholics (clinical population) and is not restricted to healthy individuals, triggering exclusion E8. Relevant participant age and confirmation of a healthy-only sample are not clearly reported for inclusion (I10 not met). Therefore the study is excluded.

This fMRI study investigates thought suppression (a form of cognitive control/inhibition) in healthy adults (mean age 19.7) using task-based paradigms (SUPPRESS, CLEAR, FREE-THOUGHT). It reports within-participant contrasts (SUPPRESS vs FREE-THOUGHT; CLEAR vs FREE-THOUGHT; CLEAR vs SUPPRESS) with group-level random-effects SPM99 analyses and voxelwise whole-brain results reported (thresholded, coordinates/BA reported). The FREE-THOUGHT condition serves as an active control (not rest/fixation). Participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria appear to be met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional set-shifting (cognitive flexibility) in healthy adults (six right-handed subjects, ages 19–25). The design includes within-subject contrasts isolating the set-shifting condition (alternate) versus active control conditions (tie, win, lose) and versus rest. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis was performed using SPM96 with thresholding and reported regional activations (text and coordinates). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This fMRI study investigates working memory (an executive function) with within-subject contrasts (high vs low WM demand), and reports participant/sample details and imaging modality; however, all reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based (PFC and amygdala) and the manuscript does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation map or coordinates/tables of whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Full text appears complete. Excluding on that basis.

This study uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (spatial n-back) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and reports within-group contrasts for healthy controls, but it recruited and analyzed a clinical sample (patients with major depressive disorder) alongside controls. It is therefore not restricted to healthy individuals, violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive task), I6 (within-participant contrast with active control: 0-back), I7 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I8 (coordinates/tables described), I9 (working memory domain), I10 (participant/sample, modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria applied: E8 (study includes clinical participants; not restricted to healthy individuals). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of working memory (executive domain) including healthy adults, reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and coordinate results, and provides participant age/imaging/task details. However, it does not include an active control condition nor a within-participant contrast of the executive task versus an active control; analyses focus on parametric/exponential decreases across retrieval blocks and use rest/break periods rather than an active control. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met and exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as only baseline without active control) applies. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The study is an fMRI working-memory task, so inclusion criteria I5 and I9 are satisfied. However several required inclusions are not met or cannot be confirmed from the provided content: I6 (no clear report of a within-participant contrast vs an active control condition), I7 (no explicit confirmation of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map; abstract ambiguously mentions 'whole-brain imaging techniques' but does not confirm voxelwise group maps), I8 (no reported coordinates/figures/tables from whole-brain results in the provided content), and I10 (participant ages and explicit confirmation of healthy sample status are not reported). Because multiple inclusion criteria are not met/confirmable and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text availability.

Full text appears to be an FDG-PET study comparing unmedicated schizophrenia outpatients and controls; a Stroop task was performed within a day of PET but the manuscript reports between-group metabolic differences (patients vs controls) rather than a within-participant task-evoked PET activation map in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I9 (Stroop is an inhibition/executive function task). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear task-based PET/fMRI activation during imaging), I6 (no within-participant contrast of task vs active control), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported), I10 (participants are not a healthy-only sample). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only between-group contrasts without within-group healthy activation) and E8 (includes clinical (schizophrenia) participants, not restricted to healthy adults). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract we can confirm: I5 (PET study of executive function) and I9 (task within executive domains—working memory/WCST). However, key inclusion criteria cannot be verified: I6 (presence of a within-participant contrast of an executive task vs an active control is not explicitly reported in the abstract), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are implied by use of SPM but not explicitly detailed or provided), I8 (whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement not accessible in the provided content), and I10 (participant age not reported; only described as “normal subjects”). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are explicitly met based on available content. Because the full text is incomplete and essential inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a working memory (digit-sorting) task in healthy adults (ages 21–48). It reports within-subject contrasts across task difficulty levels (3/4/5-digit loads), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses (ΔR2 maps) with reported Talairach coordinates and cluster sizes, and provides sufficient participant, modality, and task details. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for executive-function task activation meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (mental rotation) in healthy adults (mean age 27). It uses within-participant contrasts comparing rotation versus identity-judgment conditions (active control), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99; cluster thresholds, t-values, coordinates transformed to Talairach) with activation tables and detailed results. Imaging modality, participant characteristics, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (verbal 2-back) in healthy adults with an active control (0-back), reporting group analyses and activation-based ROI selection and Talairach coordinates. It meets I5 (fMRI executive-function task), I6 (within-participant contrast 2-back vs 0-back with active control), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported/coordinates provided), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures described), I9 (working memory is an established executive domain), and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task activation, uses active control, healthy adults 24–33). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults. It used task-based fMRI (I5) with Stroop paradigms that probe cognitive control/inhibition (I9). Within-subject contrasts were reported (ncStroop minus nStroop and ecStroop minus nStroop), providing an active-control, within-participant contrast (I6). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (thresholding and cluster correction described), with coordinates/figures referenced (I7,I8). Participant demographics, healthy control subgroup characteristics, imaging modality, and task details are reported (I10). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are violated. Therefore the healthy control within-group whole-brain Stroop activation maps are eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study uses task-based fMRI of working memory (MGS) with an active control (VGS), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and provides participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task details. However, it samples adolescents (mean ages ~12–13) and includes a high-risk clinical group (offspring of schizophrenic parents), thus failing the meta-analysis requirement for healthy adult participants (age 18–60 and restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore it must be excluded.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of short-term source memory/working memory and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates. It therefore meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample includes older adults with mean age 67.4 years (participants clearly >60 years), so it violates exclusion criterion E8 (participants outside the age range 18–60). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite satisfying all other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Study uses task-based fMRI of the Stroop task (executive function/inhibition) and reports within-participant contrasts, but the provided content is only title/abstract (full text incomplete). Crucially, the sample includes older participants aged 60–75, i.e., outside the review age range (18–60), meeting exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met based on available info: I5 (fMRI assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts of task conditions), I9 (task is an inhibition/executive domain). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable from provided content: I7 (cannot confirm group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps from abstract alone), I10 (the abstract reports ages and imaging modality but does not explicitly confirm the sample is healthy or provide full participant/clinical details). Because E8 is met and the full text is incomplete, the study should be excluded.

Only the title and abstract are provided (no methods, full results, or tables/coordinates), so the full text is incomplete. From the abstract we can confirm this is a PET study of the Stroop task in normal subjects (meets I5 and I9). However, key inclusion criteria cannot be verified in the available text: no clear report of a within-participant contrast versus an active control (I6 not confirmed), no confirmation of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map or coordinate reporting (I7 and I8 not confirmed), and participant age information is not provided (I10 not confirmed). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met based on the abstract. Because the full text is incomplete and several required inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: the study is a PET task-based investigation of inhibition using the Hayling test, so it meets I5 (PET executive-function task), I6 (within-participant contrast between response initiation and inhibition conditions), and I9 (task maps to inhibition executive domain). However, the full article text is not provided, so I cannot confirm I7 (presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map) or I8 (clear reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures), nor I10 (reporting of participant age and confirmation of healthy adult sample). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are explicitly met based on the abstract alone. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

Full text provided appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). Exclusion criterion E8 applies: the study includes mild traumatic brain injury (MTBI) patients and healthy controls, so the sample is not restricted to healthy individuals. Inclusion criteria met based on the abstract: I5 (task-based fMRI study of an executive function—working memory n-back), I6 (within-participant contrasts across n-back loads using an active 0-back control), and I9 (working memory is an established executive function domain). Inclusion criteria not met / could not be verified from the provided content: I7 (presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is not confirmed in the abstract) and I10 (relevant participant age and explicit confirmation of a healthy-only sample are not reported in the abstract). Because the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (E8) and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded.

This fMRI study uses a classic executive function task (counting Stroop; inhibition/interference) with healthy adults (n=16, ages 19–34), reports task contrasts (number Stroop vs neutral Stroop) as within-subject comparisons, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation results (thresholds and Talairach coordinates). The paper provides participant age range, healthy sample confirmation, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. There is an active control condition (neutral Stroop) used for the critical contrast. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes active control, empirical fMRI data, ages within 18–60). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

The abstract describes an fMRI study in young healthy adults comparing rule-based versus similarity-based categorization (within-participant active-task contrast) and reports regional brain activations. Based on the abstract we can confirm fMRI modality, within-subject active contrasts, and reporting of participant group as young adults. However the provided content is only title/abstract/metadata (full text not supplied), so I cannot verify whether group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps or coordinate tables were reported (I7/I8), nor fully confirm that the tasks are formally within established executive-function domains per inclusion definition (I9). Because the full text is incomplete and critical inclusion criterion I7 cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending full-text review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met from the abstract alone.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults with within-subject contrasts (MAT vs PREP/EXEC). However, the reported analyses are primarily ROI-based (functional ROIs and ROI statistics) with no clear group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinates presented for the main contrasts in the provided full text. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Exclusion applied: E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI working memory/executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts), I9 (task falls within executive function domain), I10 (participant age/health/imaging and task details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map not reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy young adults (ages 20–39). It reports within-subject task contrasts (encoding/delay/response periods and modality comparisons such as spatial vs object), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with stereotactic coordinates reported. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group patient contrasts, and the paper provides task-based contrasts beyond simple rest/fixation (including task-type contrasts). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that tests a cognitive control (reappraisal/distancing) manipulation in a task-based paradigm (monetary incentive delay with permit vs distance blocks). It reports within-subject contrasts of reappraisal versus permit (Distance > Permit and related contrasts) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (reappraisal network activations reported with coordinates and thresholds), as well as ROI and whole-brain analyses. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task methods are all provided. The reappraisal manipulation involves inhibition/control processes consistent with executive-function domains (inhibition/cognitive control). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control, empirical data in healthy adults within age range). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The abstract reports an event-related fMRI study of conflict tasks with within-subject incongruent vs congruent contrasts in 12 participants (meets I5, I6, I9). However the provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata), so I cannot verify that a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map was reported (I7) nor can I confirm participant ages and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are directly met based on available information. Because ALL inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=12, mean age 24) that examines reasoning and maintenance (working memory). It reports within-subject contrasts including reasoning versus maintenance (an active control) and maintenance versus rest, analyzed with whole-brain voxelwise SPM99 GLM and cluster-level corrected inferences; coordinates and cluster sizes are provided. Tasks fall within executive function domains (working memory and manipulation/integration), and participant health, age, modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From available information: meets I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory/executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs control conditions matched for difficulty), and I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory). However I7 (presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) cannot be confirmed from the provided content, and I10 (reporting of participant age and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample) is not reported in the abstract/metadata.
