Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I7 and/or I10) cannot be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met based on the available information.

This is an empirical fMRI study of verbal working memory (a recognized executive function domain). It reports within-subject contrasts (L6 vs L1) targeting delay-period rehearsal, includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group results reported for BA6/premotor cortex), and provides participant age range, healthy status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy samples) are met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not report any whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI activation maps or voxelwise group analyses required by the meta-analysis (I7 not met). It is primarily a behavioral comparison of performance inside vs outside the scanner; no within-participant fMRI contrasts of an executive task vs an active control are reported (I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study using working memory/long-term memory tasks), I9 (tasks fall within executive-function domain: working memory), I10 (participant ages, health status, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Exclusion criterion met: E8 — study includes elderly participants outside the 18–60 age range. Therefore the paper fails required imaging-analysis criteria and includes out-of-range participants, so it cannot be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (2-back) in healthy young adults (ages 18–22). It reports a within-participant contrast of ‘2-Back minus Match to Centre’ (an active control), and performs group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and corrected results (reported in text/tables/ROIs). Imaging modality, participant ages, health status (exclusion of Axis I diagnoses), and task paradigm are described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation, uses an active control, is empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete.

This study meets several inclusion criteria (I5: fMRI working-memory executive task; I6: within-subject contrasts 5t vs Arrows and 5t vs 2t; I9: working memory is an executive domain; I10: participant screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described). However, it does not provide a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map: data were acquired over limited frontal slices and the analyses focus on ROI-derived indices (DLPFC masks and a slice-based control region). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level map) and instead meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI-focused analyses/no whole-brain results). Additionally, the study includes a clinical sample (schizophrenic patients) and is not restricted to healthy participants, which meets exclusion criterion E8. Because any single unmet inclusion criterion or met exclusion criterion requires exclusion, I exclude this study.

This fMRI study used a within-subject semantic association task contrasted against an active letter-matching control, reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation (SPM) with listed activation clusters/peak voxels. Although the primary task is lexico-semantic, the paradigm explicitly requires short-term maintenance of nouns (verbal working memory) and the authors discuss working-memory demands as a likely contributor to inferior frontal activation. Thus the task falls within an executive function domain (working memory), includes a within-participant task vs active control contrast, reports whole-brain group analyses (coordinates/tables), and provides participant age/health, imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, participants are healthy adults 21–30). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI, event-related Stroop study in healthy-sounding adult volunteers and meets multiple inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9). However the full text does not report participant ages nor an explicit statement confirming the sample is restricted to healthy individuals, which is required by I10. All other inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Because I10 is not met (missing age and explicit healthy-sample confirmation), the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in healthy adults with within-subject contrasts versus an active 0-back control, and reports participant demographics and task details. However, the paper reports results using anatomically defined VOIs/ROIs and percentage signal changes; it does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (nor coordinate tables or whole-brain figures) needed for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive-function task), I6 (within-participant task vs active control), I9 (working memory task within executive domains), I10 (participant age/health/imaging/task reported). Inclusion criterion I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (response selection and inhibition) in healthy adults (N=12, mean age 26.2). The within-subject design includes contrasts of cognitive-control versus automatic conditions (SRRT and Go/NoGo variants), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (cluster-based thresholding, tables/coordinates and regional results). Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly examines deception, a task involving cognitive control and inhibition. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (lie > truth; lie > control) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with voxelwise thresholds, and provides participant age range and health screening, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. An active control condition (10♠) was used. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy and aged 23–48). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Only the article abstract and metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract: this is a PET study using an N-back verbal working memory task in healthy volunteers, indicating imaging modality and task domain (I5, I9) and within-participant contrasts across N-back levels including an active 0-back control (I6). However, the available content does not allow verification that group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported (I7) nor confirm that participant ages and full healthy-sample details are reported (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are demonstrably met based on the abstract. Because core full-text material (methods/results/discussion) is missing, I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria; therefore I exclude pending retrieval of the full text.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that includes within-subject contrasts of an executive function task (working memory) versus an active control (W–C; also T–C, T–W) (I6). Analyses were conducted at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise SPM maps and thresholds reported (I7,I8). The tasks include working memory (an established executive domain) and detailed task paradigms are described (I9). Participant details (healthy adults, mean age 25.8), imaging modality (fMRI), and methods are reported (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not connectivity-only, include within-group contrasts, use active control tasks, are empirical with original human data, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 26–55) using a Go/NoGo inhibition paradigm (an executive function task). The paper reports within-subject, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g. false alarms–hits; correct rejections–hits) analyzed with SPM99 and presents whole-brain results (and coordinate/cluster-focused analyses). Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are all reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of an executive function (working memory) using a task-based n-back paradigm in healthy adults (age 18–55). It reports within-subject contrasts (2-back > 0-back) comparing an executive condition to an active control (0-back). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded (family-wise error correction) and activation differences are described in the text with MNI coordinates. Participant characteristics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (executive function) in healthy adults (24 subjects; Experiment 1; plus 6 in Experiment 2) meeting age and health criteria. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., Delay Forward 5 − Delay Forward 2) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SNGA second-level GLM with MNI coordinates and thresholded maps described). Results and coordinates are reported in the full text. The task falls within the working memory executive domain, participant and imaging details are provided, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active task contrasts). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (N-back and item-recognition) in healthy adults (ages 18–37). Working memory is an executive function domain. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., 3-back vs 0-back; high- vs low-load; verbal vs nonverbal; rehearse vs detect) using active control conditions (0-back, detect) and fixation, and performs group-level voxelwise (whole-brain) ANOVAs and reports coordinates and results. Participant characteristics, imaging modality (1.5T and 3T fMRI), task paradigms, and full methods/results/discussion are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or between-group-only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (executive function) in healthy adults (ages 19–37). It reports within-participant task contrasts (e.g., remember scenes vs remember faces; remember vs passive view; reward-level contrasts) and presents group-level whole-brain activation results (reported at FDR p<0.05) alongside ROI analyses. Imaging modality, participant demographics/health status, and task paradigm are described in detail. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

Only abstract-level/fulltext header content provided; full article (methods, participants, results details) not available. Inclusion criteria met based on provided content: I5 (task-based BOLD fMRI of attentional control/task switching), I6 (within-participant contrasts across cue/target conditions are described), I9 (task switching = cognitive flexibility within executive function). Inclusion criteria not verifiable/not met from available text: I7 (no explicit statement that group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps were reported), I10 (participant ages and explicit confirmation of healthy sample not reported in the provided text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) can be confirmed from the available material. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify critical requirements (I7, I10), so I exclude pending full-text access.

The provided content is limited to title/abstract/metadata and lacks full methods, results, and participant details. Abstract indicates a PET Stroop task with within-subject contrasts against active control conditions, so I5 (PET study of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts), and I9 (Stroop = inhibition) are met. However I cannot confirm I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps) or I8 (presence/reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures) nor I10 (participant ages and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample) from the material provided. Per screening rules, full text is incomplete and not all inclusion criteria can be verified; therefore the study is excluded pending full-text review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met based on the abstract alone.

Although the study meets multiple inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (task-based fMRI of executive function with within-subject contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses reported for healthy controls), it also includes a clinical sample (bipolar disorder patients) and is not restricted to healthy adults only. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded despite reporting within-group whole-brain activations in the healthy control subgroup.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–38) using a task that manipulates cognitive control/inhibition (HC vs LC) and incentives. It includes within-participant contrasts of task conditions (e.g., High Control vs Low Control) and incentive conditions, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (F maps, cluster correction, and tables/coordinates referenced in supplemental material). Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active task contrasts, empirical with healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults (meets I5, I9, I10). However, it does not report group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps: analyses were ROI-based (authors state no statistical maps were created), so I7 is not met and exclusion E3 applies. The study also models task periods relative to an inter-trial interval/rest baseline (ITI) rather than an active control task, so I6 is not met and exclusion E6 applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it fails required whole-brain and active-control contrast criteria.

Abstract indicates an fMRI study of a spatial working memory (an executive function) task in healthy adults and reports group-level statistical maps across sites. However, the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). I cannot confirm: (1) whether analyses include a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (I6), and (2) whether participant age information is reported (I10). Based on available information I5, I7, I8, and I9 appear satisfied, but I6 and I10 are not verifiable from the incomplete text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met from the abstract. Therefore I exclude this record pending access to the full article.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (Sternberg) — an executive function domain — reporting within-group (healthy control) whole-brain, group-level random-effects activation maps and coordinate results. The paper provides full methods, participant ages and healthy control screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm details. The within-participant contrasts include retrieval-related activation (contrasted against baseline containing incorrect responses) analyzed at the whole-brain level, with results reported in tables/coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy activation maps, baseline isn’t solely rest/fixation, and participants include a healthy adult sample within typical age range). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it includes a clinical sample (drug-free patients with major depressive disorder) and thus is not restricted to healthy individuals (Exclusion E8). It does meet multiple inclusion criteria relevant to the review: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function Stroop task), I6 (within-subject incongruent vs congruent contrasts), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results reported), I8 (coordinates and descriptions provided), I9 (task falls under inhibition/cognitive control), and I10 (participant age range, healthy control details, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). No other exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

This paper is primarily a computational modeling study that describes an event-related fMRI design and notes that 10 healthy subjects were scanned; however, no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical results or within-participant contrasts are reported (data analysis is stated to be ongoing). Therefore it does not satisfy the review’s requirement for reported within-subject task contrasts and whole-brain group maps. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study design with task), I9 (tasks are executive: working memory/WCST), I10 (participant age range, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported within-participant contrasts/results), I7 (no group-level whole-brain statistical maps or coordinate results reported). No exclusion criteria strictly apply (e.g., it is not solely an ROI or connectivity paper), but it must be excluded because required inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met.

This fMRI study of a 2-Back working memory task meets the review’s inclusion requirements for modality and task: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast: 2-Back vs 0-Back active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and paired t-tests reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures), I9 (working memory is an established executive function domain), and I10 (participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). However, it violates Exclusion Criterion E8: the sample age range includes participants older than 60 years (reported age range 18–80), so the study is ineligible for inclusion. No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function). It reports within-subject contrasts of WM task delay periods versus an active sensorimotor control, and presents voxelwise whole-brain group-level analyses (thresholded Z maps, corrected for multiple comparisons) with regional/localization details. Participant demographics (healthy adults, mean age 25, range 18–45), imaging modality (fMRI), and full task paradigms are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses an active control, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study using a visual N-BACK working memory task (executive function domain) in healthy adults (N=12, mean age 26.9). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of task levels (1-,2-,3-BACK) versus 0-BACK (active control) and group-level voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise repeated-measures ANOVAs, Talairach-transformed maps, cluster thresholds). Participant demographics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active control, empirical human fMRI data, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adult volunteers (mean age 36) assessing executive functions (spatial working memory and planning). It uses within-participant task vs active control contrasts (two-back and Tower of London rehearsal/planning vs control conditions), and reports group-level voxelwise SPM99 analyses across the whole brain with coordinates and figures (including thresholding and cluster results). Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (PET), and detailed task paradigms are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses PET to measure attention during a task, so it meets I5 (PET/task-based study) and I9 (task = vigilance/attention). However, the available content is limited to title/abstract (fulltext_incomplete=true). Crucially, the sample includes PTSD patients with substance abuse and a normal control group (i.e., not restricted to healthy participants), which violates exclusion criterion E8. From the abstract we cannot confirm a within-participant contrast against an active control condition (I6), nor can we confirm that group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps were reported (I7/I8). Participant age and clear confirmation of a healthy sample are not fully reported in the provided text (I10). Therefore the study is excluded. Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata).

This study is excluded because it includes participants outside the target age range (senior adults aged 60–80), meeting exclusion criterion E8. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control/selection), I6 (within-participant contrasts, e.g., MANY vs FEW and generate vs read), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with FDR correction), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/coordinates), I9 (task taps executive function/selection domain), and I10 (reports participant ages, health screening, imaging modality, and task details). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 were satisfied). Full text appears complete. Because the sample includes participants outside the 18–60 age range, the study does not meet the age restriction for this meta-analysis and must be excluded per E8.

This fMRI study uses an n-back working-memory task (an executive function domain) with within-subject contrasts (2-back>0-back, 1-back>0-back, 0-back>rest) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster coordinates. Healthy control participants (aged 18–60) are included and within-group task contrasts for controls are reported (e.g., age effects during 2-back>0-back), with results presented as coordinates and described in text. Imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant age/health status are clearly reported. Although the paper also includes a patient group, the healthy adult within-group whole-brain activation contrasts satisfy the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study is an fMRI task assessing attention/cognitive control (meets I5) and includes within-participant contrasts (attention to action vs diverted/unattended; meets I6). The task falls within attentional/cognitive-control domains (meets I9). However, the full text lacks sufficient information to verify key inclusion criteria: (a) no access to group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps or clear reporting of whole-brain results (I7 cannot be confirmed), and (b) participant age is not reported in the available content so I10 cannot be confirmed. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm whether whole-brain activation maps were reported or whether all participant/sample details were provided; per screening rules this prevents inclusion. No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on the available content.

This fMRI study of a working memory (SIRP) task meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts including load 5 vs load 1), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (working memory is an executive function), and I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). However, the sample includes participants aged 30–63, i.e., at least one participant older than 60 (age 63), violating exclusion criterion E8 (participants outside the 18–60 age range). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study is excluded based on E8.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (N-back) in healthy adults and meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (within-participant contrasts across N-back conditions), I9 (working memory task within executive function domain), and I10 (reports participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task). However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical activation maps; the paper focuses on functional connectivity analyses (network/correlation-based measures) rather than voxelwise activation results. Therefore I7 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps) is not met. Additionally, the sample includes older adults outside the 18–60 range (mean age 68.2, range 30–89), violating E8. Because it reports only connectivity analyses without whole-brain activation maps (E4) and includes participants outside the allowed age range (E8), the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (ages ~19–25), reporting participant demographics and imaging details. The paper reports within-subject contrasts including manipulation > maintenance (i.e., an active task-vs-task contrast), as well as delay/maintenance/manipulation contrasts, satisfying the requirement for a within-participant contrast against an active control. Group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) mixed-effects analyses are reported and thresholded (cluster-corrected), and results are described in the text with coordinates and tables/figures indicated. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., the study does not report only ROI or connectivity analyses, and it does not use fixation/rest as the only baseline since it includes task-vs-task contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The abstract shows an fMRI working-memory load manipulation with within-subject contrasts (3 vs 1, 6 vs 1) and reports regional activations, so I5 (fMRI, executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrasts), and I9 (working memory is an executive domain) are satisfied. However, the provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata). Key inclusion criteria cannot be verified: I7 (presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map) is not confirmable from the abstract alone, and I10 (reported participant ages and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample) is incomplete (only “six subjects” listed; no ages/health status). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met based on available information. Because not all inclusion criteria can be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending full-text availability.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract metadata provided). From the abstract: this is an fMRI study of verbal working memory (n-back) in healthy volunteers, so it meets I5 (fMRI executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrasts across n-back levels), and I9 (working memory task). However, the paper reports path analysis/connectivity modeling of seven selected regions and does not provide evidence in the abstract of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map (I7 not confirmed). Participant ages are not reported in the provided content (I10 not confirmed). Because the study appears to report only connectivity/ROI-based analyses without whole-brain task activation maps, it meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text is incomplete, preventing confirmation of whole-brain results or ages; therefore excluded pending full-text review.

Full text provided appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata (no methods, full results, or figures), so key criteria cannot be verified. Inclusion criteria met based on abstract: I5 (PET Stroop task assessing cognitive control), I6 (within-participant contrasts reported: incongruent vs congruent and comparisons to control states), and I9 (Stroop is an inhibition/selective attention executive function task). Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed: I7 (cannot verify presence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps from the incomplete full text), I10 (participant age not reported in abstract; full sample age information cannot be confirmed). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met based on available abstract. Because I7 and I10 are required and cannot be confirmed from the supplied content, the study must be excluded pending provision of the complete full text.

This study is excluded because it includes participants outside the target adult age range (ages 12–40, i.e., includes participants <18), violating exclusion criterion E8. The paper otherwise meets inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive functions: inhibition and motor timing), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs active control conditions), I7 (voxelwise, whole-brain analyses and voxel-level statistics), I8 (results reported as coordinates and maps), I9 (tasks fall within executive domains, e.g., inhibition), and I10 (reports ages, healthy sample status, fMRI modality, and task details). Inclusion IDs not met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (Sternberg), an executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts of memory load (6-digit vs 2-digit), group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with correction, and presents results in figures/text. Participants are healthy adults with ages reported (23–35). All required study details (methods, results, discussion) are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because study does not provide a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical activation map required by I7. Instead, results are reported qualitatively as ROI activations and counts of subjects activating each region (i.e., effectively ROI/subject-count reporting), meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive/planning-related sequencing), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs an active control non-word condition), I9 (task maps onto executive domain: planning/sequence), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality and paradigm adequately reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map reported). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusion.

Full text provided is limited to title/abstract/metadata only (no full methods, results, or participant details). Based on available information: inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function via working memory) and I9 (task within executive function domains: working memory) are satisfied. However I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), I8 (confirmation that whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats), and I10 (participant ages and confirmation of healthy sample) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. Additionally, it is not possible to rule out exclusion E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline) without methods. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify key inclusion criteria; therefore the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This study uses task-based fMRI of working memory (PASAT) and reports connectivity analyses in both patients (CISSMS) and controls, but it does not meet several required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (task uses rest/fixation baseline with no active control condition described), E4 (primary reported results are effective connectivity/SEM analyses rather than whole-brain task activation maps), and E8 (sample includes patients; study is not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (fMRI study of executive function/working memory), I9 (task falls within executive function domain—working memory), I10 (reports participant/sample characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast reported against an active control condition), I7 (no clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps provided in the text), I8 (no coordinates/tables of whole-brain results presented). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not report a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map (analyses were limited to ROI-based tests and voxelwise SPM restricted to a subset of axial slices), thus meeting exclusion criterion E3 and failing inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain evidence). Additionally, the task (prepulse inhibition / attentional modulation of startle) is a sensorimotor gating paradigm and is not clearly within a standard executive-function domain required by I9. The study does meet I5 (task-based fMRI examining attentional/cognitive-control processes), I6 (within-subject contrasts: attended vs ignored vs startle-alone), and I10 (reports participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion: E8 applies — the study includes schizophrenia patients and unaffected co-twins in addition to healthy controls, so the sample is not restricted to healthy adults required by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I6 (within-subject contrasts using load 3 as an active baseline), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results and ROIs described/localized), I9 (task falls within executive function — working memory), I10 (reports imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant characterization). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 are satisfied). Full text appears complete.

Full text provided is limited to title and abstract only (fulltext_incomplete=true). Based on the abstract, this is an fMRI study of stimulus-response incompatibility involving inhibition/working memory, and within-subject contrasts (mixed vs compatible tasks) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I9 are met. However, the full text is incomplete and does not provide necessary information to confirm a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map (I7) or detailed participant information (age range, healthy sample) and full task/method details (I10). No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the abstract. Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending retrieval of the full article.

Exclusion(s) met: E6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported via SPM conjunction analysis), I8 (whole-brain results described with coordinates/figures and comparisons), I9 (some tasks included fall within executive function domains — e.g., spatial working memory, mental calculation, reasoning), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigms are reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (the study’s primary aim is characterizing the conscious resting state, not primarily to assess executive function/cognitive control tasks), I6 (no within-participant contrast presented that tests an executive function task relative to an active control condition — the paper focuses on REST vs task contrasts and reports conjunctions of REST>task rather than task>active-control contrasts). Because I6 is not satisfied and the study’s analyses center on REST baselines rather than providing within-subject task>active-control executive contrasts, it does not meet the review’s required design and is excluded.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of working memory training in healthy young adults and meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (working memory); (I6) reports within-participant task contrasts (WM task vs active baseline, and Time-by-Task interaction within subjects); (I7) includes a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analysis using SPM99 with cluster-level correction reported; (I8) whole-brain results are described in the text (and figures/tables in the paper); (I9) the task is working memory, an established executive function domain; (I10) participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical study, or out-of-range/unhealthy participants). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E8 met: study includes a clinical sample (bipolar manic patients) and is not restricted to healthy individuals, so it does not meet the review’s requirement for studies of healthy adults only. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrasts: emotion-labeling vs control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I10 (participant ages, healthy control description, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 and I9 — the paradigm is an affective emotion-labeling task (emotion regulation/perception), not an established executive function/cognitive control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation), so it fails to meet the meta-analysis scope. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for not matching the population criterion and for the task falling outside defined executive-function domains.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (N-back) comparing young and older healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps (meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, it includes participants older than 60 years (older group range up to 74 years), violating exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60). Therefore the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8 (participants include ages outside the allowed 18–60 range: sample ages 51–72, with participants up to 72 years). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function – N-back), I6 (within-participant contrast: 3-back vs 0-back), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/clusters), I9 (task is working memory, an executive function), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 are satisfied). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely due to E8.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults: it is a task-based fMRI study of an executive function domain (inhibition; Go/NoGo) (I5, I9); it reports a within-participant contrast of correct NoGo minus correct Go (active control) (I6); group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported using SPM99 with cluster/voxel thresholds and coordinates provided (I7, I8); and relevant participant information (healthy control group demographics and imaging modality and task details) is reported (I10). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing extraction of whole-brain activation coordinates for healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy contrasts).

This fMRI study uses a Stroop (inhibition) task in healthy adults and reports age, modality, and task details; however the task contrast is incongruent blocks versus fixation (rest) rather than an active control condition. Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast against an active control) is not met. Because the study uses rest/fixation as the only baseline, exclusion criterion E6 applies. The paper does report group-level coordinates (whole-brain group analysis) and other required details (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 are satisfied), but the lack of an active control contrast prevents inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (ages 19–41) that reports within-participant contrasts of task demand (6-letter > 2-letter set-size contrasts and trial-period effects). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (2×3 ANOVA) with cluster correction are reported, and results are described with Talairach coordinates and figures. Participant health screening, ages, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and participants are healthy adults). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI/EEG study of working memory in healthy adults (ages reported 18–25), so it addresses executive function (I5) and reports participant demographics and imaging modality (I10), and the task is working memory (I9). However, the neuroimaging results are reported as subject-specific ROI-based analyses and ROI-derived time-course statistics; no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or group voxelwise coordinates/figures are presented for inclusion in a coordinate-based whole-brain meta-analysis. Therefore it violates E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). In particular, inclusion criteria I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map) is not met; I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control) is also not clearly satisfied because primary localization contrasts use unmodeled ITI baseline (rest) and analyses focus on ROI/time-course contrasts rather than whole-brain task vs active-control contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based event-related fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) that includes a healthy control group (n=16). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses: ICA-derived task-related components were subjected to voxelwise one-sample t-tests (within-group maps) and two-sample t-tests (between-group comparisons) with multiple-comparison correction, and results are reported in text/tables/coordinates. An active control condition (three X's) was used. Participant/sample information, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. Analyses are not ROI-only nor resting-state-only; within-group healthy control task maps are available. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion met: E8 (study includes patient participants with frontotemporal dementia and healthy seniors likely older than 60; sample is not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study with an executive component—working memory demand), I6 (within-participant contrasts reported for task vs active control baseline), I7 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (coordinates/peak loci reported in tables/figures), I9 (task taps working memory, an established executive domain), I10 (reports imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant group descriptions and age info referenced). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable inclusion criteria present for healthy group). Final decision: EXCLUDE because the study sample is not restricted to healthy adults within the 18–60 age range and includes clinical patients, violating E8, so it does not meet the meta-analysis participant requirements.

This PET study reports task-based executive-function (2-back working memory) effects in healthy adults. It used an active control (0-back) with within-subject contrasts, and conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM96 with cluster/voxel thresholds and reported distributed activations/deactivations. Participant age, health status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active control, healthy adults aged 18–60).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided), so key inclusion criteria cannot be verified. Inclusion criteria met based on available information: I5 (task-based fMRI of verbal working memory) and I9 (working memory is an established executive function domain). Inclusion criteria not verifiable / not met from available text: I6 (no clear evidence of a within-participant contrast versus an active control condition), I7 (no explicit confirmation of group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps—abstract mentions linear regression to locate activation but full methods/results are missing), I10 (participant age and clear confirmation of a healthy sample are not reported in the provided text). No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on the available information: []. Because the full text is not provided, I cannot confirm all required criteria; per screening rules this leads to exclusion pending full text review.

This is an fMRI study of a stop-signal task (response inhibition), an executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., stop error (SE) vs stop success (SS), SE/SS vs go), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and reports MNI coordinates, and provides participant details (40 healthy adults, age 22–42), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm. All inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not truncated.

This PET study investigates verbal working memory (an executive function) using task-based paradigms and includes within-subject contrasts (serial recall vs serial repetition and interaction contrasts comparing single vs multiple irrelevant speech) at the group level. The analysis used whole-brain voxelwise SPM99 fixed-effects analyses and reports coordinate results; participant demographics (healthy adults aged 20–31), imaging modality (PET), and detailed task paradigms are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or unhealthy/out-of-age-range participants) are met. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (2-back CPT) in healthy adults that reports within-subject contrasts (2-back vs 0-back) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with peak coordinates (left BA10). Participant ages (18–55, mean 24.7), healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function whole-brain activation in healthy adults and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a PET study of syntactic sentence comprehension (plausibility judgments contrasting syntactically complex vs simple sentences) in healthy young adults. While it reports within-subject contrasts (SO vs OS), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, coordinate tables, and necessary participant/imaging details, it does not target executive function or cognitive control domains per se. The imaging task is language/syntactic processing rather than an established executive function task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I9. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a methods/empirical fMRI study that includes a verbal working memory contrast and group-level whole-brain analyses, reports participant demographics and methods. However the key within-participant contrast for the executive task is against rest/fixation rather than an active control condition. Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control) is not met, and exclusion criterion E6 (rest or fixation as the only baseline without an active control) applies. Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes an executive working-memory paradigm with within-subject contrasts against an active control (5-digit memory vs arrow control), and reports participant demographics and imaging modality. However, the analyses reported are ROI-based with small-volume corrections and region-wise voxel counts/BOLD magnitudes; the manuscript does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain coordinate tables. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text provided is incomplete (only title and abstract). Abstract indicates an fMRI study comparing two motor tasks that did/did not require sustained attention and reports a differential ACC response. From the abstract we can confirm: I5 (fMRI study of cognitive processing), I6 (within-participant contrast between two task conditions), and I9 (task involves sustained attention/vigilance). However the full text is not available to verify critical required details: I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) and I10 (participant age range and confirmation of healthy sample). Because not all inclusion criteria can be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study cannot be confidently included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met based on the abstract. Full text incomplete prevents confirmation of whole-brain results and participant/sample details required by the review.

Full text reports an fMRI group-level whole-brain analysis and provides participant age/health and task paradigm details, but it used fixation (rest) as the baseline with no active control condition. Exclusion criterion E6 applies (rest/fixation was the only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain results reported) and I10 (participant age/health, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition; only fixation baseline used), I9 (tasks are deductive reasoning problems rather than clearly falling within established executive function domains such as working memory/inhibition/planning—while the paper discusses working-memory components, the primary task is reasoning), and I5 (the study does not explicitly target executive function/cognitive control tasks per the meta-analysis scope). Therefore the study is excluded.

All required inclusion criteria are satisfied. The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of a visual oddball paradigm that probes attention/vigilance and working-memory rehearsal (I5, I9). Analyses use within-participant contrasts (target vs frequent standard events) and report within-group activation maps (I6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were computed using permutation-based inference and corrections for multiple comparisons (I7, I8). Participant details (ages 21–30), healthy sample status (no personal medical/psychiatric history), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported (I10). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

Excluded under E4: the paper reports resting-state/functional connectivity analyses (ICA, partial correlations) and compares network connectivity during rest vs a continuous 2-back task but does not present a within-participant contrast of task vs an active control nor a group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study including a working-memory task), I9 (working memory is an established executive function domain), I10 (participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Therefore the study must be excluded.

Full text incomplete: only title/abstract/metadata available. From the abstract, this is an empirical event-related fMRI study of working memory (meets I5 and I9). However, the full text is not provided so I cannot verify: I6 (presence of a within-participant contrast against an active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), or I10 (participant ages and confirmation of a healthy sample). No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on the available information. Excluded pending retrieval of the full text to confirm remaining inclusion criteria.

Excluded because study reports only region-of-interest (ROI)-based analyses rather than group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (meets exclusion E3), and the participant age range reported (18–65 years) extends beyond the allowed 18–60 range (meets exclusion E8). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: Stroop, response inhibition, Sternberg), I6 (within-participant contrasts: Incongruent vs Congruent; No-Go vs Go; Retain6 vs Retain2), I9 (tasks are established executive domains: inhibition, working memory), and I10 (reports participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task details). Inclusion criterion I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study uses a continuous performance task (vigilance) in healthy adults and patients (OA), so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/vigilance), I6 (within-participant task contrasts across CPT conditions), I9 (task falls under vigilance), and I10 (participant ages, health status, imaging modality and paradigm are reported). However, all neuroimaging analyses were performed within a hand-drawn ACC region-of-interest (ICA within the ACC) and no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinates are reported — therefore it fails I7 and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results). Additionally, the sample includes participants older than 60 (range up to 65) and includes a patient group (not restricted to healthy-only), violating E8. Because it violates required whole-brain reporting and the age/health restriction, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 18–31) using within-subject manipulations of feature (color, shape, both) and VWM load (set size 1–7). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analysis (Task > fixation, P < 0.05 corrected) used to identify ROI centers, and it presents within-participant contrasts across feature conditions and set sizes (load effects). Imaging modality, participant health/age, and task paradigm are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI executive-function task, within-subject contrasts (feature and load), whole-brain group-level results (reported/described), and required reporting details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, participants are healthy and within age range, and the study reports active task conditions beyond fixation). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on available abstract: this is a PET case study using WCST with an injured twin and uninjured cotwin; it reports within-participant WCST vs sensorimotor control contrasts and identifies differences in two regions. However, no evidence of a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map in healthy adults is available, and results are reported for limited regions suggesting ROI-based analyses. The sample includes at least one brain-injured participant (not restricted to healthy adults). Therefore it cannot be included for a meta-analysis of whole-brain task activations in healthy adults.

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adults that explicitly probes spatial working memory/planning and executive processes (covered maze). It includes within-subject contrasts of experimental conditions against active control tasks (motor control, visual control). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise SPM results reported with coordinates and Z-values. Participant demographics and health screening, imaging modality (H2 15O PET), and detailed task paradigms are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, active controls used, healthy adults 18–28).

Excluded because the task is a simple visually-guided saccade vs fixation paradigm and does not probe an established executive function domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility) nor an active control condition. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study uses fixation/rest as the only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I8 (coordinates/whole-brain results clearly reported), I10 (healthy adult participants, imaging modality and task described). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not an executive function task as defined), I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition), I9 (task does not fall within listed executive function domains). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only chapter title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: the study used fMRI of a Stroop task in healthy adults (meets I5 and I9). However, I cannot verify key required criteria: (I6) explicit within-participant contrast vs an active control condition is not fully described in the abstract; (I7) confirmation of a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map is implied but not verifiable from the provided text; (I10) participant age range and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample are not reported in the abstract. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met from the available material. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded at this stage. Recommend obtaining the complete chapter/text to reassess inclusion once methods and results are available.

Exclusion: E8 (participants outside the 18–60 age range) — the methods report mean age 17.4 years (SD 14.2), indicating the sample includes minors/outside the eligible adult range. Inclusion met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with cluster-level FWE correction), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures), I10 (participant characteristics, healthy status, imaging modality [fMRI], and task paradigm reported). Inclusion NOT met: I5 (study does not assess an established executive function/cognitive control task; main paradigm is a lexical decision/action-word processing task), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition — contrasts are linguistic/lexical: verbs vs pseudo-verbs and Do vs Don't), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, set-shifting, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Because E8 is met and key inclusion criteria for executive-function-focused meta-analysis (I5,I6,I9) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study of picture–word interference (orthographic/phonological facilitation) in overt naming. While it reports whole-brain BOLD increases and decreases (satisfying I7 and I8), the task is a language production/lexical retrieval paradigm, not a standard executive function task. The available content is limited (abstract/metadata only) so participant ages and explicit confirmation of a healthy adult sample are not provided. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not clearly assess executive function/cognitive control), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains), I10 (insufficient reporting of participant age/healthy status in provided text). No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 are clearly met based on available text. Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata), preventing definitive determination of sample details or possible secondary analyses. Excluded on that basis and lack of alignment with executive-function task inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adults (ages 19–36) using the Hayling Test (initiation and suppression), an established executive-function paradigm. It reports within-subject contrasts of executive conditions versus an active control (reading) and rest, and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with thresholding and corrected inference. Relevant participant, imaging modality (PET), and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, includes active control, empirical, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study of executive function (central executive/manipulation of working memory) using task-based paradigms with within-subject contrasts (manipulation vs serial tasks, reading vs recall) against active control conditions. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) were performed and reported (thresholds, locations/BA reported). Tasks fall within executive function domain (working memory manipulation). Participant characteristics (age 20–26, healthy), imaging modality (PET), and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range participants) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided), so key inclusion criteria cannot be verified. Inclusion met: I5 (fMRI study of working memory—an executive function) and I9 (task falls within working memory domain). Inclusion not met / cannot be confirmed: I6 (no clear report of a within-participant contrast versus an active control in the provided content), I7 (no confirmation of group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps), I8 (unclear whether whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/figures described in text), I10 (participant age/health/sample details not provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met from the available text. Because the full text is incomplete, I must exclude this study pending full-text verification.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory (meets I5, I9) reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and maps (meets I7, I8) and providing participant age/health/imaging/task details (meets I10). However, the sample includes older adults aged 65–84 (participants outside 18–60), violating exclusion criterion E8. Additionally, the study does not use an active control condition for task-vs-control contrasts (contrasts are load-dependent within-task and relative to blank/rest baseline), so inclusion criterion I6 (task vs active control) is not clearly satisfied. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded (E8).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults using a visual oddball (target detection) task that falls within the executive domain of vigilance/attention. The analysis includes a within-participant contrast (target-related BOLD response vs baseline/non-targets as modeled by a target regressor), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were produced (FLAME, cluster-corrected Z-maps). Participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, active task baseline present, empirical fMRI data in healthy 18–60 y adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10.

This fMRI study reports task-based working memory (2-back/0-back) contrasts in healthy adults and unmedicated schizophrenia patients. It provides within-participant contrasts (e.g., 2-back > 0-back and 2-back degraded > 0-back degraded), and group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses for the healthy control group (SPM maps explored and results reported, with coordinates/tables). The task (working memory) falls within an established executive function domain, imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described, and participant characteristics (healthy control group, exclusion criteria, age-matching) are reported. No exclusion criteria from the review (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-group healthy contrasts, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or clearly out-of-range/non-healthy samples) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/abstract-level information). While the abstract indicates an event-related fMRI study of working memory (satisfying I5) and the task falls within executive function (working memory), I cannot confirm other required items. The full text does not provide details to verify: (I6) that at least one within-participant contrast versus an active control condition was reported; (I7) that group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps were produced/reported (coordinates/voxelwise results not verifiable from abstract alone); and (I10) participant age and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

Excluded because the study does not address executive function task activations as defined by the review. It is a PET study using an aggression-provocation task and pharmacological (nicotine vs placebo) contrasts rather than a within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with SPM and coordinate reporting), I8 (coordinates/whole-brain results described), I10 (imaging modality, healthy sample confirmation, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is an aggression-provocation task, not an established executive function/cognitive-control domain), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition — main contrasts are nicotine vs placebo), I9 (task does not fall within specified executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E8) were explicitly triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). While this is a PET task-based study in healthy volunteers that contrasts calculation with number repetition, allowing I5 (PET task-based), I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control), and I9 (task involves working-memory/executive components) to be considered met, I cannot verify key required details: (a) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate reporting (I7/I8) are not confirmable from the abstract; (b) participant age information is not reported in the provided text so I10 is not satisfied. Because full text is incomplete, critical inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, so the study must be excluded pending provision of the complete article. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met based on available information.

The study is excluded because it includes clinical (MDD) participants and is not restricted to healthy individuals (Exclusion criterion E8). It does, however, meet multiple inclusion criteria relevant to the review: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing inhibition, an executive function), I6 (within-participant NP vs CTL contrasts), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported—whole-brain post-hoc analysis yielding putamen activation), I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (task assesses inhibition, an established executive function domain), and I10 (reports participant age range, healthy control group status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the sample is not restricted to healthy adults, the study does not satisfy the meta-analysis requirement focusing on healthy-only samples and must be excluded under E8.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy young adults (mean age 21). It reports within-participant contrasts (negative vs positive trial types) and an event-related, group-level random-effects voxelwise analysis producing whole-brain statistical maps and peak coordinates. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, empirical with healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study using an N-Back working memory task (an executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (1-Back and 2-Back > 0-Back) for healthy controls and performs group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses in SPM99 with thresholding and reported activation maxima/coordinates. Participant ages and healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The 0-Back serves as an active control. Although the paper also includes patients with schizophrenia, healthy participant within-group activation maps are provided, so it meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy contrasts, uses an active control, empirical human neuroimaging data, and participants are within adult age range). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

Exclusion: E6 (study used a passive rest baseline rather than an active control). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study assessing an executive function—working memory), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported using SPM), I8 (whole-brain results described and thresholded in text/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function domain—working memory), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition; the task was contrasted against rest/fixation only). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given E6 is met, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–33) using task-based paradigms probing an executive function (attention switching within/between working memory). It reports within-participant, parametric contrasts of switching demand (High>Medium>Low) and voxelwise group-level whole-brain analyses (ANOVAs, t-tests) with reported coordinates and cluster thresholds. Participant demographics, imaging modality, task details, and behavioral results are fully reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting baseline-only, non-empirical, or inappropriate-age/clinical sample issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract provided). Based on abstract: meets I5 (PET imaging), I6 (within-participant verbal working memory task with active visual/auditory search control), and I9 (working memory = executive function domain). However I7 (cannot verify presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map) and I10 (insufficient reporting in provided text of participant ages and explicit confirmation of healthy sample) cannot be confirmed from the supplied content. No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 are clearly met in the provided material, but because key inclusion criteria (I7, I10) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, study is excluded pending full-text availability.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract provided). Based on abstract the study meets: I5 (task-based PET study of working memory), I6 (reports task vs an active control task of attention), and I9 (working memory is an executive function domain). However, I cannot confirm I7 (presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map) because the abstract only reports regional increases without providing whole-brain maps or coordinate tables in the provided content. I10 is not met: participant ages and clear confirmation that analyses/reporting are restricted to healthy adults are not provided; moreover the study includes epilepsy patient groups (not restricted to healthy individuals), which violates exclusion criterion E8. Because the full text is not available to verify whole-brain results or participant details, and the study includes patient groups (E8), it must be excluded.

The study includes both schizophrenia patients and healthy control participants; the meta-analysis specifies healthy adult samples only. Therefore exclusion criterion E8 applies (study is not restricted to healthy individuals). The study does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I6 (within-participant 2-back vs 0-back contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain SPM analyses reported), I8 (coordinates/Talairach locations reported), I9 (working memory = executive function), and I10 (participant demographics, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm described). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete.

This paper is a methods/meta-analysis paper presenting a Bayesian network structure-learning approach applied to coordinate-based meta-analysis data (BrainMap). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports connectivity/meta-analytic network inference without presenting original whole-brain task activation maps or within-participant contrasts) and E7 (methods/meta-analysis/simulations paper rather than an original empirical fMRI/PET study reporting new within-subject task contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (uses and reports coordinate-based whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an original fMRI/PET study assessing executive function tasks in healthy adults — it is a general methodological/meta-analytic study), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive task vs active control reported), I7 (no original group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a study focused on executive function), I9 (tasks are not specifically and exclusively within established executive-function domains), I10 (does not report participant-level demographics/healthy sample info for an original dataset). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria E4 and E7.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 23.5) reporting task paradigms, behavioral results, and imaging methods. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects maps (task > fixation) and also direct within-participant contrasts between task conditions (object vs. spatial), satisfying an active within-subject comparison beyond fixation. Whole-brain results are described with maps and ROI tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, and not limited to passive baseline only). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adult participants (ages 32–56) that reports within-subject contrasts of simultaneous interpreting (translation) versus an active control (shadowing). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM and results (activations, cluster thresholds and loci) are reported. The task engages verbal working memory and cognitive control processes (lexical search, semantic processing, verbal working memory), which fall within established executive function domains.
