Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, baseline includes active control). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a task-switching paradigm (cognitive flexibility), reporting group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise decoding (searchlight + second-level statistics) of task-sets, stimuli and responses. Participants (final N=12, ages 24–30) are healthy. The paper provides full methods, results and discussion and reports whole-brain decoding accuracy maps tested against chance, satisfying requirements for task-evoked statistical maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults with within-subject condition contrasts (face vs scene distractors), and reports participant ages, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm. However, the report primarily uses subject-specific and ROI-based analyses and beta-series connectivity; the manuscript does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate table/figure of whole-brain group results that could be used for voxelwise meta-analysis. Although individual whole-brain maps were used to define ROIs, no whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation results are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I7 (group-level whole-brain map) and I8 (reporting of qualifying whole-brain results in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7, I8. Because lack of reported group-level whole-brain results prevents inclusion in the voxelwise meta-analysis, I exclude this study.

The study is an fMRI investigation using a working-memory (Sternberg) task in schizophrenia patients and matched healthy controls. It meets several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive domain — working memory), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures), I9 (task is within established executive function domains), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample description, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). However, the paper does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition (I6). The main reported contrasts are task vs rest and temporally segregated stages (encoding/maintenance/retrieval); although two task conditions (forward vs alphabetise) exist, the manuscript does not report a whole-brain, within-subject contrast of the executive manipulation (e.g., alphabetise > forward) as a group-level map suitable for inclusion. Therefore it fails to satisfy all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is an fMRI study of overt word-generation (verbal fluency) in healthy adults that reports within-subject contrasts and whole-brain, mixed-effects voxelwise analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive/ executive-related word-generation), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses / mixed-effects), I8 (results clearly described in text), I9 (task maps to an executive domain—initiation/verbal fluency). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (unclear whether contrasts are vs an active control condition; the paper describes ‘baseline’ but does not specify an active control, so it may be rest/fixation), I10 (participant ages are not reported—only that 10 healthy volunteers were examined). No explicit exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met. Because not all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I6 and I10), the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of a Continuous Performance Task (vigilance) with within-subject CPT vs active control contrast, healthy control group (age reported), and details of imaging and paradigm are provided. However, the paper focuses on ROI/masked frontal-cortex connectivity analyses: VOIs were defined within a frontal mask and the connectivity results are reported for these frontal ROIs/clusters. No group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map is reported or presented; the analyses and results are constrained to a frontal mask and VOIs. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I7) and falls under exclusion for ROI-only/connectivity-only reporting (E3, and E4). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. Exclusion criteria met: E3, E4.

This is a methods-focused fMRI study using visual checkerboard stimuli to evaluate modeling of time-varying BOLD signals. It does not investigate executive function or cognitive control tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an fMRI/PET study of executive function/cognitive control; it uses visual stimulation and methodological comparisons), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control), I9 (tasks are not within established executive function domains), I10 (the provided full text does not report participant ages — although healthy participants and imaging modality are described, age information is not present in the supplied content). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E8) are directly triggered by the available full text. Therefore the study is ineligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adults (n=14, ages 21–35) using a 2-back verbal working memory task (an executive function). It includes within-participant contrasts against an active control (0-back) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with coordinates and cluster statistics (BBR correlations, reported Talairach/MNI peaks). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigm are all reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E8 — the study includes participants outside the 18–60 year range (a child sample, ages 5–11), even though adult data are also reported. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — emotional go/no-go), I6 (within-participant contrasts across task blocks and face vs object probes), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures), I9 (task taps inhibition/executive control domain), I10 (participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: None — all inclusion criteria are satisfied. Final decision: EXCLUDED because E8 is violated (mixed-age sample includes children).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract, the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: working memory), I6 (within-subject contrasts comparing working memory and spatial-attention tasks), I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses implied by conjunction/double-subtraction and reported activation loci), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures), and I9 (task domain: working memory). However I10 cannot be confirmed from the provided content: participant ages and explicit statement of a healthy sample are not reported in the supplied text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met. Because I10 is not verifiable and the full text is incomplete, exclude pending retrieval of the complete article.

This study includes clinical (autism) participants and is not restricted to a healthy adult sample, which violates Exclusion Criterion E8. Although the paper meets multiple inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (see below) — it is an fMRI task-based study of cognitive control (I5), reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs. congruent and high- vs. low-arousal conditions) (I6), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholded maps/t-maps (I7,I8), uses an established executive function task (flanker/ANT; I9), and reports participant ages, healthy control sample details, imaging modality, and task paradigm (I10) — the presence of a clinical group means the study population is not restricted to healthy adults. Therefore it must be excluded per E8. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports ROI-based analyses without clear whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps) and E6 (uses a resting baseline as the primary control, with no active control task). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function—working memory for order), I9 (task falls within executive function domain—working memory), I10 (participant demographics, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast reported relative to an active control condition; primary contrasts use rest baseline and ROI-based comparisons), I7 (no clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported; analyses were performed within predefined ROIs). Full text appears complete for screening.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract provided). Based on the abstract: this is a PET study using a continuous performance test (CPT) of sustained attention (vigilance) and reports correlations of regional glucose metabolism with task performance. Inclusion met: I5 (PET task-based study) and I9 (task falls within executive domain: vigilance). Exclusion met: E8 — the study includes clinical groups (schizophrenia, autism) and is not restricted to healthy individuals, and no evidence that a separate, qualifying within-group whole-brain activation map for healthy adults is provided. Key inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable from available text: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast of task vs active control described), I7 (no evidence of group-level whole-brain/voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps), I10 (full participant age details and confirmation of healthy-only sample not reported). Because full text is incomplete and multiple required inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed while E8 applies, the study is excluded.

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adults investigating vigilance/selective attention (executive-domain: vigilance/target detection). It uses within-subject contrasts (selective S vs non-selective NS) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with thresholded maps and peak coordinates. Participant ages (range 24–48 across samples), healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and baseline is an active control (NS) rather than rest. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met based on abstract: I5 (fMRI task switching, an executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (within-participant contrasts reported: task switching vs performing tasks separately and vs a control condition), I9 (task switching = cognitive flexibility). Inclusion criteria not verifiable from provided content: I7 (cannot confirm a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map from the truncated abstract alone), I10 (participant age range and explicit confirmation of healthy sample not reported in the provided abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria are met (E3–E8 not evidenced). Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an event-related fMRI study of healthy adults that explicitly probes working memory and decision processes by having participants hold a first auditory word in memory and judge conceptual similarity to a second word. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function/working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts between task conditions such as Identity vs Close vs Far and S2 vs S1 that manipulate processing demands), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts reported, e.g., S2>S1 thresholded at FDR across the whole brain; whole-brain MVPA/spotlight maps), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures), I9 (task falls within working memory/executive function domain), and I10 (participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, baseline/task contrasts appropriate, empirical healthy-sample fMRI within 18–60 yrs). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The provided full text is limited to title/abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract the study is an fMRI study that includes a working memory (two-back) task (I5, I9 satisfied). However, there is no evidence in the available text of any within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control (I6 not met), nor clear reporting of a group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map (I7 not met). Relevant participant details (ages, explicit confirmation of a healthy sample) are not reported in the provided content (I10 not met). The analysis described focuses on correlation of fMRI time series with skin conductance responses (psychophysiological correlation), and the paper appears to report correlation/connectivity-type results rather than standard task activation contrasts; thus exclusion criterion E4 applies (only connectivity/physiological correlations without a reported whole-brain task activation map). Given the incomplete full text and unmet inclusion criteria, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function). The full text reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., correct vs incorrect trials, encoding vs distracter phases, and load comparisons), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with multiple-comparison correction, seed-based whole-brain maps, and ROI and voxelwise results. Participant demographics (healthy adults, mean age reported), imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain results are reported; not solely ROI/connectivity; not between-group only; healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study is an fMRI working memory task in healthy adults, so I5 and I9 are satisfied. However, I cannot verify critical criteria: I6 (explicit within-participant contrast against an active control condition is not clearly described), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are not explicitly reported in the provided text), and I10 (participant ages and explicit confirmation of healthy sample are not reported in the abstract). Because these inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the available content, the study is excluded pending full-text review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are explicitly met based on the provided information.

Although this study meets all inclusion criteria for task, imaging, contrasts, whole-brain reporting, and participant/task details (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10), it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (it includes schizophrenia patients) and participant eligibility allowed ages up to 65 years (outside the review age range 18–60). Therefore it must be excluded.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study is an event-related fMRI working-memory task (meets I5) within executive function domain (meets I9). However, I cannot verify key required items: I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control condition) is not clearly reported in the provided text; I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) is not confirmed—results focus on PFC but whole-brain analyses are not described; I10 (detailed participant ages and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample) is not fully reported (participants described only as “younger and older adults”). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm compliance with all inclusion criteria or rule out exclusions (e.g., E3 ROI-only reporting, E8 inclusion of participants outside 18–60). Therefore I exclude the study pending full-text availability for verification.

This study is excluded. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (uses fixation as the only baseline/contrast rather than an active control) and E8 (sample not restricted to healthy individuals; includes remitted schizophrenic patients). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (PET task-based study) and I9 (task is a working-memory/supraspan memory task, an executive function domain). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I6 (no within-participant contrast vs an active control condition—contrast is task vs fixation), I7 (cannot confirm a group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map from the provided abstract/full text), and I10 (insufficient reporting to confirm participant ages and restriction to a healthy sample). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=true — only title/abstract/metadata provided, core methods/results not available to verify whole-brain analyses or ages. Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied and exclusion criteria E6 and E8 apply, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

Full text provided appears incomplete (only title and abstract). The study used whole-brain fMRI and reports parametric, voxelwise activations (I7 met). However, the task probes perceptual prediction of target motion rather than a clearly defined executive function domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning), so I5 and I9 are not satisfied based on available information. There is no clear evidence of a within-participant contrast against an active control condition (I6 not confirmed). Participant demographics and health-status details are not present in the provided content (I10 not confirmed). Reporting of whole-brain results in coordinate tables/figures is not verifiable from the abstract alone (I8 not confirmed). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met. Because key inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I9, I10) cannot be confirmed and full text is incomplete, study is excluded from the executive-function meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: the study used fMRI and a Stroop task (meets I5) and the Stroop task falls within inhibition/executive function (meets I9). However, the abstract does not report a within-participant contrast versus an active control (I6 not confirmed), does not specify that group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps were reported (I7 not confirmed), and does not provide participant age/explicit healthy sample confirmation or full task/method details (I10 not confirmed). Because key inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I10) cannot be verified from the provided content and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text availability. No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met based on the abstract alone.

This PET study directly assesses working memory, a core executive function, using task-based within-subject contrasts (WM vs BL, WM vs SC) with an active baseline (repeat-last-item). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM99) and coordinates/clusters are reported. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 33), imaging modality (PET) and task paradigms are fully described. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (Incentive Change Signal Task) in healthy adults (N=24, ages 19–36). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., high vs low error likelihood; high vs low reward magnitude) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected clusters; MNI coordinates reported). Task falls within inhibition/cognitive control domain. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), reports within-group task contrasts (not only connectivity or between-group), and uses active task conditions rather than rest-only baseline. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This PET study meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults. I5: It uses PET imaging. I6: It reports a within-participant contrast (active Iowa Gambling Task minus an active sensorimotor control task) to isolate decision-making-related activation. I7/I8: Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM (random-effects two-sample t test) and results are reported with peak coordinates. I9: The task assesses decision-making/planning within executive function domains (Iowa Gambling Task). I10: Participant demographics, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-only, or non-empirical restrictions), and a within-group healthy participant activation map is available. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study) and I9 (working memory task falls within executive function domain). Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be verified from provided text: I6 (no clear report of a within-participant contrast versus an active control), I7 (no confirmation of group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps), I8 (unable to verify that whole-brain results are reported in coordinates/figures/text), I10 (participant age and healthy sample status not reported in the provided content). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met given the abstract alone (exclusion criteria applied: []). Therefore I exclude the study pending access to the complete full text to verify the remaining criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (verbal and spatial 2-back), an established executive function paradigm. It includes within-subject contrasts (2-back > 0-back) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with coordinates and cluster statistics. Healthy control participants are described (matched for sex, age, education), imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly reported, and an active control condition (0-back) was used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only without within-group maps, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or inappropriate age/healthy-sample issues) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive-function activations in healthy adults.

This study is an fMRI, task-based, whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults and reports coordinates (meets I7, I8, I10). However, the task is a face–name recognition paradigm investigating memory (episodic vs semantic retrieval) rather than an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (fMRI/PET study assessing executive function or cognitive control) or I9 (task within established executive function domains). The within-subject contrasts (1× vs 6×) are memory strength contrasts and do not constitute an executive-function vs active-control contrast required by I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of spatial working memory in healthy adults (six right-handed males, mean age 28) using a one-back spatial discrimination task (working memory = executive function). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (maintenance vs. encoding/recognition and task components), including comparisons of tactile vs. visual maintenance (active task contrasts rather than only rest). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise Z-maps were computed and thresholded with cluster criteria, and results are described in the text and figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not rest-only baseline, empirical human neuroimaging, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion met: E8 (study includes participants outside the 18–60 range — elderly group aged 60–84; sample not restricted to 18–60). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control/executive function: NO vs NN contrast targets conflict monitoring/cognitive control), I6 (within-participant contrast NO vs NN isolating control demand), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported using SPM2), I8 (whole-brain results reported and described with coordinates/tables), I9 (task involves cognitive control/inhibition domain relevant to executive functions), I10 (participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 are met). Because the study includes older adults beyond the meta-analysis age range (E8), it must be excluded despite meeting all other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adults (ages 22–29) that examines cognitive control/attentional processes during a task requiring internally-driven retrieval, strategy use, initiation, monitoring, and response selection. It includes within-subject contrasts of task versus an active control (NR-RS, TR-RS, NR-TR) and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical mapping (SPM) with reported peak coordinates and corrected statistics. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (PET), and the task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, participants healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions).

This study examines working memory (2-back) with fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps in healthy controls and patients, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/visualized), and I9 (working memory falls within executive function). However, the within-subject contrast reported is 2-back versus baseline/fixation (no active control condition such as 0-back or another active control), so it does not satisfy I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control). Because the study uses fixation/baseline as the (only) control, exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control task) applies. Additionally, participant ages are not explicitly reported in the provided text (demographics referenced elsewhere), so I10 (reporting of participant age) is not clearly met based on the supplied full text. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, this is an event-related fMRI study of working memory/executive control comparing elaborative vs rote rehearsal (meets I5, I6, I9). However, the provided content does not allow verification of group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps required by I7, nor does it report participant ages and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample and full imaging/task details required by I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are explicitly met based on the available information. Because I7 and I10 cannot be confirmed from the supplied text, the study is excluded pending access to the complete full text.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (3 participants, ages 30–32). It reports within-participant contrasts (delay-phase WM vs control task) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM2 analyses; significant clusters reported with stereotaxic coordinates, P<0.05 corrected). Imaging modality and task paradigm are described (1.5T T2*-weighted EPI, vsWM delay-response task), and participant health/ages are provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, not non-empirical, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This fMRI study investigates working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults and reports within-participant contrasts (instruction type, memory load). It reports participant ages, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm. However, the paper reports results primarily as ROI analyses (FFA, PPA, dorsolateral PFC) with no clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps presented; therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts between task conditions), I9 (working memory task), I10 (participant age/health/modality/task reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map). Full text appears complete.

This is a PET task-based neuroimaging study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. It includes a within-subject contrast of the self-ordered working memory task versus an active control task, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical thresholds, and provides participant age, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study of healthy adults (ages 21–35) examines spatial working memory (an executive function domain) using a task-based within-subject contrast (memory-guided saccades vs visually guided saccades), i.e., an active control comparison. The paper reports group-averaged, whole-brain results and Talairach coordinates (voxelwise activation maps summarized in group data/tables), describes imaging modality (3T fMRI), participant health/ages, and task paradigms in sufficient detail. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. The provided full text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete (only title and abstract provided). Based on available information: imaging modality is PET and task is verbal fluency (an executive initiation task), so I5 and I9 are satisfied. However, key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed: I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control) is unclear—while multiple tasks are reported, it is not explicit that an active control contrast was used; I7 (group-level whole-brain/voxelwise results) is not verifiable from the abstract; I10 (reporting of participant ages and full participant details) is incomplete—the abstract only states “four normal subjects” with no ages. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from available text, but because the full text is incomplete, we cannot determine eligibility. Exclude for now due to incomplete/full-text unavailability and unmet/uncertain inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I10.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control using a spatial Stroop conflict paradigm (executive function: inhibition/conflict resolution). It reports within-subject contrasts (informative cue vs neutral cue; P–N, W–N, P–W) and group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and thresholding. Participants are healthy adults (n=14 after exclusions), ages 18–32. Imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Excluding because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the available content. Inclusion criteria met based on provided information: I5 (fMRI study; authors state they used functional magnetic resonance imaging and keywords include working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast: bilateral vs unilateral conditions reported), I9 (task relates to working memory/executive domain as indicated in keywords and interpretation). Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed: I7 (no explicit confirmation in the provided content that a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map was produced or reported), I10 (participant age information not reported—only “seven normal volunteers”—so cannot confirm ages within 18–60 and other participant details). No exclusion criteria from the specified list are explicitly met. Because the full text is incomplete and essential methodological details cannot be verified, the study is excluded pending full-text availability.

Exclusion E8 applies: the study includes participants with fragile X syndrome (a clinical/non-healthy group) and is not restricted to healthy individuals, so it does not meet the review’s requirement for studies of healthy adults only. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function: switching/inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrasts for control participants using task event types), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported using SPM99), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (task falls within executive function domains), I10 (participant ages, healthy-control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract: the paper is an fMRI methods paper that used an oddball paradigm and a block working memory task to illustrate a model for removing global signal confounds. Inclusion criteria met/verified: I5 (fMRI task-based study using working memory) and I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory). Inclusion criteria not met or not verifiable from available text: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast vs an active control is reported), I7 (no evidence of group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps), I8 (no whole-brain results/coordinates reported in abstract), I10 (no participant age/healthy-sample confirmation or detailed imaging/task reporting). Exclusion criteria met: none confirmed (E7 methods-only cannot be established from abstract alone). Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E6: the working memory (executive function) task appears to use rest/fixation (long ISIs) as the baseline rather than an active control condition, and no within-participant contrast against an active control condition is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI including a working memory executive task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no evidence of a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion. Consequently the study is excluded.

Exclusion: E8 applies — sample age range is 17–25 (includes 17-year-olds), i.e., participants outside the eligible 18–60 range. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study with an executive function task: visuospatial working memory), I6 (within-subject experimental vs active control contrast for the working memory task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (working memory is an established executive function), I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore, exclude due to E8 (age inclusion violation).

Excluded because the study does not provide a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (I6 not met). The paper reports target vs. baseline contrasts (used as input to para-ICA) which appears to use an implicit/rest baseline rather than an active control (violating E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an attention/executive task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps/components used), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (task falls within executive domains—vigilance/attention/working memory), I10 (reports participant group status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-subject contrast vs an active control). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (rest/fixation or implicit baseline used without an active control contrast). Therefore exclude.

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of verbal working memory retrieval in healthy adults (mean age ~28) using a task within the executive function domain (working memory). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., Load1 > Control; L2 > L1; L3 > L2; target vs non-target paired t-tests) against an active control condition (motor control trials), and presents group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses with reported coordinate peaks and statistical thresholds (unthresholded and small-volume-corrected results), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant demographics, healthy status screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI analyses, connectivity/resting-state-only analyses, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical work, nor does it include participants outside 18–60 or non-healthy samples. Full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; thus fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–36) that uses task-based paradigms targeting working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., MGS vs SIR; cue, delay, and response epoch contrasts) and group-level surface/voxelwise statistical maps (permutation-based surface maps, with contrasts reported in text and figures). Participant demographics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-only baseline, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and can be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (an executive function) in healthy adults (five right-handed males, ages 31.6–37.2). The design includes a within-participant contrast (Incorrect Matching minus Correct Matching) comparing an inhibition condition to an active control, and group-level whole-brain activation maps were computed and reported (thresholded t-maps with Talairach coordinates). The paper reports participant ages, health/selection criteria, imaging modality (fMRI) and task details. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, coordinates) is present. Although sample size is very small (n=5), this does not conflict with the review inclusion/exclusion rules. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study is a resting-state functional connectivity (fcMRI) investigation in individuals with schizophrenia, their siblings, and control subjects. It does not involve any task-based executive function or cognitive control paradigms, contains no within-participant task-versus-active-control contrasts, and does not report task-evoked whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps. Participants include patients with schizophrenia (i.e., not restricted to healthy adults). Therefore it does not meet the inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (connectivity/resting-state analyses only, no task activation maps), E6 (resting state/eyes-closed with no active control task), E8 (study not restricted to healthy participants). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7, I9, I10.

This article reports task-based fMRI (concurrent ERPs/fMRI) of an executive function (response inhibition) using an auditory cued go/nogo paradigm (I5, I9). Within-participant contrasts (nogo minus control) are reported (I6). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps and voxelwise t-tests were conducted and reported for the healthy control group (nogo vs control), with thresholding and cluster reporting (I7; descriptions/coordinates/regions provided consistent with acceptable reporting per I8). Relevant participant information (healthy control group presence, matching to patients, age matching described, imaging modality and task paradigm) is provided (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-group healthy participant activation maps, use an active control condition (not rest-only), and are empirical human neuroimaging data. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Hence study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This empirical fMRI study reports task-evoked, group-level, voxelwise (random-effects) maps for healthy control participants performing a selective attention task. The task is a mixed block/event-related selective attention paradigm (vigilance/attention — a recognized executive domain), includes an active non-task control block (red blocks) and task-relevant blocks with event-related target onsets, and provides within-subject condition-specific activation maps (onset of task blocks and targets). Whole-brain voxelwise results are described and displayed, and participant/sample, imaging modality, and task details are reported. Therefore the study meets criteria for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This study uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (spatial working memory) with within-subject WM vs active control contrasts and reports whole-brain voxelwise results in healthy volunteers. However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the healthy sample is outside the target age range (mean age 63.8, >60) and the study includes clinical (schizophrenia) participants rather than being restricted to healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Therefore excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This is an fMRI study that includes a working memory (2-back/3-back) task, which falls within executive function. The study reports within-participant contrasts of retrieval (2-/3-back) versus an active control (1-back) and also compares retrieval versus baseline; analyses include group-level, whole-brain random-effects maps (voxelwise) reported in the text/figures. Participant demographics (14 healthy adults, age 18–31), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes active control, empirical data, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Cannot verify key inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (no sufficient evidence). Inclusion IDs not met / not verifiable: I5 (uncertain whether task is classified as an executive function task — movement preparation may reflect motor intention/planning but this is not clearly framed within established executive domains), I6 (no clear report of a within-participant contrast versus an active control condition in the provided text), I7 (no confirmation of group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps in the provided content), I8 (while results are summarized, qualifying whole-brain results or coordinate tables are not present in the excerpt), I9 (task domain mapping to established executive domains is not clearly demonstrated), I10 (participant age/health status and full task/imaging details are not reported). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm all required criteria; therefore the study is excluded pending full-text review.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study reports BOLD fMRI in healthy controls on a working-memory task (so I5 and I9 are satisfied). However, the available content does not allow verification of: a within-participant contrast vs an active control (I6), a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (I7), or reporting of participant ages and full sample details required (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) can be confirmed from the available information. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the truncated/full-text information, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory and selective attention (executive function domain). It reports within-subject contrasts (invalid vs neutral trials) assessing interactions of WM and visual selection, uses group-level whole-brain GLM and connectivity analyses (voxelwise maps with FWE correction and reported foci), and provides participant age ranges and healthy-sample status and full task details and imaging parameters. The neutral condition is an active task control. All required meta-analysis inclusion criteria are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (core content present).

Although this is an event-related fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (I7) and reports results and coordinates clearly (I8), and provides participant/sample/imaging/task information (I10), the experimental paradigm is a sentence-reading/lexical ambiguity language comprehension task rather than an established executive-function or cognitive-control task. The study does not implement or contrast a canonical executive function task (e.g., working memory manipulation, inhibition task, cognitive flexibility) within participants; reading-span is measured as an individual-difference covariate rather than an executed working-memory task. Therefore it fails to meet I5, I6, and I9. No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 directly apply.

This fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (DMTS) in healthy premenopausal women provides whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses and reports coordinates and participant details, satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, the reported neuroimaging analyses focus on encoding-related betas and contrasts of placebo vs scopolamine (a pharmacological manipulation). The paper does not present a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control task condition; encoding effects appear modeled against an implicit/rest/fixation baseline and the authors did not report an active control contrast. Therefore criterion I6 is not met and the study violates exclusion E6 (uses rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates a PET study using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task and voxelwise SPM95 analyses, so I5 (PET executive task), I7 (group-level voxelwise maps), I8 (maps/figures acceptable), and I9 (WCST = cognitive flexibility) are met. However, the abstract does not explicitly report a within-participant contrast versus an active control condition (I6 not confirmed) and does not report participant ages or explicit confirmation of a healthy sample (I10 not confirmed). Because not all inclusion criteria can be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending full-text inspection. Exclusion criteria met: none (none clearly violated based on abstract).

The study is an fMRI working-memory task with an active control and within-subject contrast, but the reported analyses are ROI-based rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps. Exclusion E3 applies (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive-function working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I9 (task is working memory). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no evidence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map reported), I10 (participant age not reported in the provided text; only ‘normal subjects’ is stated). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract provided). Based on available abstract, this is a PET study of self-face recognition (passive and active recognition) in healthy volunteers. It does not target established executive-function domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility) and thus does not meet the review’s executive-function requirement. Inclusion/exclusion summary: Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (cannot confirm from abstract). Inclusion IDs not met or not confirmed: I5 (not an executive-function task), I6 (within-participant contrast exists but not for an executive task vs active control), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise map cannot be confirmed from abstract), I9 (task not within established executive domains), I10 (participant age not reported in abstract). Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I5 and I9) is not met and the full text is incomplete, I exclude this study. If full text is provided showing the task actually probes an executive domain and reporting whole-brain group analyses and ages, inclusion could be reconsidered.

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy middle-aged adults with a within-subject 2-Back vs 0-Back contrast and full reporting of participants, imaging modality, and task. However, the reported analyses are ROI-based: a priori ROIs were applied and mean activation intensities in those ROIs were used in regression models. The paper does not present a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map or coordinates/figures of whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I7/I8) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7, I8. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Excluded for E3.

This is an fMRI study using a verbal n-back working memory task in adult cannabis users. It meets multiple methodological inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI, within-participant active-control contrasts, whole-brain group-level task maps, working memory domain, and reporting of task/paradigm and imaging modality). However, the sample consists of cannabis users (cannabis abuse allowed) rather than a healthy, non-substance-using adult sample. The meta-analysis target is executive function activations in healthy adults; inclusion of participants with substance use violates exclusion criterion E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting other imaging/task criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a verbal working memory task (an executive function domain) with healthy adult control participants. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (load levels > active control condition) and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported activation foci/coordinates and descriptions of results. Imaging modality, task paradigm, and healthy control status are described. Although some detailed coordinate tables are noted as “available on request,” sufficient whole-brain results and within-group healthy-control contrasts are described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy activation maps, uses an active control, empirical human fMRI data, and participants are adults). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This fMRI study examined working memory (2-back) and recognition tasks in healthy adults, reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps, and provided participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task details (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, all primary activation contrasts reported are task versus fixation (rest) or task-related activation relative to fixation; no within-participant contrast against an active control condition is presented. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation used as the only baseline without an active control task). Full text is complete and reviewed in detail.

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract (fulltext_incomplete=true). Based on the abstract, the study meets I5 (PET task-based study of visuospatial working memory/executive control), I6 (within-participant contrasts between motor tasks and an active visual-detection control), I7 (group-level whole-brain PET analyses reported as task-evoked rCBF increases), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/regions), and I9 (task maps onto working memory/executive function). However I10 is not met from the provided content because participant age details are not reported in the supplied text (only “eight healthy subjects” is given). Because the supplied full text is incomplete, I cannot verify all required methodological details and participant information; per screening rules the incomplete full text prevents confirming all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 are clearly met based on the available information.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of executive control (Stroop) with within-subject contrasts (incongruent > neutral) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses; however it includes participants older than the allowed age range for this review (older group aged 58–75 includes participants >60). Per exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside age range 18–60), the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast of task vs control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures), I9 (task falls within inhibition/executive domain), I10 (participant age, healthy sample confirmation, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (all applicable inclusion criteria were satisfied). Exclusion criteria applied: E8 (participants outside 18–60). Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met. Inclusion criteria met based on the abstract: I5 (PET task-based study assessing cognitive performance), I6 (within-participant contrasts including PMT vs an active motor control SHAM), I9 (task involves planning/visuospatial and rule-following processes consistent with executive domain). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable from the provided content: I7 (cannot verify presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map from the abstract alone), I10 (participant ages not reported in the provided content; only ‘eight right-handed volunteers’ stated). Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a minimal executive process ('refreshing') in healthy young adults (mean age 21.3), with clear task-based contrasts (Refresh vs Repeat) analyzed within-participants. Group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (Refresh > Repeat and Localizer contrasts), and coordinates/ROIs are provided. The task is explicitly framed as an executive/working-memory-related process (refreshing as a minimal executive function). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper is an fMRI study of working memory (executive function) including healthy controls, but its primary reported analyses are ICA-derived functional connectivity/component maps and between-group connectivity comparisons rather than standard within-subject GLM task>control activation contrasts for healthy adults. The paper does not provide a conventional group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (healthy participants) derived from a within-participant task vs active-control contrast that could be entered into an activation meta-analysis. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task of working memory), I9 (task within executive function domain), and I10 (reports imaging modality, task paradigm, and healthy control sample information). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast of task vs active control reported as a standard activation contrast for healthy group) and I7 (no conventional group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical activation map for healthy adults). Full text appears complete for assessment.

The study is a PET task-based study of random number generation vs an active counting control in volunteers, so it meets I5 (PET executive-function task), I6 (within-participant contrast RNG vs COUNT), and I9 (task falls within executive domains). However, only the abstract/metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true), so I cannot verify whether a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map was reported (I7) nor find details on participant ages and explicit confirmation that the sample were healthy adults (I10). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending full-text availability. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met from the abstract.

This is an fMRI study with healthy adult participants, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, within-participant contrasts against an active control, and reports coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I10). However, the task is an auditory temporal-order judgment (millisecond timing/perception), not an established executive function or cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The primary study aim and paradigm assess temporal perception/timing rather than executive function per se, so it does not meet I5 and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered and the full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adult participants (n=12, ages 18–34). The study reports within-participant contrasts (Item-order vs Reordering conditions and parametric load effects) and group-level random-effects ‘map-wise’ analyses with contrasts yielding t-statistics (indicating voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), participant health/age, and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within the 18–60 healthy range). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–34) that investigates cognitive control/executive processes (response inhibition, exploration/switching) using within-subject contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise group analyses. The paper reports SPM random-effects, whole-brain results (with coordinates and cluster thresholds) and also provides participant demographics, imaging modality, and full task details. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-state baseline only, not non-empirical, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study of working memory (digits forward/backward), an executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts of digit-span tasks versus an active sensorimotor control, uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with voxel-level thresholds and spatial extent correction, and describes anatomical/BA results (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). Participant information (healthy adults, ages, N, right-handed, medication-free) and imaging modality and paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, active control used, healthy adult sample in 18–60). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because participants are outside the eligible age range for the meta-analysis (E8). Although the study includes a within-participant contrast of an executive task vs an active control (I6), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with coordinates (I7,I8), and uses an executive domain task (verbal fluency; I9), it does not meet the required imaging modality criterion (I5) because the activation data are from 99mTc-HMPAO SPECT rather than fMRI or PET, and thus I5 is not met. Additionally, I10 (reporting of imaging modality as fMRI or PET) is not satisfied for the activation contrast. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Summary of criteria: Inclusion met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion not met: I5, I10. Exclusion applied: E8 (participants >60 years).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines verbal working memory and syntactic re-analysis (garden-path) using within-subject contrasts (e.g., GP–NGP, SEN–MEM, and contrasts masked with CTRL). Analyses were performed at the group level using whole-brain, random-effects SPM with cluster-level correction (p<0.05), and activations are reported across the brain (including use of the SPM Anatomy Toolbox). Participants’ ages, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly reported. The tasks probe the working memory executive domain (verbal working memory/maintenance and manipulation). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active control conditions, empirical human neuroimaging data, healthy adults within 18–60). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,and I10 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This study used event-related fMRI in 14 healthy adult participants (mean age 30.8) to examine belief-bias in deductive reasoning, specifically including inhibitory trials that require suppression of a prepotent, belief-based response (an inhibition/cognitive control process). The design includes within-participant contrasts (reasoning vs. an active baseline with a non-argument third sentence; correct vs. incorrect inhibitory trials). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects) are reported with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates. Participant health status, age, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. These features satisfy inclusion criteria I5–I10 and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used resting-state fMRI and DTI to examine structural-functional connectivity and correlated FA with neuropsychological composite scores of executive function and processing speed. It did not perform any task-based fMRI or PET executive-function activation paradigms or report within-participant task vs control contrasts or task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Additionally, the participant age range (49–80, mean 64) includes individuals older than 60, violating the review’s age restriction. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5–I9 and I10, and meets exclusion criteria E4 (resting-state/connectivity analyses only, no task activation map) and E8 (participants outside 18–60 age range). No inclusion criteria are satisfied for this meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is incomplete (only title and abstract provided), so key eligibility items cannot be verified. Inclusion criteria met from abstract: I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control/conflict), I6 (within-participant contrasts between congruent/conflict conditions), I9 (task falls within executive function domain). Inclusion criteria not verifiable / not met based on available content: I7 (cannot confirm presence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map or coordinates/figures because full methods/results are missing), I10 (participant age range and explicit confirmation of healthy sample not reported in provided text). No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the abstract alone (exclusion IDs met: none). Because required inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I exclude the study pending full-text availability.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Exclusion: E8 applies — study includes participants outside 18–60 years (mean age ~68) and includes Alzheimer patients (sample not restricted to healthy adults). Inclusion criteria met based on abstract: I5 (PET study of attention/executive function), I7 (group-level voxelwise/whole-brain analyses described: voxel-by-voxel t statistics), I9 (task falls within executive domains — sustained/divided attention/vigilance), I10 (reports participant ages, control sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not verifiably met: I6 (unclear whether within-participant contrasts use an active control condition vs. only rest/baseline). Because E8 is met, exclude.

Excluded because the study includes participants outside the allowed age range (older group mean 65.8 years), violating exclusion criterion E8. The study otherwise meets the inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control/attentional interference), I6 (within-participant contrasts: emotional vs neutral and high vs low attention cue conditions), I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses reported with peak coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and described in text), I9 (task targets attention/inhibition, an executive function domain), and I10 (participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive inhibition (executive function) in healthy adults (ages 20–30). It includes within-subject contrasts (backward/inhibition vs motor control and vs forward/automatization), uses group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise/statistical thresholds and cluster correction, and reports activation results in the text (BA labels) consistent with whole-brain SPM99 analyses. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses an active motor control baseline, empirical human neuroimaging data, and participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This article reports an event-related fMRI Go/Nogo inhibition task in a screened healthy adult sample (n=21, mean age 27.4). It includes a within-subject contrast (rare-Nogo vs rare-Go) comparing inhibition to an active control, and a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis (SPM2) with reported cluster coordinates and statistics. The task falls within the executive function domain (response inhibition). Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task details are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, empirical human neuroimaging data, age within 18–60 and healthy sample). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy young adults, using within-subject task contrasts and well-reported participant/sample details; therefore it meets I5 (fMRI task-based study), I6 (within-participant contrasts of executive task vs control), I9 (working memory is an executive function), and I10 (age, health status, modality, and paradigm reported). However, the paper’s primary neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based timecourse analyses in individually defined scene-selective ROIs. The manuscript does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the executive-function task contrasts (only a group-level localizer map for Scene>Face is reported, which is not an executive-function contrast). Thus it fails I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain task activation results). Accordingly, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adults that includes working-memory tasks (1-back, 2-back, random-number generation) — established executive function paradigms. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (task vs reading/semantic baselines) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with corrected p-values and reported coordinates. Participant age, healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigms are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants in 18–60 range and healthy). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10.

This fMRI study of an n-back working memory task in healthy adults meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: uses within-participant working-memory contrasts implicit in n-back; I9: working memory is an executive function; I10: reports healthy adult sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm). However, the paper’s neuroimaging analyses used a hypothesis-driven region-of-interest approach with voxelwise inference restricted to ROIs (significance reported FDR-corrected within ROIs) and does not present or describe a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain voxelwise map). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not present a task-based fMRI/PET investigation of executive function in healthy adults. Inclusion met: I7 (group-level whole-brain fMRI analysis reported), I8 (whole-brain results described), and I10 (participant age/health status, imaging modality, and task details provided for the fMRI sample). Inclusion not met: I5 (the fMRI task assessed self-paced motor writing, not an executive-function paradigm), I6 (no within-participant fMRI contrast of an executive task vs an active control), I9 (fMRI task does not fall within established executive domains). Exclusion criteria met: E8 — the paper includes intracranial recordings from epilepsy patients (non-healthy participants), so the study is not restricted to healthy individuals. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=28, age 20–39) that examines working memory/paired-association learning (an executive function domain). The paper reports within-subject task analyses (sustained delay-period activity during the PAa task, with the DMSv task as an active control/interleaved condition) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM results (voxelwise maps with cluster correction). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are fully reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study used resting-state FDG-PET in OCD patients and matched controls and correlated resting metabolic rates with neuropsychological test scores. It does not include any task-based, within-participant contrasts of executive function versus an active control condition, nor does it provide task-evoked whole-brain activation maps in healthy participants. It also includes a clinical (OCD) sample rather than being restricted to healthy adults, and imaging was acquired at rest (resting baseline only). Therefore it fails to meet multiple core inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of task-evoked executive function activations. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET paradigm), I6 (no within-participant task vs control contrast), I7 (no task-evoked whole-brain group-level activation map), I9 (no task-based executive-function imaging), I10 (no task paradigm reported for imaging). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only between-group/resting contrasts without within-group task activation in healthy participants), E6 (rest as the only baseline without an active control task), E8 (includes clinical patients; not restricted to healthy adults). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–35) investigating motor intention/motor planning using a task that manipulates cue-driven preparation. The task taps an executive domain (planning/initiation) and includes within-subject contrasts (motor cue vs. neutral and motor vs. spatial cues). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with corrected cluster-level statistics and MNI coordinates. Participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, empirical human data, healthy adults). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of antisaccade (inhibition) and refixation saccades, directly assessing an executive function (inhibition). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (antisaccade vs refixation) and within-group t-tests for the healthy control group, and uses group-level, voxelwise random-effects t tests with reported Talairach coordinates and effect-size maps (whole-brain analyses). Participant ages and healthy control status are reported and within the 18–60 range. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a resting PET study correlating regional resting oxygen consumption with neuropsychological (memory) test scores; it does not report task-based PET/fMRI activations. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (resting-state/metabolic correlations without a whole-brain task activation map), E3 (study focused on a limited set of a priori regions rather than reporting whole-brain task-evoked results/appears ROI-focused), and E8 (sample includes participants aged up to 68, exceeding the 18–60 age range). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study of executive function/cognitive control), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrasts), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no whole-brain task results reported), I9 (no task-based executive function imaging despite behavioral working-memory tests), I10 (does not report a task paradigm alongside imaging). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract-level content provided).

This study is an fMRI investigation of antisaccade performance (inhibition/cognitive control), an established executive function domain. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing antisaccades with prosaccades (an active control), and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates and statistical maps described in the text. Participant age range (23–32), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are all reported. There is a clear whole-brain analysis (interaction effects reported at MNI coordinates) and not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided).
